Summary: Create the Medvya monorepo skeleton (Medvya.sln, web workspaces, packages)
Description:
Create the repository layout agreed in ADR-001: Medvya.sln with src/Host.Api, src/BuildingBlocks/*, src/Modules/<Module>/{Domain,Application,Infrastructure,Api} for the P0 modules (Identity, Tenancy, Audit), src/Workers/Worker.Jobs, web/clinic, web/portal (placeholder), packages/{ui,api-client,i18n,test-fixtures}, tests/*, infra/bicep, docs, tools.
Pin the .NET 10 SDK (global.json), central package management (Directory.Packages.props), nullable + warnings-as-errors + analyzers (Directory.Build.props), pnpm workspaces for web/* and packages/*.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a fresh clone, when I run `dotnet build` and `pnpm install && pnpm -r build`, then both succeed with zero warnings.
* The folder layout matches docs/03-architecture/repository-structure.md for every folder needed in P0; later modules are not created yet.
* global.json pins a .NET 10 SDK; Directory.Packages.props holds every NuGet version; no project file contains a version number.
* web/clinic starts with `pnpm --filter clinic dev` on React 19 + TypeScript + Vite and renders a placeholder page using packages/ui.
* README.md explains prerequisites, local start and links to docs/; AGENTS.md states the synthetic-data-only and no-PHI-in-logs rules.

Summary: Record and accept ADR-001 (stack) and supporting ADRs 003–006
Description: Review the drafted ADR-001 (stack), ADR-003 (country isolation), ADR-004 (BFF), ADR-005 (tenant isolation/RLS) and ADR-006 (immutable signed records) and move them to Accepted. Superseded stack statements in the Build Plan and Azure Architecture design pages are listed in docs/01-prd/source-conflicts.md and must not be implemented.
Acceptance Criteria:
* ADR-001, 003, 004, 005 and 006 have status Accepted with date and decider.
* Each ADR lists the alternatives rejected and why (NestJS, Next.js, PostgreSQL, Cosmos DB, AKS in P0–P6).
* docs/01-prd/source-conflicts.md rows C-01…C-07 reference the accepted ADRs.
* A short note is sent to the design project owner to update the Build Plan and Azure Architecture pages (PRD v2 finding "CHANGE").

Summary: Decide launch market (ADR-002) and confirm Azure subscription and region
Description: The founder decides the launch market (default: India first) and confirms the Azure subscription, billing owner and launch region (Central India or UAE North). Also confirm Azure OpenAI and AI Speech model availability in the chosen region (PRD risk "AI model not available in-region" says confirm in P0).
Acceptance Criteria:
* ADR-002 is Accepted with the chosen market and the reasoning.
* Azure subscription ID, tenant, billing owner and launch region are recorded in docs/03-architecture/azure-deployment.md (no secrets).
* Microsoft for Startups (Founders Hub) credit application is submitted or explicitly declined.
* Availability of Azure OpenAI (chat model) and AI Speech (batch transcription + diarisation, languages en-IN/hi-IN/ta-IN or ar-AE) in the launch region is confirmed with a dated note.
* If UAE is chosen, PRD sequencing impact (EID reader and exchange on the critical path to week 29) is acknowledged in the ADR.

Summary: GitHub repository protections and PR pipeline (build, analyzers, tests, CodeQL, dependency and secret scanning)
Description: Create .github/workflows/pr.yml running on every pull request: dotnet build with analyzers as errors, dotnet test (unit + Testcontainers integration), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit, vitest, CodeQL (C# + TypeScript), dependency review, secret scanning with push protection, Dependabot for NuGet/npm/GitHub Actions. Protect main: PR required, status checks required, linear history, no force push, signed tags for releases. Add CODEOWNERS and a PR template with the X1–X8 checklist.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A PR that fails build, tests, lint, type-check, CodeQL or secret scanning cannot be merged into main.
* Direct pushes and force pushes to main are rejected.
* Dependabot opens update PRs for NuGet, npm and Actions weekly.
* The PR template contains the X1–X8 Definition-of-Done checklist and a "synthetic data only" confirmation.
* Pipeline duration for the skeleton is under 10 minutes.

Summary: Local development environment with Docker Compose (PostgreSQL, Azurite, mail and SMS sinks)
Description: docker-compose.yml with PostgreSQL 17, Azurite (Blob), smtp4dev (email sink) and a fake SMS endpoint, plus a one-command start (`make dev` or `pnpm dev`) that applies EF Core migrations and seeds the synthetic tenant. Local identity uses a development Entra External ID tenant or a dev-only OIDC stub that is impossible to enable outside Development.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given Docker is running, when I run the documented start command, then API, web/clinic and all dependencies start and the seeded synthetic tenant can sign in within 5 minutes on a clean machine.
* The dev OIDC stub refuses to start unless ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development (verified by a test).
* No real secrets are needed locally; .env.example lists variable names only.
* Emails and SMS sent locally appear in the sinks and are never delivered externally.

Summary: Azure environments as code (Bicep): App Service, PostgreSQL private access, Blob, Key Vault, App Insights, Defender, budgets
Description: infra/bicep/main.bicep (+ postgres.bicep) for the India dev environment, which is the pilot target. Staging and production parameters, the staging slot, Defender plans and a Storage private endpoint move to MDV-P1-039 (decided 13 Nov 2026). App Service (Linux, .NET 10) with VNet integration; Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server with Entra-only auth, private access (VNet-integrated), public network access disabled; Storage with private endpoint and no public blob access; Key Vault with RBAC, soft delete and purge protection; Application Insights + Log Analytics; Defender for Cloud plans; budgets and cost alerts per environment; Azure Policy denying resources outside the allowed region(s).
Acceptance Criteria:
* `az deployment group what-if` and, after a reviewer approves, a real deployment of dev succeed from CI (`infra-dev` workflow) with no manual portal steps.
* The PostgreSQL server `publicNetworkAccess` is Disabled and only reachable from the VNet (verified by a connectivity test from outside the VNet failing).
* Key Vault has purge protection enabled; Storage has `allowBlobPublicAccess=false`.
* A budget with email alerts at 50/80/100 % exists for the dev environment.
* Azure Policy assignment denies creating resources in any region other than the configured country region(s).
* No secret value appears in any Bicep or parameter file.

Summary: GitHub OIDC federation to Azure and tagged deploy to dev
Description: Federated credentials (one app identity per environment) so GitHub Actions deploys without stored cloud secrets. deploy-dev.yml runs on a tag `v*` that points at a commit on main (main only takes GitHub-signed squash merges, so the main-only check is the control; tags themselves are not signed): build once, run migrations inside the VNet with the migration identity, deploy, smoke test. The staging slot with swap and the approved production workflow move to MDV-P1-039 (decided 13 Nov 2026).
Acceptance Criteria:
* No Azure client secret or publish profile exists in GitHub secrets (only federated credentials).
* Pushing a tag on main deploys to dev end-to-end and the health endpoint returns 200 with the tag version.
* A tag on a non-main commit is rejected by the workflow.
* Migrations run with the dedicated migration database user, not the app identity.
* Deploy is repeatable: re-running the same tag is idempotent.

Summary: Database security baseline part 1: Entra-only auth, managed identity, least-privilege users per module and for migrations
Description: Configure Microsoft Entra-only authentication on the logical server. The App Service managed identity is the only application principal. Create one database user/role per module schema (identity, tenancy, audit, … ) with GRANT only on its own schema, a separate migration principal with DDL rights, and a read-only reporting role. Connection strings use `Authentication=Active Directory Managed Identity; Encrypt=Strict`. No SQL logins with passwords exist.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Attempting SQL authentication with a username/password fails (Entra-only is on).
* The app identity cannot ALTER/CREATE objects; the migration identity can; verified by integration test against Testcontainers PostgreSQL using equivalent roles.
* A module's database role cannot SELECT from another module's schema (architecture/integration test).
* Connection strings in App Service settings contain no password; `Encrypt=Strict` is enforced.
* Human access to production data is only via just-in-time elevation (documented runbook, links MDV-P0-025).

Summary: Database security baseline part 2: national/insurance ID encryption, masked access, storage encryption with a customer-managed key
Description: Column master key in Key Vault usable only by the API identity; column encryption keys for: Aadhaar last-4, ABHA number/address, Emirates ID, passport, visa/residency number, insurance member number. Deterministic encryption for exact-match lookups (EID, ABHA), randomized + VBS enclave where range/LIKE is required. Dynamic data masking on phone, email and date of birth for support/reporting roles. TDE protector switched to a customer-managed key with automatic rotation.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A DBA/admin querying an encrypted column (SSMS without CMK access) sees ciphertext only.
* The API can insert and look up a patient by exact Emirates ID and by exact ABHA through EF Core (integration test with a test CMK).
* A login in the support role sees masked phone/email/DOB values.
* TDE protector is a Key Vault key with rotation policy; backups inherit it.
* The protected-column list is documented in the data classification register (MDV-P0-016) and kept deliberately small.

Summary: Tenancy model with EF Core global filters and PostgreSQL row-level security (cross-tenant test in CI)
Description: Organisation (tenant) → facility → membership model. `tenant_id` (PRD: clinic_id) on every clinic-owned table. A DbConnection interceptor sets SESSION_CONTEXT(N'tenant_id') read-only on every open from the authenticated membership; a SQL security policy applies FILTER and BLOCK predicates; EF Core global query filters mirror it. One user can hold memberships in several clinics; the active facility is chosen at sign-in.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given two tenants with data, when user A of tenant 1 queries any tenant-owned table, then no row of tenant 2 is returned, even when the EF query filter is disabled with IgnoreQueryFilters() (RLS still blocks).
* Inserting or updating a row with another tenant's tenant_id is blocked by the BLOCK predicate.
* A user with memberships in two clinics sees only the active facility's tenant data and can switch facility, which re-establishes session context.
* Session context is reset on every pooled connection open (test opens 100 pooled connections alternating tenants with zero leaks).
* The cross-tenant read/write test runs in CI on every PR and fails the build on any leak (P0 exit gate 3).

Summary: Staff sign-in through the BFF with Entra External ID: MFA (TOTP), passkeys and recovery
Description: Implement OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE against Microsoft Entra External ID inside Host.Api (BFF). Tokens stay server-side; the browser gets an HTTP-only, Secure, SameSite=Strict session cookie and an antiforgery token. MFA is mandatory for all staff (TOTP authenticator; passkeys preferred; SMS OTP only as fallback where allowed). Account recovery flow. Screen F-03: email or mobile → "Continue with passkey" / "Use a one-time code instead" → 6-digit code → facility picker.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A staff user cannot reach any authenticated page or API without completing MFA.
* After sign-in no access or refresh token is readable from JavaScript (document.cookie and storage contain none).
* Wrong codes are counted and the account is locked by the identity provider (Entra smart lockout: threshold and 15-minute duration set and recorded in the runbook), because codes are typed on the provider's pages and Medvya never sees them; Medvya rate-limits starting sign-in. The "2 attempts left" copy is the provider's, not ours.
* Passkeys and the one-time-code fallback run on the provider's pages; the F-03 page offers "Continue with passkey" and "Sign in with SSO" (built). The unsupported-browser message depends on the External ID tenant.
* SSO-enforced tenants moved to MDV-P7-004: hiding options before sign-in needs a verified-domain model, and a lookup would reveal which organisations exist.
* Recovery ("Can't sign in?") leads to the provider's self-service recovery, which re-verifies identity and re-enrols MFA; Medvya's own pages never reveal whether an account exists (sign-in start takes no email).
* Sign-in, refusals and sign-outs that Medvya sees are written to the audit log (MDV-P0-017); provider-side failures, lockouts and recovery are in the Entra sign-in log, and the runbook says how to read it.

Summary: Session control: facility picker, idle timeout on shared clinic PCs, device/session revocation
Description: After MFA the user picks a facility ("Choose where you are working today") listing each membership with role. `/v1/me/context` returns user, active membership, permissions and feature flags. Configurable idle timeout per tenant (default 15 min on shared-device mode, 8 h max session); unsaved drafts are kept locally (encrypted, no PHI in plain localStorage) and on re-auth the user must re-confirm the patient (F-05a). Users can see and revoke their sessions/devices; admins can revoke any staff session.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a user with two memberships, when they sign in, then they must choose a facility and the session is scoped to it; switching facility re-scopes without re-entering MFA.
* After the idle timeout the session ends and the "Session expired" screen (F-05a) appears; signing in again returns to the previous route and asks to confirm the patient before continuing.
* Revoking a session from "My devices" or by an admin ends it within 60 seconds on the next request.
* No patient data is stored in localStorage/sessionStorage in clear text (automated check in Playwright).
* `/v1/me/context` never returns permissions the role does not grant.

Summary: Invite a colleague and accept the invitation (membership invited → active)
Description: An admin invites a person by email or mobile with a role and facility scope. The invitee opens /invite/:token, sees "Join {clinic} … invited you as {Role}", the capability list (✓ allowed / ✕ not allowed, e.g. reception cannot see clinical notes), facility scope and hours, then creates a passkey (or MFA) and joins. Membership moves invited → active. Expired or reused tokens show "Ask your admin to resend".
Acceptance Criteria:
* Invitation tokens are single-use, random (≥128 bits), expire after the configured period (default 7 days) and are stored hashed.
* The acceptance screen shows role, facility scope and capability list exactly as derived from the role-permission matrix.
* After acceptance the membership is active and the user lands on the role's home route.
* An expired, revoked or already-used token shows the expired state and creates no membership.
* Invites and acceptances are audited; the invite email/SMS contains no patient data.
* Clinician invites are flagged "licence verification required" (verification itself ships in P1, MDV-P1-007).

Summary: Server-side authorisation from the Foundations role-permission matrix
Description: Encode the role-permission matrix (solo doctor, doctor, receptionist, nurse, practice admin, care coordinator, patient; hospital roles later) as capabilities. ASP.NET Core authorization policies check tenant, facility, role/capability, and — as hooks for P2 — care relationship and purpose. Every endpoint must declare a policy; an architecture test fails the build for any endpoint without one. Export the matrix as docs (role matrix is part of the P0 delivery package).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Every API endpoint has an explicit authorization policy; an automated test enumerates endpoints and fails if any is anonymous by accident (allow-list for public endpoints).
* A receptionist calling a clinical-note endpoint gets 403 regardless of UI (security test), and the attempt is audited as "Denied".
* Capabilities per role match the Foundations matrix cell-by-cell (table-driven test generated from docs/02-design/data/foundations.json).
* Custom roles can only be composed from existing capabilities; locked capabilities from a built-in role cannot be granted (preparation for F-10).
* docs/02-design/sitemap-and-permissions.md is the published role matrix and is linked from the R0 release notes.

Summary: System state screens: session expired, 403 no facility access, 404, offline
Description: Implement F-05a Session expired, F-05b No access to this facility (Request access), F-05c Page not found (Back to Today), F-05d You are offline (Retry now) with the designed copy, icons and single CTA. API Problem Details 401/403/404 map to these screens; offline detection uses navigator.onLine + failed fetch.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A 401 from any API shows F-05a at once, without waiting for the session poll.
* A 403 from any API re-reads the session: a membership that was revoked or suspended leaves the facility, and a missing capability keeps the screen's own refusal (microcopy key err.403).
* A member removed from their only clinic sees F-05b "You don’t have access to this facility.", not the practice setup wizard.
* "Request access" (stored, audited, notifies the owner) ships with care-relationship access in MDV-P2-024; pilot clinics add staff by invitation (MDV-P0-013).
* An unknown route shows F-05c and states that nothing has been changed.
* Going offline shows F-05d without losing form input; reconnecting restores the page.
* Each state is keyboard-accessible, announced to screen readers, and translated (en/hi/ar) with RTL layout for Arabic.

Summary: Data classification register and ERD → PostgreSQL type mapping
Description: Produce docs/03-architecture/data-classification.md listing every planned field for P0–P2 entities with its class (public, internal, personal, sensitive health, national ID) and control (RLS, masking, Always Encrypted, audit-on-read). Finalise the ERD → Azure SQL mapping (uuid → uniqueidentifier, jsonb → json/nvarchar(max)+ISJSON, exclusion constraint → unique slot index + app lock, RLS policies → security predicates, money → bigint minor units). Add a [Classification] attribute in code used by the PHI redaction processor and EF configuration.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Every column in the P0 schema has a classification attribute; a unit test fails if a new entity property lacks one.
* The register lists the encrypted national-ID column set and the masked-view set used by MDV-P0-009.
* The mapping table closes the PRD completeness item "ERD mapped to Azure SQL types" (status Covered).
* The data map (what data, where stored, which country, which processors) is published as part of the P0 delivery package.

Summary: Append-only audit log on hash-chained PostgreSQL tables with audit middleware
Description: AUDIT_EVENT as an append-only ledger table: actor, tenant, facility, patient ref (opaque id), action, resource ref, purpose, outcome (allowed/denied), timestamp, IP, correlation id — no PHI values. A mediator behaviour and endpoint filter write an event for every read and write of patient data, sign-in, export and permission change. Ledger digests are exported daily to immutable Blob and verified by a scheduled job.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Every endpoint tagged as patient-data read or write produces exactly one audit event per request (test enumerates endpoints).
* The app identity cannot UPDATE or DELETE audit rows (permission test); ledger verification detects a tampered row in a test database.
* Audit events contain opaque patient ids only; a test scans payloads for names, phone numbers and identifiers and fails if found.
* Daily digest export to an immutable (time-based retention) container succeeds and verification runs on schedule with an alert on mismatch.
* Denied authorization attempts are audited with outcome "denied".

Summary: Observability with OpenTelemetry and PHI redaction (structured logs, telemetry processor)
Description: OpenTelemetry tracing/metrics/logs → Application Insights. A telemetry processor drops request/response bodies, query strings, auth headers, blob URLs and any field marked sensitive by the classification attribute. Structured logging with message templates only (no string-concatenated values of classified fields). Front-end error reporting strips URLs with ids and never sends form values.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A test request containing a synthetic patient name, phone and Emirates ID produces telemetry in which none of those values appear (automated log scan in integration tests).
* Request bodies and query strings are never exported; correlation ids are.
* Dashboards show request rate, p95 latency, error rate and dependency failures for staging.
* An alert fires on 5xx rate > 2 % over 5 minutes in staging/prod.

Summary: Backups, point-in-time restore and a timed restore drill
Description: Configure PITR retention (35 days in prod), long-term retention per country rule, backups kept in-country; storage soft delete/versioning for Blob. Write runbook docs/runbooks/restore.md and perform one restore of staging to a new database, verifying data and timing.
Acceptance Criteria:
* PITR and LTR settings are defined in Bicep, not set by hand.
* A restore drill of staging completes and the elapsed time is recorded in the runbook (P0 exit gate 2).
* Restored database passes a smoke test (row counts per table match the point in time).
* Backup storage redundancy keeps data in-country (no geo-replication outside the country).

Summary: Medvya design system in code: shadcn/ui + Tailwind tokens and clinical status primitives (packages/ui)
Description: packages/ui is the design system (ADR-010): shadcn/ui components (Radix) and Tailwind 4 tokens from Foundations/Handoff (`styles.css`), plus the clinical primitives: Button states (default/hover/focus/loading/disabled with count), StatusChip (ordered/received/reviewed/completed, icon + label), ProvenanceTag (AI draft · not reviewed dashed violet / Verified / Synced from HIS / Patient reported / Imported / Signed), Alert (critical/attention/info with words), TextField states, RecordingPill (REC/paused/declined), IdentityBanner (name, age, sex, MRN, DOB, allergies never collapsed, consent, encounter, SYNTHETIC marker). A storybook-like gallery page in web/clinic (/__ui) shows every state.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Tokens in packages/ui/src/styles.css (palette, Manrope/JetBrains Mono, radius 10, breakpoints 360/768/1280/1600) match docs/02-design/tokens.md, with WCAG deviations listed in docs/02-design/README.md; buttons are ≥ 44px, bold, not uppercase; cards have a 1px #DFE7ED border and no shadow.
* Every primitive renders all states listed in Handoff §1; no status is conveyed by colour alone (icon + text present, checked by test).
* Focus ring is 2px #2563EB with 2px offset on all interactive primitives.
* axe reports no violations on the gallery page; text contrast of tokens matches the Foundations ratios (≥ 4.5:1 for text).
* prefers-reduced-motion disables animation in RecordingPill/progress.

Summary: Internationalisation pipeline: English, Hindi, Arabic with full RTL
Description: packages/i18n with ICU message format, keys from Handoff microcopy (ai.badge, note.signBlocked, consent.declined, result.received, msg.delivered, pay.pending, ai.unavailable, err.403, push.generic …). Locale switch en/hi/ar; Arabic switches MUI to RTL (stylis RTL plugin, logical properties), Noto Sans Arabic font, flipped directional icons. Brand name "Medvya" comes from a single key so the working name can be replaced globally.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Switching to Arabic flips layout direction for the whole app shell and the gallery without visual overlap (Playwright screenshot test at 360 and 1280 px).
* No user-facing string is hard-coded in components (lint rule fails on JSX text literals outside i18n).
* Missing translation keys fall back to English and are reported in CI.
* Handoff microcopy keys exist with the exact English text from docs/02-design/components-theme-copy.md.
* Numbers, dates and currency format per locale and country (₹ with Indian grouping, AED).

Summary: App shell with role-based navigation (desktop sidebar, tablet rail, mobile tabs)

Summary: Synthetic data generator and seeded staging tenant
Description:

Summary: Per-tenant feature flags with owner and kill switch

Summary: Shared Table component (shadcn) and table controller pattern; replace the four raw tables
Description: Add the shadcn `Table` set (Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell, TableCaption, scroll wrapper) to `packages/ui` through the shadcn CLI, with tokens, logical utilities for right-to-left, sticky header, numeric columns and 44 px row targets. Summary: Accept ADR-012: PostgreSQL with EF Core, application-level national-ID encryption, hash-chained audit
Description: Review and accept ADR-012 (Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server per country, EF Core on Npgsql, row-level security with `current_setting`, envelope encryption of national IDs with Key Vault keys and an HMAC blind index, hash-chained audit and signed records, masked views). Mark the SQL Server statements in ADR-001, 005 and 006 as superseded.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given ADR-012, when it is reviewed, then it is Accepted with date and decider and lists the alternatives rejected (Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, an ORM change).
* Given ADR-001, ADR-005 and ADR-006, when they are read, then each points to ADR-012 for what changed.

Summary: Swap the platform to PostgreSQL: Npgsql provider, Testcontainers.PostgreSql, Hangfire.PostgreSql, local services and CI
Description: Replace Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer with Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL, Hangfire.SqlServer with Hangfire.PostgreSql and Testcontainers.MsSql with Testcontainers.PostgreSql in `Directory.Packages.props`. docker-compose runs PostgreSQL 17 instead of SQL Server. CI runs the integration tests on Postgres. Replace SQL Server types and functions in the code (rowversion, datetimeoffset, NEWSEQUENTIALID, OPENJSON, HASHBYTES) with Postgres equivalents and keep time in UTC timestamptz and money in integer minor units.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the solution, when it builds, then no SqlServer package or type remains and warnings stay at zero.
* Given CI, when it runs, then the integration tests run against PostgreSQL in Testcontainers.
* Given local services, when they start, then PostgreSQL, Azurite and the email sink come up with one command.

Summary: One baseline migration per module on Postgres, regenerated seeder and ERD, forward-only after that
Description: No real data exists yet, so delete the 46 SQL Server migrations and create one baseline migration per module on Postgres (schemas per module kept). From then on migrations are forward-only and reviewed. Regenerate the ERD (`python3 -I tools/erd/generate.py`), update the seeder and the dev database. Merge freeze on schema-changing PRs from the moment this starts until it merges.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given an empty Postgres database, when migrations run, then every module schema exists from its single baseline.
* Given the ERD, when the baseline merges, then `docs/03-architecture/erd.md` is regenerated and CI is green.
* Given a schema-changing PR, when is open during the freeze, then it is rebased onto the baseline before merge.

Summary: Tenant isolation on Postgres: FORCE row-level security, per-module roles, EF filter kept as layer one
Description: Rewrite ADR-005's mechanism for Postgres: every clinic table has `tenant_id`, `ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` with policies reading `current_setting('medvya.tenant_id', true)`, set per connection through the existing interceptor with `set_config(..., false)` reset on return to the pool, and the facility-picker `user_id` branch kept. Replace `infra/sql/roles.sql` with an idempotent Postgres roles script (migrator, app, one role per module, jobs, audit, reporting) with no BYPASSRLS and no superuser for the app. Keep EF global query filters as layer one.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a cross-tenant read or write, when the EF filter is bypassed, then row-level security still blocks it (test fails when the policy is removed).
* Given the app role, when it connects, then it has no DDL, no BYPASSRLS and only its module schema.
* Given a pooled connection, when it is reused for another tenant, then the tenant setting is reset first.
* Given the facility picker, when it runs with only a user id, then it sees that user's memberships and nothing else.

Summary: National IDs unreadable to database admins: envelope encryption with Key Vault keys and an HMAC blind index
Description: Replace Always Encrypted. National and insurance IDs are encrypted in the application with AES-256-GCM using a per-tenant data key that is wrapped by an Azure Key Vault key (the database never holds an unwrapped key). Exact-match lookup uses an HMAC-SHA-256 blind index with a separate Key Vault key. An EF value converter keeps the `NationalId` type and the `[Classification]` rule. Key rotation re-wraps data keys without rewriting rows. Only the app identity may unwrap; admins and support roles cannot.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a database admin, when reads the column with raw SQL, then only ciphertext is visible.
* Given a lookup by national ID, when it runs, then it uses the blind index and finds exactly one patient.
* Given a key is rotated, when the job runs, then data keys are re-wrapped and existing rows still decrypt.
* Given Key Vault, when is unreachable, then the app fails closed and logs no identifier.

Summary: Tamper-evident audit and signed records without SQL ledger: hash chain, append-only triggers, daily digest to immutable Blob
Description: Replace ledger tables for audit events, signed note versions, consent receipts and issued invoices: each row stores the hash of the previous row (per tenant chain), triggers refuse UPDATE and DELETE for the app roles, and a daily job writes a signed digest to an immutable (time-based retention) Blob container and a scheduled job verifies the chain and alerts on mismatch. Hashes are integrity evidence, not a legally qualified signature.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given an audit row, when an UPDATE or DELETE is attempted, then the database refuses it (test fails when the trigger is removed).
* Given a row is altered by a superuser, when verification runs, then the chain mismatch is found and an alert is raised.
* Given the daily digest, when it is written, then it lands in the immutable container and can be verified later.

Summary: Support and reporting access without dynamic masking: reporting role, masked views, no decrypt right
Description: Replace SQL Server dynamic data masking: the reporting and support role reads only masked views (initials, age band, last four of identifiers as ciphertext length only), has no unwrap right and no write. Tests prove the role sees no clear name, date of birth, contact or identifier.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the reporting role, when it queries a patient view, then identifiers and contact fields are masked.
* Given the reporting role, when it tries a base table, then the database denies it.

Summary: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server in Bicep: private endpoint, Entra-only auth, customer-managed key, in-country HA and point-in-time restore
Description: Supersedes the SQL parts of MDV-P0-006, 008, 009 and 019. One Flexible Server per country (Central or South India first), private endpoint only, Entra-only authentication with managed identities, customer-managed key for storage, zone-redundant HA and PITR kept in-country, logs to the country workspace, Azure Policy denying other regions, and a timed restore drill.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the Bicep, when it deploys, then the server has no public endpoint and password login is off.
* Given a restore drill, when it runs, then point-in-time restore completes within the agreed time and is timed in the runbook.
* Given a resource, when is created outside the allowed regions, then policy denies it.

Summary: Re-baseline load and desk tests on Postgres
Description:
Also measure the cost of the hash-chain trigger (MDV-P0-036): AccessLogTests seeds 150,000 audit events through the per-row chain trigger; locally that takes seconds but on a shared CI runner it exceeded Npgsql's 30 s default (fixed for the tests with a 300 s command timeout). Record the rows-per-second of an audit insert and of a bulk load, and decide whether bulk loads of ledgered tables need a batch path before the P5 legacy migration.
The P1-037 budgets were measured on SQL Server. Re-run the booking, check-in and calendar load tests on Postgres, confirm 0 double bookings in 100 parallel bookings, and update the budgets and docs.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given 100 parallel bookings for one slot, when they run, then exactly one succeeds.
* Given the desk load profile, when it runs, then the p95 budgets in load-testing.md still hold or are updated with evidence.
* Given the hash-chain trigger, when 150,000 audit events are inserted on the CI runner, then the rows per second are recorded in load-testing.md and the AccessLog 30-day budget test passes without a raised timeout, or the batch path decision is recorded.

Summary: Repository structure: Host.Api to composition only, mobile and shared packages in the workspace, tickets and design into docs, link check, CI path filters
Description:
Apply ADR-013. Keep `src/`, `web/`, `tests/`, `infra/`, `tools/` and `packages/` where they are (renaming them for taste costs hundreds of reference edits for no benefit). Add what the roadmap needs, and create a folder only when the ticket that builds it starts (no empty scaffolding). Do it inside the schema-change freeze that MDV-P0-033 needs: this ticket merges first, then MDV-P0-033 builds the baseline migration. Use `git mv`; one PR per chunk; CI green after each; chunk 3 goes last because it rewrites paths the others touch.
Chunk 1, Host.Api to composition only: the feature endpoints in `src/Host.Api` (AuditLog, Invitations, Notifications, Onboarding, Settings, Staff) move into module Api projects (AuditLog to Audit, Invitations and Staff to Identity, Notifications to a new Notifications.Api, Settings and Onboarding to Tenancy or a new Practice module if they span modules). Host keeps Program.cs, Auth/BFF, Context, Middleware, Observability, PublicSite and module registration. An architecture test fails when Host holds endpoints, services or entities of a feature.
Chunk 2, workspace and shared packages: `mobile/*` added to pnpm-workspace.yaml with the rules in ADR-013; `packages/tokens` split out of `packages/ui` (CSS variables for web, a theme object for native); `packages/api-client` generated from the OpenAPI document that Host.Api exports at build time, with a CI drift check; the two `parts.tsx` files split into named components; lint import boundaries for packages (no package imports an app, native packages never import web UI).
Chunk 3, docs consolidation: `tickets/` becomes `docs/05-delivery/tickets/` and `design/` becomes `docs/02-design/source/`; every reference in tools (tickets build, gh_issues footer, prd-extract, ERD), CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README and docs is rewritten; CI gains a relative-link check.
Chunk 4, CI and docs: path filters per area (backend, web, mobile, packages, infra, docs), CODEOWNERS and dependabot paths, `docs/03-architecture/repository-structure.md` and README updated to the real tree, layout rules added to AGENTS.md.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given `src/Host.Api`, when the architecture test runs, then it fails if endpoints, services or entities of a feature are present, and passes with only composition, auth/BFF, middleware, observability and the public site.
* Given each moved endpoint group, when its existing tests run, then they pass unchanged and every endpoint still declares a policy or is explicitly public.
* Given `packages/api-client` or the exported OpenAPI document, when either drifts from the API, then CI fails.
* Given `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, when `pnpm install` runs, then `web/*`, `mobile/*` and `packages/*` resolve and no package imports an app.
* Given the whole repo, when the link checker runs, then there are zero broken relative links and CI runs it.
* Given the repository root, when listed, then `tickets/` and `design/` are gone and everything they held is under docs.
* Given a change to one area, when CI runs, then only the affected jobs run and the required checks still gate the merge.
* Given the new tree, when `dotnet build`, `dotnet test`, `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm -r lint`, `pnpm -r test`, `pnpm e2e` and `python3 -I tools/tickets/build.py` run, then all pass.

Summary: Postgres hardening from the security review: narrower grants, DataKeys protection, stable ledger hash, destructive-migration gate
Description: Fix the confirmed findings that are not Azure wiring. (a) `patients.DataKeys`: REVOKE DELETE for the module role and allow UPDATE only through the re-wrap path; `TenantKeyRing.Get` must throw, not silently create a new key, when the tenant already has encrypted identifier rows but no key row (otherwise a deleted key row makes every identifier unreadable). (b) `medvya_reporting` gets per-table SELECT on `tenancy` (or masked views for Invitations, DoctorLicences, Profiles, SettingsChanges) instead of SELECT on all tables. (c) Ledger hash: hash an explicit column list stored per table in `ledger.Tables`, not `to_jsonb(row)`, so adding a column later does not break every old chain; a test adds a column and verifies the chain still passes. (d) Exempt tables (`ledger.Tables`, `ledger.Chains`, `TenantIndex`, `OutboxTenants`): revoke DELETE, insert into `ledger.Tables` only from migrations, and have the ledger functions ignore unknown table names. (e) Gate the destructive national-ID migration with a data-present check that fails loudly outside an empty database. (f) Document in database-security.md that the tenant and user settings are user-settable and who may hold app or reporting logins (accepted limit, for the external review). (g) Bind each ciphertext to its row (add the row id to the associated data) or record why not.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a module role, when it tries to DELETE a DataKeys row, then the database refuses it.
* Given a tenant with identifier rows and no key row, when the key is requested, then the call throws and no new key is created.
* Given the reporting role, when it reads Invitations, DoctorLicences or Profiles, then it is refused or sees only masked columns.
* Given a column is added to a ledger table, when verify_chain runs, then every old chain still verifies.
* Given an app role, when it deletes from ledger.Chains or TenantIndex, then the database refuses it.
* Given a database that already holds identifier rows, when the national-ID migration runs, then it stops with a clear error instead of dropping data.

Summary: Make the Azure dev environment actually run on PostgreSQL: app settings, Entra token connection, migration runner in the deploy workflow, immutable ledger-digests container
Description: The review found the deployed environment cannot work yet. (1) `infra/bicep/main.bicep` sets `Postgres__Host`, `Postgres__Database` and `ColumnEncryption__KeyVaultKeyUrl`, but the code reads `ConnectionStrings:Medvya`, `NationalIdProtection:KeyVaultKeyId`, `Audit:DigestKey` and `Storage:ConnectionString`. Align the names, add `Audit__DigestKey` as a Key Vault reference, and connect with an Entra access token (Npgsql with the managed identity; no password). (2) `.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml` still runs SQL firewall rules and an SQL connection; migrations must run from inside the private network (self-hosted runner, a Container Apps job or a deploy-time job in the VNet) as `medvya_migrator` then apply `infra/postgres/roles.sql`. (3) Create the `ledger-digests` container in Bicep with a locked time-based immutability policy, give the app identity append-only access, and make a missing digest Critical once any digest has existed. (4) Use the versionless Key Vault key URI everywhere so rotation needs no redeploy. Prove it with a real dev deployment and a smoke test: sign in, create a patient, see the audit chain verify.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the Bicep app settings, when the app starts in Azure, then it finds a database connection, the national-ID key id and the digest key and registers every module.
* Given the deploy workflow, when a tag is pushed, then migrations and roles run inside the private network and the deploy succeeds with no SQL firewall step.
* Given the ledger-digests container, when anyone with the app identity tries to delete or overwrite a digest, then the storage account refuses it.
* Given a tenant chain that has had a digest, when the digest is missing at verification, then a Critical alert is raised, not a warning.
* Given the dev environment, when the smoke test runs, then sign-in, patient create and chain verification all pass.

Summary: Public site on Razor Pages and landing page (clinic / hospital CTAs, region-aware copy)
Description: Server-rendered Razor Pages in Host.Api/PublicSite (no patient data). Nav: For doctors · For hospitals · Trust centre · Pricing (placeholder) · region switch India/UAE · Sign in. Summary: Country and data-residency selector that binds a new tenant to one data plane
Description: "Where do you practise?" with India (Azure Central India · DPDP Act · ABDM integration available) and UAE (Azure UAE North · separate deployment · DoH/DHA/MOHAP per emirate) cards. Summary: Clinic sign-up with the six-step onboarding wizard (autosave); the onboarding request itself is MDV-P1-062
Description: Steps: 1 Your profile · 2 Licence (council/authority, number, certificate upload; "Verification pending" notice) · 3 Clinic (name, address, CE reg./facility licence, GSTIN/TRN) · 4 Hours & fees · 5 Note templates (multi-select, used from P2/P3) · 6 Invite your team (optional). Summary: Practice settings: profile, locations, operating hours and holidays (F-08)
Description: /settings with tabs: Profile (clinic name, logo "Shown on prescriptions, invoices and the patient portal", address, registration numbers, contact), Locations (multiple sites, rooms/resources such as procedure room), Hours (operating hours per location, weekday toggles), Holidays (closures; booking blocked). Description: Notifications tab: which events send messages (booking confirmation, 24 h reminder, 2 h reminder, cancellation), channels enabled (email, SMS; WhatsApp placeholder for P4), sender name, quiet hours, template preview (no clinical details). Summary: Add doctor (clinic mode): details, licence India/UAE, verification, schedule link, fees, access and signature image (F-09)
Description: Settings → Doctors → Add doctor wizard: details (name, specialty, qualifications, languages) → licence (country, authority: state medical council/NMC or DoH/DHA/MOHAP, number, category, expiry, certificate upload) → verification (status pending/verified/rejected, verified_by, verified_at; done by Medvya operations or owner attestation per policy) → schedule (link to MDV-P1-011) → fees (default consultation fees; full services in P4) → access (role and facility scope) → signature (drawn or uploaded image; optional clinic stamp). Creates CLINICIAN_PROFILE and CLINICIAN_LICENCE and sends an invitation.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A doctor cannot record or sign until licence status is Verified; the restriction is enforced server-side.
* Licence number format is validated per authority where a format is known; expiry date is required.
* The verification decision records who verified and when, and is audited; rejected licences notify the owner with the reason.
* The signature image is stored privately and appears only on printed prescriptions; the UI states "Signing in Medvya is always an authenticated action by the doctor (passkey / MFA), never the image alone."
* The new doctor appears in schedule columns once hours are set.

Summary: Add staff with role, facility scope, permissions and invite; custom roles (F-10)
Description: Settings → Staff: table (Name, Role, Access, MFA, Status) and "Add staff member": role picker with descriptions (receptionist, nurse, care coordinator, practice admin; doctors redirected to Add doctor) → facility scope and hours → permissions (locked rows from the role cannot be granted/removed here) → invite. Custom roles composed from capabilities.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Choosing "Doctor" shows "Doctors need licence verification. Use Settings → Doctors → Add doctor." and does not create a staff membership.
* Locked permissions from a built-in role are displayed but not editable; custom roles cannot exceed the capabilities of practice admin.
* The invite uses the P0 flow; the staff table shows invited/active/suspended/offboarded and MFA enrolment state.
* Every permission change is written to the audit log ("Every change is written to the audit log").
* A receptionist created here cannot open clinical endpoints (security test reused from P0).

Summary: Staff offboarding removes access immediately and ends all sessions
Description: "Offboard" on a staff member sets membership to offboarded, revokes all sessions and devices for that tenant, cancels pending invites, reassigns or flags their open items (none clinical yet in P1), and records reason and actor.
Acceptance Criteria:
* After offboarding, the next request from any of the person's sessions in that tenant fails within 60 seconds and they cannot sign in to that tenant.
* Memberships in other tenants are unaffected.
* The action requires confirmation, a reason, and is audited.
* The last practice admin cannot offboard themselves (prevents lock-out).

Summary: Licence/registration expiry reminders and quarterly access review prompt
Description: Scheduled job notifies owners 60/30/7 days before a doctor licence or facility registration expires and on expiry (doctor recording/signing then disabled again). Quarterly access review: owners get a task listing every active membership, role and last sign-in; they confirm or offboard each and the completion is recorded.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Expiry notifications are sent at 60/30/7/0 days and appear in the notification centre (D-03) and by email.
* On expiry, capabilities that require a verified licence are disabled server-side until renewed and re-verified.
* The quarterly review lists all memberships and records a decision per person; completion date is shown in settings.
* Both jobs are idempotent and audited.

Summary: Schedule templates: working hours, breaks, slot length per service, per-location calendars, time zones
Description: Per doctor and location: weekly template (weekday, start, end, room/resource), breaks (e.g. lunch), default slot length (15/20/30 min) and per-visit-type length (e.g. new consult 40 min = 2 slots). Facility time zone; all times stored UTC and displayed in facility time. Resources (procedure room) can be scheduled like a doctor column. Generates bookable slots on the fly (no pre-materialised slot table required) or materialises slots per day — decision recorded.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a template Mon–Fri 09:00–13:00 and 17:00–20:00 with 20-minute slots, then the calendar shows bookable slots exactly in those windows in facility local time.
* Breaks and closed days show as Unavailable (hatched) with the reason and cannot be booked.
* Changing a template affects only future unbooked slots; existing appointments outside new hours are listed for action.
* Visit types can span multiple slots and the calendar renders them spanning.
* Daylight-saving-free zones (IST, GST) and a test zone with DST are handled correctly (unit tests).

Summary: Leave and schedule exceptions with re-offer of affected appointments
Description: Add leave (from, to, reason) or one-off exceptions (extra session, shortened day). Before saving, the system lists booked patients in the range; reception chooses to offer new slots (sends rebooking message with link/phone) or reschedule manually. Leave is saved only after each affected appointment has an action.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Saving leave that overlaps booked appointments shows the count and list and requires an action per appointment before save.
* Affected patients receive a rebooking message (no clinical details) and the appointments move to "needs rebooking" on the board.
* Extra sessions create bookable slots for that day only.
* Leave and exceptions are audited.

Summary: Patient registration — India full flow (identity, ABHA optional, Aadhaar last 4, Indian address, payer)
Description: /patients/new full mode, India: steps Identity & IDs → Contact & address → Family & emergency (MDV-P1-020) → Payer → Consents (MDV-P1-019) → Review (MDV-P1-016). Identity: first/last name, DOB or age ("estimated"), sex at birth, optional gender identity, preferred language, ABHA number (14 digits) and address (optional, manual entry; "Verify with ABHA" banner shows the P8 path as disabled/coming later), other ID type with Aadhaar last 4 only. Contact: mobile (required), alternate, email, house/flat, street, city, district, state/UT, PIN (6 digits), country. Payer: self-pay / corporate / private insurance (TPA) / government scheme (reference only). Side panel shows preview card and the country rules (the "Data map · this step writes" panel was removed by MDV-P1-052 as developer-facing text).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Minimum to register (India): name, DOB or age, sex, mobile; other fields optional; validation messages match the design (e.g. "PIN code must be 6 digits").
* Aadhaar can only be stored as last 4 digits; entering 12 digits is rejected with an explanation; ABHA is stored with envelope encryption (ADR-012) and is never required for care.
* On save, PATIENT (demographics), PATIENT_IDENTIFIER (tokenised), PAYER_COVERAGE, CONSENT_RECEIPT and AUDIT_EVENT PatientRegistered.v1 (no PHI in payload) are written in one transaction and a facility-scoped MRN is assigned.
* The success screen shows name, MRN, timestamp and actor and offers Book appointment · Check in now (walk-in) · Register another.
* The receptionist cannot see any clinical data from the registration or directory screens (security test).
* Form is keyboard-completable, errors announced via aria-live, works at tablet width.

Summary: Patient registration — UAE flow (Emirates ID manual entry, Arabic name RTL, emirate, insurance card)
Description: UAE variant: full name as on EID (English) + Arabic name (RTL input, Noto Sans Arabic), DOB, sex, nationality, preferred language, Emirates ID (format 784-YYYY-NNNNNNN-N) and expiry, passport/visa for visitors; UAE address (villa/building, area, emirate required, Makani optional, P.O. Box); payer insurance/self-pay/corporate with insurer/plan, member card no. (envelope-encrypted), card expiry, network; eligibility marked "M4/P5".
Acceptance Criteria:
* Minimum to register (UAE): name, DOB, sex, mobile and Emirates ID or passport.
* Invalid EID format shows "Format 784-YYYY-NNNNNNN-N"; an expired EID shows a warning but never blocks registration.
* Arabic name field accepts RTL input and displays correctly in the preview card and review step.
* The selected emirate determines the HIE label (Malaffi / NABIDH / Riayati) shown in consents (no connection in P1).
* UAE tenant data is stored only in the UAE deployment (configuration test: UAE tenant cannot be created in the India deployment).

Summary: Quick registration for a busy desk with a completion task
Description: Mode toggle "Quick (busy desk)" with minimum safe fields (India: full name, mobile, DOB or age, sex, ABHA optional; UAE: name as on EID, mobile, DOB, sex, Emirates ID). On save, a CARE_TASK-like front-desk completion task "Address, emergency contact and payer are missing" is added to the queue for the patient's next arrival; payer shows Missing.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Quick registration can be completed in under 45 seconds by a trained user with keyboard only (timed usability check).
* After quick save, the patient card on the board and the patient header show an "Incomplete registration" tag until the task is closed.
* Completing the missing fields later closes the task automatically.
* Duplicate check (MDV-P1-016) still runs in quick mode.

Summary: Duplicate warning while typing and duplicate resolution before save
Description: As name + DOB (and identifiers) are typed, call /v1/patients/duplicate-check (debounced) and show "Possible match" inline. On the Review step, a side-by-side NEW vs EXISTING panel ("Attention · possible existing record. Matched on name + date of birth. A shared phone number alone is never treated as a match.") with actions: Not the same person · continue / Use existing record / Request merge review (P-03). Save is blocked ("Resolve duplicate to save") until one is chosen.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A candidate is suggested when name similarity + identical DOB, or an exact identifier (ABHA/EID/passport) match exists; phone-only matches never produce a suggestion (test).
* Duplicate-check responses show initials, age and masked identifiers only, never full details of the other record until "Use existing record" is chosen.
* Save remains disabled until the receptionist resolves the duplicate; the decision and actor are audited.
* "Use existing record" opens that patient without creating a new one; "Request merge review" creates a merge request (MDV-P1-017).
* p95 duplicate-check latency < 300 ms on staging data of 50,000 synthetic patients.

Summary: Duplicate / merge review with second approver when both records hold clinical data (P-03)
Description: /patients/merge: side-by-side comparison (name, DOB, sex, mobile, ABHA/EID, visits, allergies) with actions Not the same person / Request clinician approval. Merge executes only after approval; when both records have clinical data (from P2 on) a second approver (clinician) is required. Merge keeps both originals, maps the loser to the survivor and is reversible.
Acceptance Criteria:
* "Not the same person" closes the request and suppresses the same pair from future suggestions.
* A merge without the required approver(s) is impossible (server-side), and approvals are audited.
* After merge, searching either MRN finds the surviving record; appointments and identifiers move; the merge can be undone by an admin within the retention period.
* Merge history is visible on the patient record.

Summary: Patient directory and privacy-safe search for the front desk
Description: Search by name, MRN, phone, ABHA/EID (exact). Results show the full name, age, sex and the MRN and phone tails (MDV-AUDIT-1100, a product decision of 13 Nov 2026: staff who register and book can see the name; the doctor's ⌘K lookup still shows initials); the rest of the record needs it opened, which is audited with purpose "registration/booking". Directory list with filters (incomplete registration, recently registered) and pagination. Blind-index (HMAC) columns support exact ID lookups.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Searching by full phone number or exact EID/ABHA returns the matching patient(s); partial ID search is not allowed.
* Result rows show the full name, age, sex and MRN and phone tails (never the whole phone, birth date or identifiers); full demographics appear only after opening, which writes an audit event.
* Empty state: "No patients match. Register a new patient".
* Search p95 < 300 ms with 50,000 synthetic patients; endpoint rate-limited.

Summary: Legal terms and separate versioned consents at registration (treatment, reminders per channel, sharing, portal, marketing)
Description: Tenant level: owner accepts Medvya Terms of Service and the clinic Data Processing Agreement during onboarding; the clinic privacy notice is published (versioned). Patient level (Consents step): treatment (required, locked), reminders on WhatsApp/SMS (per channel), link to ABHA (India) / HIE (UAE, per emirate), portal access (invite in P4), health tips & offers (off by default). Each decision stores CONSENT_RECEIPT with consent_type, policy_version, jurisdiction, decision, decided_at, channel and actor. Recording consent is NOT asked here (per-visit, P3).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Every consent is a separate toggle; marketing defaults off; treatment is required and cannot be toggled off.
* Each decision creates an immutable receipt (ledger) with policy version and jurisdiction; changing a decision creates a new receipt and keeps history.
* The privacy notice version shown at registration is the currently published one; publishing a new version does not alter old receipts.
* Activation is one accepted-terms record on the tenant (terms version, timestamp, who accepted): until it exists, the production tenant cannot book appointments or send messages; accepting it records all three (decision 5 Nov 2026, built on the draft wording).
* Reminder sending (MDV-P1-032/033) checks the channel consent before every send (test).
* Final wording is the legally reviewed text from MDV-P1-044 in en/hi/ar.

Summary: Family, emergency contact and guardian rules (under-18 guardian required)
Description: PATIENT_RELATIONSHIP: emergency contact name, relationship, phone (required for full registration), guardian (required when age < 18; UAE: guardian/sponsor for dependants). Note shown: emergency contacts get no portal access; caregiver access is via patient-authorised proxy (P4 R-04).
Acceptance Criteria:
* When DOB indicates age < 18, guardian becomes required and save is blocked without it.
* Emergency contact is required for full registration but not for quick registration.
* Emergency contacts never receive portal access or patient data (no account is created).
* Relationship values are country-specific (UAE includes Sponsor).

Summary: Create an appointment from the calendar with a short slot hold
Description: Clicking an empty slot opens the booking panel for that doctor/resource and time; select or register a patient, visit type (sets length), reason category (free-text reason never shown on reception screens beyond category), channel. A slot hold (default 2 minutes) reserves the slot while the receptionist completes the form; confirmation creates the appointment and triggers the confirmation message (MDV-P1-032).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Opening the booking panel creates a hold; another user trying the same slot sees it as "being booked" and cannot confirm it.
* Holds expire automatically after the configured time and the slot becomes free.
* A booking for an unavailable column (doctor not working) is impossible from UI and API.
* Booking writes AppointmentBooked.v1 (no PHI) and an audit event; the appointment appears on the board in Booked.
* Booking API p95 < 300 ms under the P1 load profile (MDV-P1-037).

Summary: No double booking under concurrency (unique index, serializable transaction, doctor-day app lock)
Description: Filtered unique index on (doctor_id, location_id, slot_start) for non-cancelled appointments; booking inside a transaction holding pg_advisory_xact_lock on "doctor:{id}:{date}"; the frontend check is only a convenience. Multi-slot visits reserve every covered slot.
Acceptance Criteria:
* An automated test fires 100 parallel booking attempts at one slot; exactly one succeeds and 99 receive a clear "slot no longer available" error (exit gate 2), on Testcontainers PostgreSQL and on staging.
* Overlapping multi-slot bookings are rejected the same way.
* Deadlocks/lock timeouts are retried safely without creating duplicates.
* The test runs in CI on every PR touching Scheduling.

Summary: Calendar views: day, week and list (per doctor and resource), mobile/tablet responsive
Description: Day view with columns per doctor/resource and time rows; week view per doctor; list view (agenda) for mobile and printing. Appointment chips show name, type, time and state with icon + label (Booked, Checked in, In room, Completed, No-show dashed, Cancelled dashed, Unavailable hatched). Doctor filter, date navigation, today button. Doctors see their own schedule view (read-only booking actions per permissions).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Calendar first render < 2.5 s on a clinic PC over throttled 4G for a 3-doctor day (Lighthouse/Playwright perf budget).
* States are distinguishable without colour (icon + label) and announced to screen readers; empty slots are buttons with accessible names like "Book Dr. Arjun Rao at 10:20".
* Week and list views show the same appointments as day view (consistency test).
* At ≤ 767 px the list/agenda view is the default with a pinned "+ Book" action.

Summary: Reschedule (incl. drag with confirm), cancel with reason, mark no-show with rebook offer
Description: Detail panel actions with state rules: Check in (only Booked), Reschedule (not Completed), Cancel (asks reason; not Completed/Cancelled), Mark no-show (only Booked). Drag-and-drop reschedule asks for confirmation and uses the same booking concurrency path. No-show offers "Rebook" which opens booking with the patient preselected. Reschedule/cancel notify the patient (MDV-P1-032).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Disallowed actions are disabled with an explanation and rejected by the API if called.
* Cancel without a reason is impossible; reasons are a short list + free text.
* A reschedule keeps history (old slot, new slot, actor, time) and frees the old slot atomically.
* No-show offers rebook and is counted in the no-show metric (MDV-P1-041).

Summary: Walk-in registration and booking straight to the queue
Description: "Walk-in" on the board: find or quick-register the patient, choose doctor (or "next available"), create an appointment in the next free slot or as an unscheduled walk-in, and check in immediately; card tagged Walk-in. Timing a trained receptionist at under 60 seconds is an acceptance criterion of MDV-P1-040, which owns reception training at the pilot (owner decision 10 Nov 2026).
Acceptance Criteria:
* If no slot is free, the walk-in is queued without breaking the no-double-booking rule (unscheduled walk-ins do not occupy slots).
* Walk-ins appear in the Checked in column with wait time and the Walk-in tag.

Summary: Recurring appointments (series) with per-occurrence exceptions
Description: Create a series (e.g. weekly physiotherapy × 10): each occurrence is a normal appointment booked through the same concurrency path; conflicts are reported before confirming; editing/cancelling one occurrence or "this and following".
Acceptance Criteria:
* Creating a series shows which occurrences conflict and lets the user skip or move them before confirming.
* Each occurrence is an independent appointment protected by the double-booking rules.
* Cancelling "this and following" cancels the remaining series with one reason and one notification.

Summary: Waitlist with "offer earlier slot"
Description: Patients can be added to a waitlist with preference (doctor, days, earliest/time window). When a slot frees (cancellation/reschedule), matching waitlist entries are highlighted with "Offer {time}". Offering sends a message; acceptance books through the normal path.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A freed slot shows matching waitlist candidates ordered by request time.
* "Offer" places a hold and sends a message without clinical details; if not accepted within the hold window, the next candidate can be offered.
* Accepting books the slot and removes the patient from the waitlist.

Summary: Reception board with visit columns and one-tap check-in
Description: /front-desk board for today: Booked → Checked in → With nurse → Ready for doctor → In consult → Billing → Done with counts. Card shows name, time, doctor/visit type and nonclinical tags; CTA per column (Check in, Send to nurse, Intake done, Call in, Consult done, Payment received). "Receptionist view hides clinical notes" banner. Check-in for a returning patient: find appointment → confirm identity (name + DOB) → mark arrived, flag incomplete registration.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A returning patient with an appointment can be checked in with ≤ 3 interactions; median check-in time is instrumented from arrival click to checked-in (exit gate 3 measurement).
* Column transitions follow the visit state machine; invalid moves are rejected server-side.
* Cards never show clinical information (reason shown only as category); verified by a security test on the board API payload.
* Billing column exists but payment actions are placeholders until P4 (feature flag).
* Board works at tablet width (horizontal scroll per responsive rules).

Summary: Real-time board updates, call/room patient, nonclinical statuses (SignalR)
Description: SignalR hub scoped per tenant+facility pushes board changes to all open boards and Today views. "Call in" assigns a room and changes state; wait timers update live ("Waiting 12 min"). Reconnect logic resyncs state.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A state change on one device appears on another device's board within 2 seconds.
* Hub connections are authorised per facility; a user cannot subscribe to another facility's board (security test).
* After a network drop the board resyncs without duplicates or lost moves.
* Messages carry ids and nonclinical fields only.

Summary: Clinic overview: multi-doctor Today and shared waiting room (D-04)
Description: Clinic view showing each doctor's queue length, running delay and next patient, a shared waiting room list, and the ability to reassign a waiting patient to another doctor (with reason). Doctor workload panel on the board.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Overview lists every doctor working today with counts per state and current delay estimate.
* Reassigning a waiting patient moves the appointment to the other doctor's queue atomically and is audited.
* Doctors see their own schedule view in P1 (read-only) with their next patients.

Summary: Queue TV display with tokens only, never names (P-05)
Description: Tokens issued at check-in (prefix per doctor/room, e.g. A-07). TV route /queue/tv?display=… authenticated by a device display token (no user login) shows "Now: token · room · doctor" and "Next: token · ≈ wait". Large type, high contrast, auto-refresh via SignalR, works on a basic smart-TV browser.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The TV payload contains tokens, rooms, doctor display names and waits only; no patient names, MRNs or reasons (API contract test).
* Display tokens are revocable and scoped to one facility.
* Calling a patient updates the TV within 2 seconds and optionally plays a chime.
* Layout is readable at 3 metres (minimum 48px token text) and in Arabic/English.

Summary: Email confirmations and 24 h / 2 h reminders via SendGrid and Hangfire
Description: Hangfire server (Worker.Jobs) on PostgreSQL in its own schema/user — no Redis or Service Bus in P1. Email provider: SendGrid (founder decision 20 Oct 2026, free tier) behind the Notifications adapter; Azure Communication Services remains an alternative. Events: booking confirmation, reschedule, cancellation, 24 h and 2 h reminders, leave rebooking. Templates per tenant/language without clinical details. NOTIFICATION and NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT record provider id, delivery state and retries with backoff; reminders are cancelled when the appointment changes.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Booking triggers a confirmation within 1 minute; reminders are sent at 24 h and 2 h before (facility time), respecting quiet hours and channel consent.
* Rescheduling or cancelling cancels pending reminders and sends the right message once (idempotency test).
* Delivery status (queued, sent, delivered, failed, bounced) is stored and visible to reception for each appointment.
* Failed sends are retried with backoff up to the configured limit and then shown as failed on the board/notification centre.
* Hangfire dashboard is only reachable by Medvya operations through authenticated admin route; no Redis or Service Bus resources exist in P1 infrastructure.

Summary: SMS confirmations and reminders with India DLT templates and delivery receipts
Description: SMS adapter (Azure Communication Services where supported, otherwise a DLT-registered aggregator) behind the Notifications interface. India messages use the registered DLT template IDs and sender; UAE uses its approved sender. Delivery receipts update NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT. Reminder delivery rate is computed per clinic.
Acceptance Criteria:
* SMS uses only registered templates; a message not matching a registered template is not sent (validation test).
* Delivery receipts are processed (webhook verified/authenticated) and update status; failures are visible to reception.
* Delivery rate dashboard shows ≥ 98 % delivered during the pilot or lists every failure with reason (exit gate 4).
* Messages contain no clinical details; sender name is the clinic's.

Summary: Notification centre for staff (D-03), push-safe content
Description: Bell with count opens an overlay listing in-app notifications (kind, title, time) with "Mark all read". P1 events: reminder failed, leave rebooking needed, licence expiring, access request, quarterly access review due. Browser/phone push (optional) uses the generic text only.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Notifications are scoped to the user's tenant/facility and role.
* Push or browser notifications never include patient names or results; content is "New update from {clinic}. Open Medvya to view." (test on payload).
* Mark all read and per-item read state persist across devices.
* Overlay is keyboard accessible and screen-reader friendly.

Summary: Practice access log for owners (F-12): who opened which record and when
Description: /settings/audit: filter by staff member, patient (search), action, date range; shows time, actor, role, action, patient (name visible to the owner after selecting), purpose and outcome (allowed/denied). Export to CSV (watermarked, audited).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Only practice owners/admins can open the log (403 for others, audited).
* Filtering by patient lists every read and write of that patient's record by anyone, with timestamps.
* Denied attempts (e.g. receptionist opening a clinical note) appear with outcome "Denied".
* Exports are audited and watermarked with exporter and time.
* Query p95 < 600 ms for a 30-day range in the pilot volume.

Summary: Tablet-responsive reception views (desk tablet)
Description: Verify and fix registration, calendar, board, queue and settings at 768–1024 px (landscape and portrait): icon rail navigation, 44 px targets, board horizontal scroll, booking panel as a drawer.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Playwright visual checks at 768×1024 and 1024×768 pass for every P1 screen without clipped controls.
* All touch targets ≥ 44 px (automated check).
* Registration and check-in journeys complete on a tablet emulation end-to-end.

Summary: Performance budget and load test for booking and calendar
Description: Load profile for two clinics plus headroom (e.g. 20 concurrent receptionists, 200 bookings/hour, board subscriptions). Measure booking API p95, search p95, board load, calendar first render on throttled 4G. Add the budgets to CI (nightly) with alerts on regression.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Booking API p95 < 300 ms and reads p95 < 300 ms / writes < 600 ms under the profile on staging.
* Calendar first render < 2.5 s on a typical clinic PC profile over 4G throttling.
* Nightly performance job fails and alerts on > 20 % regression.

Summary: P1 security review: threat-model update, ASVS checks, authorisation tests, dependency scan — no open high/critical
Description: Before real demographics enter production: update the threat model for P1 features (public site, registration, booking, messaging, TV display), run ASVS L2 checks, the authorisation matrix tests, IDOR tests on patient and appointment endpoints, DAST against staging, dependency/container scan, and a short external review of security-sensitive code.
Acceptance Criteria:
* No open high or critical findings; mediums have dated remediation tickets.
* IDOR test suite covers every P1 endpoint taking a patient/appointment id.
* Public endpoints (landing, demo, TV display, webhooks) are rate-limited and pass DAST.
* The review report is stored in docs/compliance and linked in R1 release notes.

Summary: Production deployment for the launch country and a production tenant per pilot clinic
Description: Add staging and production parameters to infra/bicep (Defender plans, Storage private endpoint, budgets per environment), a staging slot with smoke test and swap, and a production workflow that needs a manual approval and only accepts tags from main. Deploy production for the launch country from a tag, verify private networking, backups, alerts and the 12 data-protection layers, then create one production tenant per partner clinic with owner accounts (MFA) and feature flags for R1 only.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Staging deploys from a tag on main with a slot swap; production deploys only after a manual approval.
* Production passes the 12-layer checklist (docs/04-security-compliance) with evidence.
* Each partner clinic has its own tenant; owners signed in with MFA and accepted ToS/DPA.
* Only R1 features are enabled by flags; clinical modules are not reachable.
* Synthetic data is never present in production (check).

Summary: Reception training (30 min), one-page desk card and support channel with named contact
Description: 30-minute reception training, in the screen names of MDV-P2-051 (register quick/full from the Register patient button, duplicates, book/reschedule/cancel/no-show, walk-in, check-in, Front desk with its By status and By doctor views, Patients and the Patient record's Details, TV, reminders, what reception cannot see). One-page desk card per country (A4, en + local language). Support channel (WhatsApp/phone) with a named contact and hours; escalation path for security/privacy incidents.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Training delivered to every receptionist at both clinics, attendance recorded.
* During training at the pilot, a trained receptionist quick-registers and checks in a walk-in in under 60 seconds, timed and recorded (moved from MDV-P1-025).
* Desk card printed and available at each desk, covering the top 8 tasks and who to call.
* Support contact, hours and escalation are communicated in writing and listed in the R1 release notes.

Summary: Baseline metrics capture and in-product measurement (check-in time, no-shows, double bookings, reminder delivery)
Description: Capture each clinic's pre-Medvya baseline (no-show rate, check-in time, double-booking incidents) during the first 2 weeks, and instrument: check-in time (arrival → checked in) median, no-show rate, double-booking constraint violations, reminder delivery rate. Owner-facing mini report (full reports P4).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Baseline values per clinic are recorded with method and dates.
* Median check-in time for returning patients is computed from event timestamps and is ≤ 60 s during the measured pilot weeks (exit gate 3) or the gap is reported.
* Metrics contain no PHI and are visible to owners.

Summary: R1 pilot (2 consecutive weeks of real bookings), exit gate review and release notes
Description: Pilot on flags with daily check-ins in week one, then exit gate review with evidence: two consecutive weeks of real bookings without paper fallback at both clinics; double-booking test result; median check-in; reminder delivery ≥ 98 % with failures visible; no open high/critical findings. Publish R1 release notes and known issues; turn J3 front-desk steps green in the journey specs.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Evidence for each of the five exit criteria is attached and confirmed by founder, clinical advisor and one pilot user.
* If the holiday period prevents two consecutive weeks, the gate is formally moved to the first two full January weeks and recorded (no silent slip).
* R1 release notes list P1-01…P1-12 delivered status, known issues and what is not included (clinical notes, Rx, billing, AI, portal).
* Journey J3 front-desk steps (P-01, P-02, P-03) pass in Playwright.

Summary: Safe retries: idempotency keys, request timeouts and bounded retry (merges the proposed P1-047 and P1-048)
Description: On flaky connections a request can reach the server while its answer never reaches the desk, and a retry must not book, check in or register twice. Server chunk: an Idempotency-Key on the booking, check-in and registration POSTs with server-side dedupe (the key is stored with the outcome, scoped to tenant and user; a repeat returns the first outcome). Client chunk: one shared API client with a 15 second timeout and bounded retry with jitter for GETs and keyed POSTs, a clear failed state that keeps the form, and the same key reused across retries of one submission. No patient data is stored in the browser.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A booking, check-in or registration POST that repeats with the same Idempotency-Key creates exactly one record and returns the first outcome (integration test on PostgreSQL, mutation-checked: remove the dedupe and it fails).
* A retry that arrives after another user took the slot gets a conflict, the UI offers other slots, and no duplicate exists.
* The client times out after 15 seconds, shows a retry message and does not clear the form; retries are bounded, jittered and reuse the key.
* The key store holds no patient data, is scoped to tenant and user, and expired keys are removed.

Summary: Service worker for static assets only (app shell loads with no network, no patient data)
Description: Cache the built app files (script, style, fonts) with a service worker so a reload with no network shows the app shell and an offline state instead of a browser error. Static assets only: no API response, no patient data and no identifier is cached or stored. Deferred until pilot interviews say outages are a real problem.
Acceptance Criteria:
* With the network off, reloading a page opened earlier today loads the app shell with the offline state and shows no patient data.
* Browser storage contains no patient identifiers (automated check that fails if one appears).
* A new deploy replaces the cached files (no stale shell after a release).

Summary: Printable day sheet for the desk (no phone numbers or national IDs)
Description: A print view of today's schedule, one page per doctor, in the facility time zone: time, token, first name and age, doctor and a reason code. No phone number and no national or insurance ID. Printing is a read of patient data, so it is audited with who printed it. Deferred until pilot interviews say the desk needs a paper fallback.
