* The sheet excludes phone numbers and national IDs (test).
* An access-log entry records who printed it.

Summary: Encrypted read-only schedule cache for outages (needs an ADR first)
Description: Show today's schedule read-only, labelled "as of <time>", when the network drops, from a per-user encrypted cache that expires after 12 hours and is wiped on sign-out or deactivation. No search; create, edit and cancel stay disabled. Requires an ADR (what may be stored in the browser, key handling) before any code; not to be built unless pilots show the printed day sheet is not enough.
Acceptance Criteria:
* An ADR records what is stored, how it is keyed and why, and is accepted before implementation.
* During an outage the schedule is shown read-only with an "as of" label and create, edit and cancel are disabled.
* The cache is deleted on sign-out, after 12 hours and when the account is deactivated.
* Inspecting the browser store shows only ciphertext, and the test fails if the encryption is removed (mutation check).

Summary: Front-desk fixes from the live walk-through, round 2 (queue displays, cancelled slot, walk-in, schedule, log, reminders, invitations, polish)

Summary: Staff sign-in, sign-up, invitation, location and signed-out screens to the 6 Nov design
Description: The Medvya-owned screens of the 6 Nov sign-in flow in web/clinic, in the designed two-panel frame (brand panel, help, language, region line): Sign in (work email, "This is a shared computer", continue, passkey and single sign-on entry), which starts the Entra sign-in with the email as a login hint; Create account step 1 (practice type, name, city) and step 2 (name, email, mobile, "I'm the doctor" / "I manage the clinic"), which feed the existing sign-up (MDV-P1-004) before the Entra account is made; invitation acceptance (what the role can and cannot see, full name, expiry); choose location (last used first, signed in as, not you); and signed out / session ended. Summary: Entra External ID branding for the email code, MFA set-up and recovery pages

Summary: Practice set-up wizard to the 6 Nov design (practice, hours and services, team, patients, payments and messages, ready)
Description: Rework the onboarding wizard (web/clinic/src/features/onboarding) to the 6 Nov steps with the live booking-page preview: 1 your practice (type, specialties, registration number by country rules), 2 hours and services (prefilled from the specialty, appointment length, services and fees in minor units), 3 your team (invite nurse, doctor, front desk with the "front desk never sees clinical notes" line), 4 your patients (upload a spreadsheet, ask us to move data, or start fresh), 5 payments and messages (connect now or later), and the ready screen (book your first patient). Steps whose back end is not built yet (spreadsheet import, payment connections) record the choice and link to Settings; each such limit is a recorded shortcut.
Acceptance Criteria:

* Given a step, when it is submitted, then the server validates it with the country rules and shows errors under the field, announced to screen readers.
* Given the team step, when an owner invites a front-desk member, then the invitation is sent with the front-desk role and that role cannot open clinical notes (server-side test).
* Every step is keyboard-complete, 44 px targets, axe clean in en, hi and ar; Arabic is right to left.

Summary: Onboarding request at sign-up: choose Clinic or Hospital, give the required documents, submit for Medvya review
Description:
Context: what we decided and why. Medvya is a platform and approves organisations, never individual doctors (ADR-016, owner decision 10 Nov 2026). There is no solo-doctor account: a doctor working alone registers a Clinic and is its owner. Clinic and Hospital are one build; Hospital adds documents. Review by a person is the trust gate, so the request must carry what the reviewer needs.
What to build. Sign-up asks first for the type, Clinic or Hospital, then collects the documents. Clinic: clinic registration certificate, tax registration (GSTIN or TRN), owner's government ID, owner doctor's medical council registration (kept as a document, not verified as a doctor check). Hospital: the same plus hospital registration certificate, authorised signatory letter, IT or security contact, and a signed DPA before approval. Files go to private Blob and are readable only by Medvya operations. Submit moves Draft to Submitted; the applicant sees a status page (Submitted, Needs changes with the reason, Approved, Rejected) and can resubmit. Autosave and resume from MDV-P1-004 stay. An organisation has 1..n locations from the start: the first location is created at onboarding, more are added by the owner later (MDV-P1-070). Hospital HIS and SSO is P7.
Touched: Medvya.Tenancy.Api/OnboardingEndpoints.cs, Medvya.Identity onboarding drafts, Medvya.Tenancy.Infrastructure/PracticeProvisioning.cs (a request is created, the practice is active only on approval), web/clinic/src/features/onboarding (new type and documents steps, status page, domain/onboarding.ts rules, Zod schemas), public site CTAs (Host.Api/PublicSite), packages/i18n en, hi, ar, ERD.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given an applicant starts sign-up, when they have not chosen Clinic or Hospital, then they cannot continue, and only that type's documents are asked.
* Given a required document or field is missing or fails the country rules, when they submit, then the server refuses with errors under the field announced to screen readers.
* Given a Hospital request, when it is submitted without the signed DPA, signatory letter or IT contact, then it is refused.
* Given a Submitted request, when the applicant signs in, then they see its status and, for Needs changes, the reviewer's reason, and can edit and resubmit.
* Given an uploaded file, when it is wrong type or too large, then it is refused; accepted files sit in private Blob and only Medvya operations can open them. (The malware scan of these files moved to MDV-P2-006: it owns the scan seam; until then the shortcut in OrganisationRequests.cs stands.)
* Given the flow, when used in English, Hindi and Arabic, then it is keyboard-complete and axe clean, with Arabic right to left, and no PHI or document content appears in logs, URLs or telemetry.

Summary: Organisation state and set-up-only mode before approval: server-side gate replaces the doctor licence gate
Description:
Context: what we decided and why. Until an organisation is Approved it may only set itself up: profile, hours, rooms, adding staff. No patient registration, booking, check-in, notes or signing, so no patient data exists before Medvya has reviewed the organisation. The Medvya licence gate (LicenceRules) is retired by ADR-016 and this organisation gate takes its place.
What to build. Add the organisation state (Draft, Submitted, NeedsChanges, Approved, Rejected, Suspended) to the tenant and check it in IStaffAccess for every capability, replacing LicenceRules.Apply and the licencePending session flag. While not Approved the server refuses patient, booking, check-in, note, prescription and signing capabilities; settings and staff invitations work. Suspended refuses new registration, booking and signing but keeps existing records readable for care. The shell shows a plain notice per state. The state belongs to the organisation and applies to all its locations (1..n from the start, MDV-P1-070).
Touched: Medvya.Tenancy.Domain (state on the tenant, Practice.cs), Medvya.Tenancy.Application/IStaffAccess.cs and Infrastructure/StaffAccess.cs, Host.Api/Auth/SessionControl.cs, the capability policies in Medvya.Tenancy.Api/StaffPolicies.cs, web/clinic session domain and App.tsx banner, i18n, ERD, a row-level-security-safe read of the state.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given an organisation that is not Approved, when any user calls a patient, booking, check-in, note, prescription or signing endpoint, then the API refuses with 403 and the attempt is audited.
* Given a not-Approved organisation, when the owner edits profile, hours or rooms or invites staff, then it works.
* Given the organisation becomes Approved, when the same calls are made, then they work as before.
* Given an organisation is Suspended, when staff open an existing record, then it is readable and new registration, booking and signing are refused.
* Given each state, when the shell loads, then a plain notice is shown in English and Arabic and the state is never conveyed by colour alone.

Summary: Operations approval queue in the platform console (Host.Platform) and interim documented API: approve, ask for changes, reject, suspend
Description:
Context: what we decided and why. The pilot cannot wait for the full console (MDV-P5-044, weeks 26 to 29). The owner decided a simple approval queue is built now in the platform console, approved by a configured Medvya operations user; until the console runs on Azure, a documented API call does the same and stays.
What to build. An organisation-approval capability replaces OperationsPolicies.LicenceReview and the Operations:LicenceReviewers id list. Operations endpoints (reason of 5 to 500 characters, audited, applicant emailed a plain reason for changes, rejection or suspension) list Submitted requests and apply approve, ask for changes, reject and suspend. A simple queue page in web/platform-admin calls them. The review reads only the control-plane request and documents through a narrow reviewed read path (ADR-014), never clinic patient data. Document the API call in docs/runbooks.
Touched: Medvya.Tenancy.Api/DoctorEndpoints.cs (remove licence verify and reject routes and OperationsPolicies), Medvya.Tenancy.Infrastructure/LicenceReview.cs and ILicenceReview (remove), Host.Platform and Medvya.Platform (queue read path and page), web/platform-admin, a configured operations user list, docs/runbooks.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a user without the organisation-approval capability, when they call the endpoints or open the queue, then they get 403.
* Given a Submitted request, when a configured operations user approves, asks for changes, rejects or suspends with a reason, then the state changes, the audit names the operator, and the applicant is emailed the reason.
* Given a Hospital request without a signed DPA, when approval is attempted, then it is refused (design 10 Nov 2026).
* Given an action without a reason, when it is sent, then it is rejected.
* Given any queue or approval endpoint, when it returns data, then it holds no patient field and logs none (architecture test).
* Given the console is not deployed, when an operator follows the runbook, then the documented API call approves a request.

Summary: Owner attests each doctor's licence (number, authority, expiry), printed on prescriptions; retire Medvya licence verification
Description:
Context: what we decided and why. What happens inside an approved organisation is its own responsibility. Medvya does not check doctors; the owner enters the licence and attests it, accepting liability in the terms (MDV-P1-067). The owner accepted that there is no independent check, including for controlled drugs.
What to build. The licence record (number, authority, expiry) is required and entered by the owner for each doctor, and for the owner-doctor in the wizard, with an attestation checkbox. The audit (append-only) stores the owner, time and values. Remove the Verified, Pending and Rejected states, the verification step in the Add doctor wizard, ILicenceReview and the "Verification pending" notice; recording, signing and prescribing no longer depend on VerifiedAt. The doctor list shows "Attested by {owner} on {date}". The licence number and authority are kept on DoctorLicence for the prescription print to read; printing them is a criterion of MDV-P2-017, which owns the print. Expiry reminders stay; an expired licence warns the owner and doctor and asks the owner to re-attest (does not block; open question).
Touched: Medvya.Tenancy.Infrastructure/Doctors.cs, Application/IDoctors.cs, Domain/Practice.cs (DoctorLicence, LicenceStatus, LicenceRules), PracticeProvisioning.cs, Host.Api/Auth/SessionControl.cs, web/clinic doctors and onboarding features, App.tsx LicenceNotice, the prescription print, i18n, ERD.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given an owner adds a doctor, when licence number, authority, expiry or the attestation is missing, then the doctor cannot be added.
* Given a doctor was added, when anyone views the doctor list, then it shows who attested and when, and the audit holds the values.
* Given an approved organisation, when a doctor with an attested licence records, signs or prescribes, then it is allowed with no Medvya check.
* Given a licence nears or passes expiry, when the reminder runs, then the owner is told to re-attest and signing is not blocked.
* The licence gate tests are replaced by attestation tests and no endpoint still reads VerifiedAt.

Summary: Retire solo-doctor naming: Role.SoloDoctor, session flags, copy and docs
Description:
Context: what we decided and why. There is no individual account; a one-doctor practice is a clinic whose owner is a doctor. Names and copy must say so and must not say Medvya verifies licences.
What to build. Rename or retire Role.SoloDoctor (RoleMatrix.cs, the web Role type, role matrix tests, about 52 files), keeping the owner-doctor as an owner who is a doctor. Remove licencePending from the session and shell (SessionControl.cs, session.ts, App.tsx LicenceNotice). Rewrite copy that says Medvya verifies licences (onboarding.licence.notice, doctors.intro, invite.licence, inviteForm.licence, onboarding.team.doctors, staff.doctorNotice) in en, hi and ar. A change to a stored role value ships with a forward-only migration.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the codebase, when searched for SoloDoctor or "solo doctor" in user-visible text, then nothing remains.
* Given an existing owner-doctor, when they sign in after the change, then access is unchanged.
* Given copy in en, hi and ar, when read, then it says the owner attests licences and Medvya approves the organisation.
* Given the role matrix tests, when run, then they pass; the ERD is regenerated if a table or column changes.

Summary: Terms of Service and DPA update: the organisation is responsible for the licences it attests
Description:
Context: what we decided and why. Medvya approves the organisation only. A false licence is the organisation's liability, so the terms and DPA must say so in plain words, and a Hospital signs the DPA before approval.
What to build. New terms and DPA version stating that Medvya does not verify individual doctors, that the owner is responsible for who they add and for attesting each licence including the effect of a false attestation, and that Medvya may suspend an organisation. Bump TermsPolicy (ITermsAcceptance.cs) so owners re-accept through the existing terms gate. The attestation step shows a short reminder. Counsel reviews the document lists too. Counsel's written sign-off of this wording before use with a real pilot clinic is an acceptance criterion of MDV-P1-044, which owns the legal review; until it exists the draft marker blocks deploys beyond dev.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the new version, when an owner signs in, then they must accept it before booking or messaging (existing gate).
* Given the attestation step, when shown, then it carries the plain-language reminder in en, hi and ar.

Summary: Migrate existing tenants to Approved and their doctor licences to owner-attested
Description:
Context: what we decided and why. Dev and pilot tenants exist already and must keep working when the gate arrives.
What to build. A forward-only migration setting every existing tenant to Approved with an audit entry naming the migration, and marking existing doctor licences attested by the tenant's owner as of migration time (the owner re-confirms on next sign-in). Regenerate the ERD (python3 -I tools/erd/generate.py) in the same change. Touched: Medvya.Tenancy.Infrastructure migrations and Persistence, docs/03-architecture/erd.md.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given an existing tenant, when the migration runs, then it is Approved and keeps working with no new step.
* Given a doctor licence that was Verified, Pending or Rejected, when the migration runs, then it shows owner-attested and the audit names the migration.
* Given the migration, when run twice or on an empty database, then it is safe.

Summary: Starter plan cap: 1 doctor and 2 staff enforced server-side
Description:
Context: what we decided and why. Subscriptions will have seats, but plans are built in P5. Until then every organisation gets one hard-coded starter plan so growth is bounded and the upgrade conversation exists: 1 doctor plus 2 other staff (any mix of nurse, receptionist, admin; the owner-doctor is the doctor), counted per organisation in total across all its locations (MDV-P1-070); a bigger chain needs a bigger plan (MDV-P5-042). Patients are not capped. Self-service upgrade comes with MDV-P5-042 and MDV-P5-016; the owner is responsible for what they choose then.
What to build. One place (a small plan class with a shortcut: comment, hard-coded plan, replaced by entitlements when MDV-P5-042 lands) counts active and invited doctors and other staff per organisation (tenant), in total across its locations, never per location. Adding a doctor, adding staff and sending an invitation are refused server-side beyond the cap with the message "Your plan allows 1 doctor and 2 staff; contact Medvya to upgrade". The web shows the same message. Offboarded members and revoked invitations free their seat. A race of parallel invitations cannot exceed the cap.
Touched: Medvya.Tenancy.Infrastructure/Doctors.cs, Invitations.cs, Medvya.Identity.Api/StaffEndpoints.cs, Medvya.Tenancy.Api settings endpoints, web/clinic staff and doctors features, i18n en, hi, ar.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a clinic with its owner-doctor and 2 other staff, when the owner adds a third staff member or invites one, then the server refuses with "Your plan allows 1 doctor and 2 staff; contact Medvya to upgrade".
* Given a clinic with 1 doctor, when the owner adds a second doctor, then it is refused with the same message.
* Given a staff member is offboarded or an invitation is revoked, when the owner adds another, then it is allowed.
* Given an organisation with several locations, when staff are added at different locations, then they count together against the one cap.
* Given any number of patients, when patients are registered, then no cap applies.
* Given parallel add or invite calls, when they race, then the cap still holds (integration test).

Summary: Add a location to an organisation (Settings, Locations): certificate and tax record, same country, audited
Description:
Context: what we decided and why. One organisation, many locations, like a hospital group with branches in several cities. The organisation is approved once; the owner adds branches inside it with no new Medvya approval, and uploading the branch's registration certificate and tax number is a record the owner is responsible for (same principle as attesting a doctor). The first location is created at onboarding. Overlap: MDV-P7-003 (organisation, facilities and departments administration) is the hospital-scale version; this clinic-level ticket is built first and P7-003 extends it with departments.
What to build. Settings, Locations (exists from MDV-P1-005) gains Add location: name, address, time zone, registration certificate (private Blob) and tax number (GSTIN or TRN format-checked). The location's country must equal the organisation's country (refused otherwise, data stays in country, ADR-003). The audit log records who added it and when. The existing location picker lists the new location. Hours, rooms and holidays are set per location as today. The owner may add a location in any set-up state (Draft, Submitted, NeedsChanges, Approved), because it is set-up work that holds no patient data (ADR-016); a Suspended organisation is refused. Only its owner or admin with practice configuration may add one.
Touched: Medvya.Tenancy.Infrastructure/FacilityDirectory.cs and PracticeSettings.cs, Medvya.Tenancy.Api/SettingsEndpoints.cs, Facility domain (certificate name, tax number), web/clinic settings locations tab, i18n en, hi, ar, ERD.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given an organisation in any set-up state (not Suspended), when its owner adds a location with name, address, time zone, certificate and tax number, then it is created, appears in the location picker, and the audit names the owner and time.
* Given a location in another country than the organisation, when it is submitted, then the server refuses it.
* Given a missing certificate, a missing or malformed tax number or time zone, when submitted, then the server refuses with errors under the field announced to screen readers.
* Given a user without practice configuration, or a Suspended organisation, when they call the endpoint, then 403.
* Given the new location, when the owner sets hours and rooms, then they apply to that location only (hours and rooms are per location).

Summary: Staff and doctors across locations: a membership covers one or more locations; schedule, board and queue stay per location
Description:
Context: what we decided and why. People and the plan belong to the organisation, so one doctor or nurse can work at several branches. The plan cap counts them once (MDV-P1-069). Overlap: MDV-P7-003 and MDV-P7-002 (facility scope for hospital roles) extend this for hospital departments later.
What to build. A membership gets a set of locations within the organisation (today one facility; MDV-P1-009 scoped it). The owner assigns locations when adding or editing staff and doctors, and invitations carry them. The facility picker lists only the member's locations. Schedule, reception board and queue stay per location; a doctor with two locations has one schedule template per location. Reassigning or walking a patient between doctors of different locations is out of scope. Offboarding removes access at every location at once.
Touched: Medvya.Tenancy.Infrastructure/StaffAccess.cs, Invitations.cs, Doctors.cs, membership and facility scope in Medvya.Tenancy, Medvya.Identity.Api/StaffEndpoints.cs, Medvya.Scheduling (SchedulingAccess.cs, schedule, board, queue by location), web/clinic staff, doctors and facility picker, i18n, ERD.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given an owner edits a staff member, when they pick two locations, then the member can switch between them in the picker and sees only those.
* Given a member without a location, when they call an endpoint for that location, then 403 (server-side).
* Given a doctor at two locations, when the reception board or queue opens at one location, then it shows only that location's visits.
* Given a member is offboarded, when it is saved, then access ends at every location immediately.
* Given the starter plan, when the same person is at two locations, then they count once.

Summary: Shared patient record across an organisation's locations: one MRN and one chart, search across locations, location in the access log
Description:
Context: what we decided and why. In a chain a patient who visits Surat and then Mumbai is one person with one chart. Patients are one shared record across the organisation: one MRN and one chart, opened by staff at any location under the existing access, care-relationship and audit rules. Tenant isolation stays on the organisation: the EF filter and row-level security use the tenant, not the facility. Overlap: MDV-P7-002 and MDV-P7-003 (record authority per facility) deal with hospital groups; this is the clinic-level version, built first.
What to build. Check what assumes patient-per-facility and change it: Patient.FacilityId stays as where the patient was registered; PatientRegistry allocates the MRN with NextMrnAsync(tenantId, facilityId) and requires registration at the active facility, searches by facility (FacilityId filter around line 140) and checks duplicates by facility: move the MRN sequence, search and duplicate scope to the organisation. PatientDirectory.cs and PatientMerges.cs filter pairs by FacilityId (merge and review queues): scope them to the organisation. RegistrationCareRelationship.cs and AccessRequestEndpoints.cs and the care-relationship rules must still hold for staff at another location. Scheduling, Encounters and Billing references by patient stay valid. The access log shows the location where the record was read (role and facility at event time exist). Existing MRNs stay unique; migration handles two facilities of one tenant that issued the same MRN (collision plan in the ticket). Out of scope: reassigning or walking in a patient between doctors of different locations.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a patient registered at location A, when staff at location B of the same organisation search by name, MRN or phone, then the patient is found and opens as one chart with one MRN.
* Given a new registration at location B, when the name and date of birth match a patient at location A, then the duplicate warning shows that patient.
* Given staff at location B open the record, when the access log is read, then the entry shows location B.
* Given staff from another organisation, when they search or open the record, then it is refused by both the EF filter and row-level security.
* Given a member not scoped to location B, when they search there, then they cannot reach it (MDV-P1-071).
* Given existing data with the same MRN at two facilities of one tenant, when the migration runs, then every MRN is unique per organisation and nothing is lost.

Summary: Clinical advisor walks the six journeys and signs off (moved from MDV-P0-023)
Description: A person's task, moved out of MDV-P0-023 (it is P0 exit criterion 1) so the design-system epic could close. Decision 12 Nov 2026 (docs/releases/r0.md): the founder approves R0, and the clinician walk-through becomes the pilot entry check, done by the pilot clinic's own doctor; nothing clinical reaches a patient before it. Walk that doctor through J1–J6: the built steps on the Azure India dev environment, the rest on the storyboard. Record sign-off, or change requests with owners, per journey. Do it before the R1 pilot (MDV-P1-042) with at least one sprint left to build what the advisor asks for in the pilot clinic flow.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Clinical advisor sign-off (or a list of requested changes with owners) for each of J1–J6 is recorded in docs/02-design/journeys.md with the date and the advisor's role.
* Any change requested by the advisor is raised as a ticket in the relevant phase; changes to the pilot clinic flow are scheduled before MDV-P1-042.
* The P0 exit gate item "Clinical advisor walks all six journeys and signs off" is evidenced.

Summary: Keep Azure logs flowing all day: PostgreSQL audit and connection logs must not exhaust the Log Analytics daily cap
Description: Found 13 Nov 2026 while seeding the Azure dev load practice (MDV-P1-037). The dev workspace `log-medvya-dev-*` has a 0.2 GB daily cap and is OverQuota most days, so every log after the cap (App Insights traces and requests, Container Apps job logs, alerts that read them) is dropped until the 12:00 UTC reset. Ingestion: about 224 MB on 11 Nov and 354 MB on 12 Nov in AzureDiagnostics alone, almost all `PostgreSQLLogs`: on 12 Nov about 110k pgaudit SESSION READ lines, 86k WRITE, 8k DDL and 14k connection/disconnection lines. The server parameter `pgaudit.log` reads `write, ddl, role` (read was turned off on 7 Nov), so find what still enables READ (a role- or database-level `pgaudit.log` setting, or a session setting) and remove it. Then keep PostgreSQL diagnostics from starving the application: send only the categories needed (or route PostgreSQL logs to their own table, plan or storage), and size the cap so a normal day plus a seed or load run stays under it. Two WRITE audit lines on 12 Nov held literal VALUES: check they carry no patient values (dev is synthetic, but the pilot will not be).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a normal day on Azure dev, when the Usage table is read, then ingestion stays under the daily cap and the workspace is never OverQuota.
* Given a database session as the app role, when it runs a SELECT, then no pgaudit READ line is written.
* Given a Container Apps job run (db migrate or seed) at any hour, when it finishes, then its console log is in Log Analytics.
* Given pgaudit WRITE lines, when they are sampled, then none holds a parameter value (log_parameter off and no literal patient values).

Summary: Design rules: write PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md from the audit blueprint and amend AGENTS.md section 4
Labels: phase-P1 design-system documentation ux epic-ux-programme track-design wave-d0
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D0. This is audit backlog UX-35 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: No screen. Readers: every developer and AI agent that writes front-end code; the founder as owner of the rules.
Findings and reviewers: F-45, F-19, F-20, F-21 · reviewers B-27, C-04, C-05, C-11 · arbitration rulings 2, 5, 6 and 8.
Rationale: There is no written rule for density, page headers, card sizes, how many primary buttons a view may have, or which shared component a pattern must use. That is why three patient headers, 20 view switches and about 350 size patches exist. Everything else in track D builds on these rules, so they are written first.
Proposed UX behaviour: Two short files at the repository root. PRODUCT.md: who uses Medvya (doctor, nurse, receptionist, owner, practice admin), what each must be able to do all day, the eight design principles of blueprint section 1, the device strategy of section 11 and the phone rule of ruling 5. DESIGN.md: the layout grid and widths (section 2), navigation model (3), the two densities (4), spacing, type, radius and elevation (5), tone meanings (6), the component list with states (7), pinned chrome rules (10), motion rules with the never list (12), the accessibility targets by WCAG 2.2 criterion (13) and the guardrails (14). Both files carry the non-negotiables of the epic and the list headed Do not change without clinical validation. AGENTS.md section 4 is amended in the same change for the rules that change: 44 px is the library default and a feature never patches a control height; comfortable density is mandatory for every control that changes state, every row that picks a patient, medicine lines and any device with a coarse pointer; compact 36 px rows are allowed only on the audit log, formulary, order sets and staff tables; typed clinical text is 16 px; 1024 px is a named layout tier and sm:grid-cols is not used for column changes; the shared components that a feature must use once they exist, each with the ticket that builds it; one primary button per view; pinned chrome takes at most 30 % of the height and nothing focusable sits under it; the motion tokens and the never list; a new shared component is not done until it is in the /__ui gallery in English and Arabic. docs/02-design/tokens.md gets one line at the top saying DESIGN.md describes the build and wins where they differ.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/08-design-system-blueprint.md, all sections; docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/medvya-workspace-concept.html as the picture of the target; docs/product-ux-audit/12-prototype-guide.md (What the concept deliberately does not settle).
Components and tokens affected: None built here. Names every component and token group that waves D1 to D3 build.
Front end and back end split: Docs only. No front-end or back-end code.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None. This is the first ticket of track D; every other track D ticket depends on it through the lint and ratchet ticket of the same wave.
Clinical sign-off: Not required to write the rules. The allergy presentation and the strip contents are recorded as proposals that wait for questions 3 and 4 of docs/product-ux-audit/11-pilot-doctor-validation-plan.md.
Effort and regression risk: S · Low. Docs only; the risk is writing a rule the code cannot yet meet, so each such rule names the ticket that makes it true.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Any change to packages/ui or to a screen. (2) The lint rules and the CI count (the next ticket of this wave). (3) A palette or typeface change, or a second component library: both are forbidden by the rules being written.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the repository root, when PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md are opened, then each section of blueprint sections 1 to 14 is present in one of them and docs/README.md and AGENTS.md section 8 link to both
* Given DESIGN.md, when the density, phone, navigation rail and owner page rules are read, then they match arbitration rulings 2, 5, 8 and 7 word for word in meaning and name the four tables that may be compact
* Given AGENTS.md section 4, when it is read after this change, then it states the 44 px library default, the two densities, 16 px typed clinical text, the 1024 tier, the shared components to use and the motion rules, and each rule the code does not yet meet names the ticket that makes it true
* Given DESIGN.md, when the list headed Do not change without clinical validation is read, then it holds every item of blueprint section 14 and of the executive verdict, and the epic's seven non-negotiables
* Given DESIGN.md, when the accessibility section is read, then it lists the WCAG 2.2 criteria of blueprint section 13 as design requirements and makes no claim of conformance
* Given the changed Markdown files, when python3 -I tools/check-links/check.py runs, then it reports 0 broken links

Summary: Guardrails: lint rules and a CI count that may only fall, so shared patterns stop drifting
Labels: phase-P1 design-system ci frontend epic-ux-programme track-design wave-d0
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D0. This is audit backlog UX-35 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: No screen. Runs in pnpm -r lint and in the PR workflow.
Findings and reviewers: F-19, F-20, F-21, F-45 · reviewers C-01, C-03, C-04, C-11, C-16 · reviewer C rebuttal section 6.
Rationale: A rule that is only written drifts again. The house already enforces tables by lint; the same is needed for control heights, raw colours, font sizes, column breakpoints, page titles and locally rebuilt Message, Field, Card and Empty components.
Proposed UX behaviour: A small script (tools/check-ui-drift, run as pnpm check:ui-drift and in the PR workflow's web job) counts, in web/clinic/src/features and web/platform-admin/src: min-h-11 or h-11 on Input, SelectTrigger, Textarea and Button; arbitrary font sizes (text-[...]) outside an allow-list for the queue display and print; raw hex colours in class names (bg-[#...], text-[#...], border-[#...]), also in packages/ui; sm:grid-cols-*; raw h1 elements in features; the string border bg-card in features; and local components named Message, Field, Card or Empty in features/*/components. Today's numbers are committed as the baseline (about 350 height patches, 103 raw hex in packages/ui, 30 sm:grid-cols, 37 raw h1, 97 inline cards, and 10, 5, 2 and 2 local components). A pull request fails when any count rises; a count may only fall, and the baseline is lowered in the pull request that lowers it. When a count reaches zero, the ticket that got it there turns the matching oxlint rule to error and removes the count. The script has a self-test in the style of tools/check-links.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/08-design-system-blueprint.md section 14.
Components and tokens affected: No component. Adds one tool, one package.json script, one workflow step and the baseline file.
Front end and back end split: Tooling only.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the design-rules ticket of this wave (the rules being enforced must be written first).
Clinical sign-off: Not required.
Effort and regression risk: S · Low. It adds a guard and weakens none; no existing lint rule or threshold changes.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Fixing any of the counted places: each count falls in the ticket that owns the pattern. (2) The browser test that the patient strip stays visible (in the pinned-strip screen ticket). (3) Repointing the contrast test to the tone tokens (in the tone-token ticket).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the committed baseline, when a pull request adds one more local Message component or one more h-11 patch in a feature, then pnpm check:ui-drift exits 1 and names the file
* Given a pull request that removes patches, when the baseline in the same pull request is lowered to the new number, then the check passes and the old number can no longer be reached
* Given the script, when it runs with --self-test, then a sample with one extra hit fails and a sample at the baseline passes
* Given a pull request that touches web/, packages/ or the tool, when the PR workflow runs, then the count step runs in the web job and a failure blocks the merge
* Given web/clinic/.oxlintrc.json and the workflow, when this change is compared with main, then no existing rule, test or threshold is removed or lowered
* Given the baseline file, when the counts are re-measured on main at merge time, then each number equals the measured number

Summary: Library defaults: 44 px Input, Select and Textarea, a required Table label, and 44 px hit areas for Switch

Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D1 (a, foundations). This is audit backlog UX-13 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Every form and table, all roles; shown first in /__ui. The platform console inherits it.
Findings and reviewers: F-20, F-33, F-44, F-24 (labels) · reviewers C-01, C-13, C-22, B-20, A-17.
Rationale: The library default (36 px) contradicts the house 44 px rule, so 164 call sites patch it and a missed patch gives a small control (seen in the platform console). Four scrollable tables have no label, so keyboard users cannot name or scroll them. Switches are 32 by 18 px. This is one of the three system changes the arbitration allows before the pilot.
Proposed UX behaviour: In packages/ui: Input, SelectTrigger and Textarea default to 44 px; select options are 44 px on a coarse pointer; Table's label prop becomes required in TypeScript, and the four tables without one (day sheet, merge review, growth card, timeline) get a translated label in the same change; Switch keeps its track size and gains a 44 by 44 px hit area by padding. A ChoiceRow helper makes the whole row the target of a native radio or checkbox. The gallery shows each control at default size with its measured height, in English and Arabic. The call-site patches stay in place in this ticket (they are now redundant, not wrong) and are deleted by the codemod ticket that follows.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/08-design-system-blueprint.md section 4 (Density) and section 7 (Before the pilot).
Components and tokens affected: input.tsx, select.tsx, textarea.tsx, table.tsx, switch.tsx; new ChoiceRow; gallery entries. No token change.
Front end and back end split: Front end only (packages/ui, four table labels with i18n keys in en, hi and ar).
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the lint and ratchet ticket (D0). File ownership in wave D1a: this ticket owns the five control files above and nothing in tokens or styles.css.
Clinical sign-off: Not required. The device check (question 20 of the validation plan) confirms mouse or touch at the pilot desk; the default is safe for both.
Effort and regression risk: S · Low. Visible change only where a control was never patched.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Deleting the call-site patches (the codemod ticket, which merges alone). (2) Applying ChoiceRow to the 26 native radios and checkboxes in features, and making name-link rows one target (second part of the codemod ticket). (3) Compact density (after the pilot, with the table ticket).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the /__ui gallery, when Input, Select trigger and Textarea render with no class added, then each is at least 44 px tall in English and in Arabic
* Given the screens that already patched their controls to 44 px, when screenshots before and after are compared, then no control changed size
* Given the call sites that had no patch, when the change is reviewed, then the pull request lists each one and each now measures 44 px, including the platform console invite form
* Given any Table in web/clinic or web/platform-admin, when it is used without a label, then TypeScript fails the build, and the four tables that lacked one announce a translated label to a screen reader
* Given a Switch on a 1024 px touch viewport, when its hit area is measured, then it is at least 44 by 44 px and the visible track is unchanged
* Given the gallery page in English and Arabic, when axe runs, then there is no violation and the controls mirror in right-to-left

Summary: Tokens: nine type sizes, the spacing scale, page and panel widths, the 1024 tier, density and two motion values

Rationale: The app renders 12 font sizes against a documented scale of 7, has no maximum page width, and uses four different side-panel widths. The components of waves D1b and D1c need named values to build on, or each will invent its own again.
Proposed UX behaviour: Add to packages/tokens (and through the generator to tokens.css, theme.ts and the Tailwind theme in packages/ui/src/styles.css): the nine type tokens of blueprint section 5 (display, title, heading, subheading, body, body-large, label, caption, mono) with size, line height and weight, and tabular numerals as a utility; the spacing scale 2 to 64; widths (page maximum 1600, reading 1152 and about 72 characters, form 768, side panel 320 and 360 for the consultation chart panel); layout sizes (top bar 48 and 56, rail 72, sidebar 232, header row 44, gutters 16, 24 and 32); radius 6, 10, 12 and full; the two elevations; density (control 44 and 36, row 48 and 36); the breakpoint named wide at 1024 beside 360, 768, 1280 and 1600; and two motion tokens, ease-out cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) and a fast duration of 150 ms. Existing utilities keep working; no feature file changes.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/08-design-system-blueprint.md sections 2, 4, 5 and 12.
Components and tokens affected: packages/tokens/src/tokens.json, generate.mjs output (tokens.css, theme.ts), packages/ui/src/styles.css. Gallery specimen page.
Front end and back end split: Front end only (tokens and styles).

Waves D1b and D1c do not edit either file.

Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Applying the type tokens to features, body weight 500 and the page maximum width (the after-pilot ticket that applies them). (2) Tone tokens (the next ticket). (3) Any palette or typeface change.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given packages/tokens, when the generator runs, then the nine type tokens, the spacing scale, the widths, the density values, the wide breakpoint and the two motion tokens are in tokens.css and theme.ts and usable as Tailwind utilities
* Given the 20 most-used screens, when they are captured before and after, then no pixel differs
* Given mobile/ and packages/ui-native, when their type check and tests run, then they pass with the extended tokens
* Given /__ui, when the type and spacing specimen is opened in English and Arabic, then each token is shown with its name and measured size, Arabic uses Noto Sans Arabic, and axe finds no violation

Persona and route: No screen changes. Every status chip, alert and banner in every role, through the library.
Findings and reviewers: F-20, F-19 · reviewers C-03, C-21. Part 1 of 3 of audit backlog UX-21 (part 2 builds Chip, Tag and Banner; part 3 replaces the local chips in features).
Rationale: Tokens style the chrome and 103 raw hex colours style the meaning. Dark and high-contrast themes cannot be built on literals, web and native can drift, and a palette fix means editing look tables by hand.
Proposed UX behaviour: Add a tone layer to the tokens: danger, warning, success, info, brand, ai and neutral, each with a foreground, background and border value taken from the colours used today. Repoint the look tables in packages/ui/src/primitives.tsx to the tones, with no visual change. The contrast test in packages/ui reads the tone tokens, so a tone that fails 4.5:1 for text or 3:1 for a border fails the build. The names match the Tone type already used in packages/ui-native. Delete the dead dark: variants in tabs.tsx and switch.tsx. The raw-hex count in the ratchet for packages/ui falls to zero and its lint rule turns to error.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/08-design-system-blueprint.md section 6 (tone table and rules).
Components and tokens affected: tokens.json (tone layer), styles.css, primitives.tsx, primitives.test.tsx (contrast), tabs.tsx and switch.tsx (dead classes).
Front end and back end split: Front end only.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the type and spacing token ticket (same two files; that one merges first). The clinical components of wave D1b rebase on this.
Clinical sign-off: Review only: the looks must be unchanged. The allergy look itself is decided in part 2 (question 4 of the validation plan).
Effort and regression risk: M · Low, if the comparison is exact. Any difference is a mapping error.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) A new allergy presentation (part 2, needs clinical sign-off). (2) Dark and high-contrast themes (MDV-P5-023, which must not start before this ticket). (3) Any change to the palette.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the tokens, when the tone layer is read, then danger, warning, success, info, brand, ai and neutral each have a text, background and border value and a written meaning
* Given packages/ui/src, when it is searched for hex colours in class names or style objects, then there is none, the ratchet count is zero and the lint rule is an error
* Given the /__ui gallery, when every status primitive is captured before and after in English and Arabic, then no pixel differs
* Given the contrast test, when a tone's text colour is changed to one that gives less than 4.5:1, then the test fails
* Given every primitive that uses a tone, when it renders, then it carries a text label, and an icon where one existed before
* Given packages/ui and packages/ui-native, when the tone names are compared, then they are the same seven

Findings and reviewers: F-02, F-19 · reviewers A-01, B-03, B-08, C-02. Part 1 of 3 of audit backlog UX-03 (part 2 is the layout footer and save status; part 3 puts them on the screens).
Rationale: Three patient headers exist and the allergy looks different in each: a red pill on the chart, plain text in the consultation. The most safety-relevant element needs one form before it is pinned anywhere, or the pin hard-codes the difference.
Proposed UX behaviour: One PatientBanner in packages/ui with three variants. full: the chart header as today (avatar, name, age and sex, MRN in the mono face, date of birth, life stage, allergy block, consent, care team where recorded). strip: one row at 1024 px and wider and two rows at most below, 56 px, with name, age and sex, MRN, date of birth, the allergy block in words, consent, and slots for token and room; it wraps and never clips or shows an ellipsis alone. desk: name, age and sex, masked MRN, date of birth and no clinical data at all. The allergy block has one look everywhere: recorded allergies as a solid danger block with an icon and the words (for example Allergy: Penicillin (rash)); with more than two, the first two in words and a count that opens the full list; Allergies not recorded as a warning block with its own words; No known allergies as neutral text with a tick. Unknown is never shown as none. The strip exposes a pinned option and un-pins itself at 400 % zoom. The gallery shows every variant with one, three and five allergies, a long name, Arabic right-to-left and 375 px.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/medvya-workspace-concept.html, doctor view, audit note 2; screenshots docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/screenshots/doctor-1440.png, doctor-1024.png, doctor-768.png and doctor-375.png (the 375 one shows the clipping this ticket must not repeat); blueprint sections 6, 7 and 10.

Front end and back end split: Front end only. No API change: the component takes props the screens already have.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the D1a tickets for control defaults, type tokens and tone tokens. File ownership in wave D1b: this ticket owns patient-banner.tsx and its test and gallery section only.
Clinical sign-off: Required before merge: questions 3 (what the strip shows; how five allergies show) and 4 (one look for the allergy, for not recorded and for no known allergies) of docs/product-ux-audit/11-pilot-doctor-validation-plan.md. The agreement is written on the issue with a date.
Effort and regression risk: M · Low in this ticket (no screen uses it yet). The allergy wording and the unknown, none and not recorded distinction must not change: the component only presents what the screens pass in.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Using it on any screen (the screen ticket in wave D2). (2) Changing allergy rules, wording or data. (3) The queue button in the strip (the queue rail ticket).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given /__ui, when the PatientBanner section is opened, then full, strip and desk render from the same component and the desk variant contains no allergy, diagnosis, medicine or vitals text

* Given the allergy block, when it is viewed in greyscale and read by a screen reader, then the word Allergy and the substance are present as text
* Given the gallery in English and Arabic, when axe runs on every variant, then there is no violation and the layout mirrors in right-to-left
* Given the strip with the pinned option at 400 % zoom, when the page scrolls, then the strip scrolls with the content
* Given this ticket's issue, when it is closed, then it holds the pilot doctor's dated agreement on the strip contents and the allergy look

Rationale: The floating Review and sign bar covers fields and hid 2 of 45 tab stops (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 at risk). The save message is a fixed sentence that cannot say Not saved.

It is a polite live region, changes by an opacity swap of 150 ms (instant under reduced motion), has no tick animation and no toast, and never shows Saved unless told the server answered.

Clinical sign-off: Not required for the components. The sign bar's behaviour on the consultation is validated with the screen ticket.
Effort and regression risk: S · Low.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Wiring to the note controller (audit backlog UX-04, track S). (2) Putting the footer on the consultation (the screen ticket in wave D2). (3) Any change to what Sign or Authorise do.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a long page in the gallery with the footer, when the last field is scrolled to, then the whole field is visible above the footer
* Given the gallery page, when every control is reached with Tab, then each focused element is fully inside the visible area and none is under the footer
* Given SaveStatus, when it is set to saving, saved at 10:42 and failed, then it reads Saving…, Saved 10:42 and Not saved. Trying again., and it cannot render Saved without a time
* Given a screen reader and reduced motion, when the state changes, then the new text is announced once and swaps with no movement
* Given 400 % zoom, when the page scrolls, then the footer scrolls with the content
* Given the gallery in English and Arabic, when axe runs, then there is no violation

Summary: A free-text medicine needs a reason before authorising when the patient has, or may have, an allergy
Labels: phase-P1 prescribing allergies safety clinical-safety epic-ux-programme track-safety wave-s1 needs-clinical-sign-off
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S1. This is audit backlog UX-01 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: /consult/:id, Prescription, Safety checks and Authorise · doctor.
Findings and reviewers: F-01 · reviewer A-02 (P0 safety; pilot blocker for prescribing, agreed by all three reviewers).
Rationale: Augmentin 625 Duo, a penicillin-class brand, was typed as free text for a patient with a recorded penicillin allergy and authorised as RX-CAEE099F with No alerts from the checks that could run. The print shows Allergies: Penicillin directly above the medicine. Indian outpatient prescribing is largely by brand and the formulary holds 23 generics and no brands, so free text is likely on day one.
Proposed UX behaviour: When a prescription line is free text and the patient has any recorded allergy, or allergies are not recorded, Safety checks raises the existing severe check-could-not-run alert for that line, naming every recorded allergy in words: Not checked against: Penicillin. Augmentin 625 Duo was typed as free text. Authorise stays blocked until the doctor gives a reason, exactly as for other severe alerts. The reason is stored with the line, written to the audit record and carried on the print. With No known allergies confirmed, today's amber Not checked note stays and no reason is asked. The honest Not checked wording already on screen stays. The rule lives on the server in the prescription safety check and the authorise guard; the screen only shows it.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/medvya-workspace-concept.html, doctor view: type a brand in the medicine box; screenshot docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/screenshots/doctor-1440-free-text-ack.png. The concept's inline box is a sketch: in the product the line is added through the existing Add medicine dialog.
Components and tokens affected: SafetyChecks, AddMedicinePanel; no new component. Wording in en, hi and ar.
Front end and back end split: Back end: the rule in the prescription safety check and the authorise guard, the reason on the line, the audit event and the print. Front end: the alert wording and the existing reason step.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None in code: it does not wait for any component. Started on day one of track S.
Clinical sign-off: Required before merge: questions 1 and 2 of docs/product-ux-audit/11-pilot-doctor-validation-plan.md (brand or generic; the wording Not checked against; whether a typed reason on every such line is acceptable), recorded on the issue with a date. Safe acceptance criterion 3 of the plan applies.
Effort and regression risk: M · Low for regressions. Product risk: if the doctor prescribes mostly by brand, a reason on every line trains dismissal, so the brand list ticket matters as much as this one.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Brand names in the formulary (the next ticket). (2) Replacing the Add medicine dialog or adding an inline free-text box (forbidden until this is closed and a clinician has seen a replacement). (3) Interaction or dose checks for free text. (4) Any change to how a formulary medicine is checked.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given Meera Iyer with a recorded penicillin allergy and a free-text line Augmentin 625 Duo, when the doctor presses Authorise without a reason, then the server refuses and the prescription stays a draft
* Given a patient with two recorded allergies, when a free-text line is added, then the severe alert reads Not checked against, names both allergies and the typed medicine, and does not rely on colour
* Given a patient whose allergies are not recorded, when a free-text line is added, then the same severe alert and reason step apply
* Given the doctor gives a reason and authorises, when the audit log and the print are read, then both carry the reason for that line
* Given a patient with No known allergies confirmed, when a free-text line is added, then only the amber Not checked note shows and no reason is asked
* Given the integration test on real PostgreSQL that authorises a free-text line for an allergic patient, when the server rule is removed, then the test fails (mutation check, shown in the pull request)
* Given the alert and the reason field, when they appear, then they are announced, reachable by keyboard and axe finds no violation in English or Arabic
* Given the refusal, when logs, telemetry and the address bar are read, then they hold no medicine name tied to a patient and no allergy text

Summary: Load the pilot clinic's brand names into the formulary, mapped to generic and class; offer generic matches for typed text

Description:

Findings and reviewers: F-01 · reviewer A-02.
Rationale: A brand typed as free text skips the allergy check. If the doctor's usual brands are in the formulary, mapped to their generic and class, most lines are checked and the reason step of the previous ticket stays rare enough to be read.
Proposed UX behaviour: The pilot doctor's usual brands (about 100 medicines) are added to the clinic formulary, each mapped to its generic, strength, form and allergy class, so a search by brand finds a checked medicine. When typed text has no exact match, the dialog offers Did you mean with the closest generic and brand rows before Add as free text. Search matches at the start of words, not inside them.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/screenshots/doctor-1440-allergy-block.png (a formulary conflict blocked in words).
Components and tokens affected: Formulary data and import; AddMedicinePanel search list. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Data and a clinical review of the mapping; a small front-end change for the suggestion; back end only if brand search is not yet indexed.
Prerequisites and blocked by: A person: the pilot doctor's list (question 1 of the validation plan). Started in parallel with the free-text rule on day one, because the list takes calendar time.
Clinical sign-off: Required: clinical review of each brand's generic and class mapping (ADR-015 already asks for it; see #1041), recorded on the issue with the reviewer's role and date.
Effort and regression risk: M · Low in code. A wrong class mapping is a safety risk, which is why a named reviewer signs the mapping.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) A national brand database. (2) Automatic mapping without review. (3) Interaction data for brands beyond what the generic already has.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the loaded list, when the doctor searches Augmentin, then the amoxicillin and clavulanate row is offered with the brand shown
* Given a patient with a penicillin allergy, when that brand row is chosen, then it is blocked in the dialog and at authorisation exactly as the generic is
* Given typed text with no exact match, when the list opens, then the closest formulary rows are offered above Add as free text
* Given the imported list, when the issue is closed, then each brand's generic and class mapping carries a named clinical reviewer and date
* Given two clinics, when one loads its brands, then the other clinic's formulary and search do not show them (integration test with row-level security)
* Given the search list in English and Arabic, when axe runs, then there is no violation

Summary: The note always shows what the server holds; the last keystrokes survive a page change and a reload
Labels: phase-P1 notes encounters reliability safety epic-ux-programme track-safety wave-s1
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S1. This is audit backlog UX-04 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: /consult/:id and back from /consult/:id/problems · doctor.
Findings and reviewers: F-03, F-26 · reviewers A-03, A-15.
Rationale: Type in Assessment, open Problems within two seconds, come back: the field shows old or empty text although the server has the new text. The signed note later carried text the screen had not shown. A reload within two seconds of typing loses the last sentence.
Proposed UX behaviour: On mount the consultation refetches the note. Leaving the page flushes pending text and writes it to the query cache. On pagehide the pending text is sent with keepalive. The save status reads Saving…, then Saved with the time, or Not saved. Trying again.; it never says Saved before the server answered. No draft is kept in browser storage: AGENTS.md 1.2 forbids patient data there, and changing that needs a security decision and an ADR, which this ticket does not ask for.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/medvya-workspace-concept.html, audit note 7 (save status in the footer).
Components and tokens affected: The note controller hook. SaveStatus from the library when it has landed; until then the existing status text with the three honest wordings.
Front end and back end split: Front end only.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None. It does not wait for the SaveStatus component: the wording ships with the existing element and moves to the component later.
Clinical sign-off: Not required (engineering validates). Safe acceptance criterion 6 of the validation plan applies: no Saved the person did not cause.
Effort and regression risk: S to M · Low. The conflict detection between two tabs must keep working.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) A local draft in browser storage. (2) Changing autosave timing or the conflict rule.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given text typed in Assessment, when the doctor opens Problems within 500 ms and comes back, then the field shows the new text
* Given text typed in Plan, when the page is reloaded within 500 ms, then the new text is there
* Given a slow or failed save, when the status is read, then it says Saving… or Not saved. Trying again. and never Saved
* Given the page-hop test, when the refetch on mount is removed, then the test fails
* Given the same note open in two tabs, when both type, then the second writer is told and keeps their text, as today
* Given a consultation in use, when localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB are read, then they hold no note text
* Given a screen reader, when the status changes, then it is announced politely, and axe finds no violation in English or Arabic

Summary: Ending or signing with an unfinished prescription or order asks first; unfinished ones show on the doctor's day

Description:

Persona and route: /consult/:id (End consultation, Sign note) and /today · doctor.
Findings and reviewers: F-04 · reviewer A-04.
Rationale: End consultation is one click with no dialog. A draft prescription or unplaced orders are left read-only for ever, Today says nothing about them, and the patient leaves without a valid prescription.
Proposed UX behaviour: End consultation, and Sign note, with a draft prescription or unplaced orders open a dialog that names the patient and lists what is unfinished, with three choices: Authorise now (goes to the prescription; authorising stays its own act with its own step-up), Discard the draft (with a reason, audited), End anyway. Today lists Prescriptions to authorise beside Notes to sign, each row opening the consultation at the prescription. A draft can be completed and authorised after the visit ended, by the same doctor, until it is discarded. Sign, authorise, place orders and end stay four separate, recorded acts.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/medvya-workspace-concept.html, To finish in the queue rail and audit note 7.
Components and tokens affected: The existing Dialog (ConfirmDialog use); Today list. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Front end: the dialog and the Today list. Back end: allow editing and authorising a draft after the encounter ended, a pending-prescriptions query scoped to the doctor, the discard reason and audit events.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None in code. Product decision first: may a draft be finished after the patient left?
Clinical sign-off: Required before merge: question 6 of the validation plan, recorded on the issue with a date.
Effort and regression risk: M · Medium: touches the encounter and prescription state rules; signed notes and authorised prescriptions must stay immutable.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Reopening an ended consultation's note. (2) Authorising as a side effect of signing. (3) A reminder to the patient.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a draft prescription, when the doctor presses End consultation, then a dialog names the patient and the draft and nothing ends until a choice is made
* Given unplaced orders, when the doctor presses Sign note, then the same dialog lists them before the sign dialog
* Given End anyway was chosen, when the doctor opens Today, then Prescriptions to authorise shows the patient and opens the consultation at the prescription
* Given an ended visit with a draft, when the same doctor completes and authorises it, then it is authorised with its own audit record; another doctor without a care relationship is refused by the server
* Given Discard the draft with a reason, when the audit log is read, then it holds who, when and the reason, and the draft no longer appears on Today
* Given the integration tests for authorise-after-end, when the same-doctor rule or the ended-visit rule is removed, then a test fails
* Given a visit taken to the end, when the audit log is read, then sign, authorise, place orders and end are four separate events
* Given the dialog, when it opens, then focus is inside it, Escape cancels, and axe finds no violation in English or Arabic

The Review and sign bar becomes the StickyActionBar footer that reserves its space. The Add medicine dialog and the sign dialog keep repeating the patient, as today. No rule, wording or field changes.

Safe acceptance criterion 2 of that plan applies: whose record is this and what is she allergic to, answered without scrolling, three times out of three.

Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) The consultation layout pass (next ticket in this wave). (2) The queue button in the strip (queue rail ticket). (3) Nurse intake on a phone: blocked until one group shows per screen (phone rule ticket). (4) Any change to allergy rules or wording.

* Given an open consultation for a patient with a recorded penicillin allergy at 1440 by 900, 1024 by 768 and 768 by 1024, when the page is scrolled to the prescription, then the patient's name and the words Allergy: Penicillin are inside the viewport
* Given the medicines and problems sub-pages and nurse intake at 1024 touch, when each is scrolled to its last field, then the strip is still visible and names the same patient

Rationale: The server refuses correctly, but the screen says Page not found. The link may be old. A person thinks the product is broken. A nurse opening a consultation sees two red error lines.

Components and tokens affected: PageMessage (denied). i18n keys in en, hi and ar.
Front end and back end split: Front end only. The server's refusals are unchanged and are not relaxed.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the page components ticket (PageMessage).
Clinical sign-off: Not required.
Effort and regression risk: S · Low. The control is on the server; this is only the message.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Any change to who may open what. (2) Hiding Today for roles that only get the board (the navigation names ticket).

Summary: Check-in time is measured from opening Walk-in to the token, so the pilot metric cannot read 0 s, target met
