Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S2. This is audit backlog UX-22 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Walk-in and check-in (receptionist); Settings → Practice → Pilot metrics (owner).
Findings and reviewers: F-29 (the verified metric defect) · reviewer A-19. Part 1 of 2 of audit backlog UX-22 (part 2 is the owner's Clinic today page, after the first pilot weeks).
Rationale: A walk-in is created and checked in by one action, so its timed check-in is zero and the metric reads Check-in time, returning patients (median): 0 s. Target of 60 s met. The one number meant to prove the desk is faster will always look perfect. No number the system did not earn.
Proposed UX behaviour: Check-in time runs from opening Walk-in (or the first search keystroke at check-in) to the token being issued. The duration is sent with the check-in and stored; a missing or impossible duration is stored as not measured and left out of the median, never counted as zero. The pilot metric shows how many check-ins were timed and says No data yet when none were. Past zero-second rows are excluded from the median and labelled not measured.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/screenshots/owner-1440.png (Not tracked yet wording).
Components and tokens affected: Pilot metrics panel; walk-in and check-in controllers. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Front end: capture the start. Back end: store the duration, the median rule, the exclusion of old zero rows.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None.
Clinical sign-off: Not required. The owner is asked what they expect in question 17 of the validation plan.
Effort and regression risk: M · Low. The walk-in path must not gain a click.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) The Clinic today page (part 2). (2) Per-doctor consult times (they wait for the undo ticket). (3) Changing the baseline capture of MDV-P1-041.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a walk-in checked in 40 seconds after Walk-in was opened, when the metric is read, then that check-in counts as about 40 s
* Given a check-in with no measured start, when the median is computed, then it is left out and shown as not measured
* Given the metric test, when unmeasured rows are counted as zero again, then the test fails
* Given no timed check-ins in the period, when the metric renders, then it says No data yet and not a number
* Given the walk-in path, when it is measured, then it is still at most 6 clicks new and 3 returning
* Given two clinics, when metrics are read, then each sees only its own; no patient data is in the metric, logs or address

Summary: Staff: only an owner can offboard an owner, step-up on any offboarding, change a role in place; link or remove /admin/staff
Labels: phase-P1 staff offboarding authorisation security roles epic-ux-programme track-safety wave-s3
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S3. This is audit backlog UX-27 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Settings → People → Staff; /admin/staff · owner, practice admin.
Findings and reviewers: F-30 · reviewers A-23, C-14, C-15.
Rationale: A practice admin is offered Offboard on the owner doctor and the dialog opens; the code refuses only the last administrator. If it goes through, a hired admin ends the owner's access and moves the owner's patients to Needs rebooking. A role cannot be changed without offboarding and inviting again. /admin/staff is a second invite flow reachable only by typing the address.
Proposed UX behaviour: First, a test on real PostgreSQL records what the server does today when a practice admin offboards an owner. Then: only an owner may offboard an owner, and never the last owner; the server refuses anyone else. Any offboarding asks for the identity step-up. The Offboard button is absent on rows the signed-in user may not offboard and on their own row, with a short reason in words. Change role is offered on a staff row: it takes effect on the next request, ends sessions that hold the old role, and is audited. /admin/staff is either linked from Settings → People or removed with its route.
Prototype and blueprint reference: None.
Components and tokens affected: Staff table row actions; the existing Dialog and step-up. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Back end: the owner rule, step-up on the offboard endpoint, the change-role endpoint with policy and audit. Front end: row actions, dialog.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None in code.
Clinical sign-off: Decision required before merge: question 18 of the validation plan (may a practice admin remove a doctor, or only the owner), recorded on the issue.
Effort and regression risk: M · Medium: authorisation and sessions. ponytail-review and a mutation check are required by the house rules for anything touching auth.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Custom roles (exist). (2) Bulk changes. (3) Compact rows on the staff table (after-pilot table ticket).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a practice admin and an owner, when the admin calls the offboard endpoint for the owner on main, then a test records the answer and the issue states it
* Given a practice admin, when the offboard endpoint is called for an owner, then the server answers 403 and nothing changes
* Given one owner, when anyone tries to offboard them, then the server refuses
* Given any offboarding, when it is confirmed without a recent step-up, then the server asks for it
* Given a receptionist, when an owner changes her to nurse, then her next request has the nurse's access, her old sessions end, and the audit log holds who, when, from and to
* Given the integration tests, when the owner rule or the step-up requirement is removed, then a test fails
* Given the staff table, when a user may not offboard a row, then no Offboard button is offered there; axe finds no violation in English or Arabic
* Given the app, when /admin/staff is opened, then it is linked from Settings or answers Page not found

Summary: UX validation sessions with the pilot doctor, nurse, receptionist and owner: the 21 decisions, the brand list, the training date and the device check
Labels: phase-P1 pilot clinical needs-person ux epic-ux-programme
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track people gate, wave People. No audit backlog id. Created from the audit's rulings and blueprint, not from a backlog line (see Findings).

Persona and route: Sessions on the Azure dev app after the redeploy, with the concept open beside it. Synthetic patients only.
Findings and reviewers: All findings marked as needing clinical validation; the 21 decisions of the validation plan. No UX number in the backlog: the plan itself is the source.
Rationale: No clinician, nurse, receptionist or owner took part in the audit. Nothing safety-sensitive should be built from the audit alone, and twelve tickets may not merge until a named person has agreed.
Proposed UX behaviour: The founder runs the four scripted sessions of the plan (doctor 40 minutes on the room device, receptionist 30 at the desk, nurse 20 on a tablet, owner 20) and records each of the 21 decisions with the person's role and the date, on the ticket that the decision blocks. Rows 1 to 5 come first, before the first safety tickets merge. The founder also collects the doctor's list of about 100 medicines with brands, fixes the training date and says whether screens may change shape before it or only after the first pilot weeks, and checks on site which devices are used at the desk, in the room and by the nurse (mouse or touch), including one run of the consultation and nurse intake on a real tablet.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/medvya-workspace-concept.html and docs/product-ux-audit/12-prototype-guide.md (What to try).
Components and tokens affected: None.
Front end and back end split: People only. No code.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the Azure redeploy ticket (the sessions run on the redeployed app) and by the signed pilot agreement (MDV-P1-043).
Clinical sign-off: This ticket is the sign-off. It stands apart from the clinical advisor's journey sign-off (MDV-P1-073), which is still required.
Effort and regression risk: M (calendar time, not build time) · None to the code. Schedule risk: every ticket that names a question waits for it.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) A clinical safety standard: the plan's criteria are the audit's proposals. (2) Real patient data in any session. (3) The journey sign-off of MDV-P1-073.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the validation plan, when the first safety tickets are ready to merge, then decisions 1 to 5 are recorded with role and date on the tickets they block
* Given the plan's table, when this gate closes, then each of the 21 rows has an answer, a name by role and a date, on the blocked ticket and summarised here
* Given the doctor's session on the changed consultation, when asked whose record is this and what is she allergic to without scrolling, then the answer is right three times out of three
* Given the doctor's session, when the usual antibiotic is prescribed for the penicillin-allergic synthetic patient, then no medicine of that class is authorised without a stop the doctor noticed
* Given the receptionist's session, when she presses Call in on the wrong patient, then she recovers without help
* Given this gate, when it closes, then the brand list is attached to the brand ticket, the training date is written on the navigation names ticket and the device check is written here
* Given every session, when notes and screenshots are stored, then they hold synthetic patients only and no real person's health data

Summary: The server refuses to sign a consultation note until the doctor has confirmed identity with the patient
Labels: phase-P1 signing encounters safety clinical-safety security epic-ux-programme track-safety wave-s3
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S3. No audit backlog id: an open finding from the MDV-P1-091 review, decided by the owner on 14 Nov 2026.

Persona and route: Sign note on /consult/:id (and from Today after the consultation ended) · doctor.
Findings and reviewers: MDV-P1-091 stores "Confirmed with the patient" (IdentityConfirmedAt, set once, never cleared), and the signing checklist blocks Sign until it is there. The sign endpoint does not check it, so any other client or a direct call can sign a note whose identity was never confirmed.
Rationale: Authorisation and safety rules are enforced on the server (AGENTS.md 1.3). A rule that lives only in the browser is not a control.
Proposed UX behaviour: Signing a consultation note whose encounter has no stored identity confirmation is refused with 409 and a plain reason key (identity not confirmed with the patient). Nothing is signed, no signed version is written and the audit records the refused attempt without patient data. The web app already prevents this through the checklist, so a doctor using it sees no change; if the server refuses anyway (for example a stale page), the note page shows the reason and the confirm action. Addenda to an already signed note are not affected.
Prototype and blueprint reference: None.
Components and tokens affected: ConsultNoteService.SignAsync and its endpoint; the note controller's error mapping. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Back end; a small front-end error mapping.
Prerequisites and blocked by: MDV-P1-091 (done). Touches the same sign path as MDV-P2-049 (print snapshot at signing); whichever merges second rebases.
Clinical sign-off: Not required: it enforces on the server a rule the pilot doctor's checklist already applies.
Effort and regression risk: S · Low. Fixtures and journeys that sign notes must confirm identity first.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Any change to how identity is confirmed. (2) Notes signed without the patient present (for example a result review) are not a feature today; if one is added it needs its own decision. (3) Addenda.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a draft note on an encounter with no identity confirmation, when the sign endpoint is called directly by the treating doctor, then it answers 409 with the identity reason, the note stays a draft and no signed version exists
* Given the same note after the doctor confirms identity, when it is signed, then it signs as today
* Given a refused sign, when the audit and the logs are read, then the attempt is recorded with the encounter id and no patient name, date of birth or note text
* Given the integration test of the refusal, when the server check is removed, then the test fails (mutation check)
* Given the web app with a stale page that skipped the checklist, when the server refuses, then the note page says identity is not confirmed and offers the confirm action, in English and Arabic, axe clean
* Given a signed note, when an addendum is signed, then the identity rule does not apply

Summary: Encounters module: start a consultation from the board/Today, bound to one patient and appointment
Description: ENCOUNTER aggregate (tenant, facility, patient, lead clinician, appointment, status, started_at, authority_mode = medvya), created when the doctor calls the patient in / starts the consultation. Board state "In consult" and Today reflect it. Identity banner component bound to the encounter (name, age, sex, MRN, DOB, allergies, consent state, encounter date/room).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Starting a consult creates exactly one active encounter for the appointment; a second start reuses it (idempotent).
* Every clinical screen in P2 shows the identity banner for the bound encounter; switching patient requires closing or explicitly leaving the encounter.
* Encounter start/end events update the reception board within 2 seconds.
* Encounter APIs require the clinician relationship/purpose policy (MDV-P2-024).

Summary: Doctor Today (D-01): schedule, patient flags, pending notes, inbox counts
Description: /today: today's schedule with time, name, age/sex, reason category and status chips (Seen · note signed, In room, Waiting · 12 min, Checked in · vitals done, Joined waiting room, Booked, No-show); "Next patient" hero with Start consultation; pending/unsigned notes; flags (allergy, incomplete registration); inbox counts (P4 placeholder behind flag); mine vs clinic toggle (D-04). Mobile version with bottom tabs.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Today shows only the signed-in doctor's appointments by default and the clinic view when toggled (permissions respected).
* Unsigned notes from previous days appear as "pending notes" until signed.
* Clicking a patient opens Patient 360 for that encounter; "Start consultation" starts/opens the encounter.
* Status chips use icon + label and update live from the board.
* Mobile layout keeps the consult button in thumb reach with the next patient hero.

Summary: Privacy-safe global search (⌘K) with care-relationship check and "Request access"
Description: ⌘K / Ctrl+K overlay: search name, MRN, phone. Results show initials + age + MRN tail until opened. Patients outside the user's care relationship show "Request access" (in clinics: request to owner; hospitals: break-glass in P7). Actions: Open chart · Start visit · Book.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Results never include full names or identifiers before a record is opened (payload test).
* Opening a patient without a care relationship is blocked and offers Request access; the request is audited and notifies the owner.
* Keyboard: open with ⌘K/Ctrl+K, arrow navigation, Enter to open, Esc to close; screen-reader announcements.
* p95 search latency < 300 ms.

Summary: Patient 360 (E-01): banner with identity and allergies always visible; problems, medicines, vitals trends
Description: /patients/:id: fixed identity banner (allergy chip never collapses; text + icon), verified chart cards: problems (with verification state), medicines (active/stopped with source), allergies, last vitals, key labs with trend mini-charts (HbA1c, BP, weight), last encounters. Start consultation in banner. Tablet two-column layout. The right-hand "AI summary · not reviewed" panel is reserved and hidden by flag until P3.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Allergy state is shown with icon + text (e.g. "Allergy: Penicillin · verified"); "No known allergies" and "Allergies not recorded" are distinct states.
* Every chart fact shows its provenance tag (Clinician verified, Patient reported, Imported, Synced from HIS) — never an unlabelled value.
* Opening Patient 360 writes an audit event with purpose.
* Receptionist role cannot load Patient 360 (403, audited).
* Layout matches desktop and tablet designs; works at 200 % zoom.

Summary: Longitudinal timeline and trends with source labels and filters (E-02)
Description: /patients/:id/timeline: one chronological list across encounters, labs, medicines, documents with filters (All, Encounters, Labs, Medicines, Documents, source) and provenance tags (Medvya · signed, Clinician verified, Lab feed, Synced from HIS, Uploaded by patient, Imported). Trend chart toggle (HbA1c / BP / weight) with values and dates. "Load earlier…" pagination.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Each entry shows date, title, subtitle, author/source and provenance tag.
* Filters combine and persist per user session; empty filter result shows a clear empty state.
* Trend charts show values with units and dates, accessible as a data table for screen readers.
* Pagination loads older entries without losing scroll position.

Summary: Documents: upload, malware scan, secure viewer with time-limited links, scan to patient file (E-03)
Description: Upload PDF/images (desk scanner, phone camera, file) with type and source; stored in private Blob (CMK) with random keys; Defender for Storage / malware scan before availability; viewer streams via user-delegation SAS valid ≤ 5 minutes, watermarked with viewer and time; no download for reception; original file always kept; failed upload → retry.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A file is not viewable until the malware scan passes; infected files are quarantined and the uploader is told.
* Viewer links expire within 5 minutes and are bound to the requesting user; blob names contain no PHI.
* Receptionists can upload and see the document list but cannot open clinical documents (policy test).
* Original files are immutable; metadata edits (type, date) are audited.
* Phone camera capture works on mobile web (multi-page to single PDF).
* Follow-up moved from MDV-P1-062: an organisation onboarding document (MDV-P1-062) is scanned by the same seam, is not openable by Medvya operations until the scan is clean, and an infected file is refused and quarantined. Needs the seam in a shared place both Encounters and Tenancy may use, and the organisation documents in their own container.

Summary: Nurse intake queue and vitals with out-of-range re-measure and escalation (N-01)
Description: /nurse intake queue (cards from "With nurse" column, Open intake) → /nurse/:id/intake: identity check, large inputs for BP systolic/diastolic, pulse, temperature, SpO₂, weight with previous value; out-of-range values flagged in words ("High · re-check", "Outside usual range", "+2.2 kg since …"), prompt to re-measure, then "Escalate to doctor" with reason (creates an urgent item on the doctor's Today). Chief complaint in patient's words.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Values are validated for physiological plausibility (reject impossible values) and flagged against configurable ranges with text, not colour only.
* A flagged value requires re-measure or an explicit "keep value" before handoff.
* Escalate to doctor requires a reason and appears on the treating doctor's Today within 2 seconds.
* Saved vitals become OBSERVATIONs with source "Nurse intake", verified by the nurse, visible in Patient 360.
* Tablet-first layout with ≥ 44 px targets.

Summary: Allergy verification and patient-reported medicines with handoff to the doctor (N-01)
Description: Each existing or reported allergy must be set to Confirmed / Patient reported / Unknown / Not an allergy; new allergies can be added with reaction. Medicines captured as patient-reported (name, dose, frequency) or "Needs clarification" for unknown names. "Hand off · Ready for doctor" is disabled with "Confirm allergy status to hand off" until every allergy has a status; handoff moves the board card to Ready for doctor.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Handoff is impossible (UI and API) while any allergy lacks a status.
* Allergy statuses and medicine statements store source (nurse intake, patient) and actor.
* Handoff updates the board and Today in real time.
* "No known allergies" must be explicitly confirmed; it is never the default.

Summary: Consultation note editor: chief complaint, SOAP, specialty templates, manual note when recording is declined (E-04)
Description: Note editor with sections (Chief complaint, Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan) per template; Objective prefilled from verified chart only (nurse vitals) with provenance; quick phrases and previous-note snippets; autosave drafts every few seconds (server-side, encrypted at rest) so refresh/network loss loses nothing. This is the non-AI baseline that AI must never break; in P3 the "Recording declined" banner reuses it without guilt copy.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Drafts autosave and survive refresh, network drop and session timeout (restored after re-auth with patient confirmation).
* Prefilled content is only from verified chart data and is labelled with its source.
* Templates can be switched; switching preserves typed content in matching sections and warns about unmapped content.
* Note editor is fully keyboard operable and readable at 200 % zoom.

Summary: Diagnosis coding with ICD-10 and problem verification states (E-07)
Description: Problem list editing in the encounter: ICD-10 search (code + description), add/update problems with verification state (Verified, Added today · verified, Patient reported, Provisional), onset, status (active/resolved). Coded diagnoses link to the encounter for later claims (P5).
Acceptance Criteria:
* ICD-10 search returns results by code or words in < 300 ms.
* Each problem stores code system/version, verification state, author and encounter.
* Provisional problems are visually distinct and not exported as confirmed diagnoses.
* Code set version is configurable per country (decision recorded).

Summary: Medication reconciliation: chart vs patient-reported vs other source, keep / change / stop (E-07)
Description: Reconciliation table: medicine, chart, patient-reported, other source (HIS column hidden until P7), conflict flag, decision Keep / Change / Stop (patient-only items: Add / Ignore). Summary "n of m decided · k sources disagree". "Confirm changes" disabled until every row has a decision; confirmed decisions update MEDICATION_STATEMENT review_state and feed the Rx composer (stop → discontinue line).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Confirm is disabled until all rows are decided (UI + API).
* Each decision records actor, time and reason for Stop/Change; history is kept.
* Conflicts are flagged with text (e.g. "atorvastatin active in chart, patient says stopped").
* Stopped medicines show as stopped with date in Patient 360 and the timeline.

Summary: Sign and finalise: immutable signed note v1 with re-authentication (E-06)
Description: Sign modal: "Sign note for {name}? MRN · DOB · encounter id. I have reviewed every section … read-only after signing. Prescriptions and orders are authorised separately." CTA "Sign as Dr. {name}" requires passkey/MFA step-up. Signed NOTE_VERSION v1 is stored in a hash-chained table (MDV-P0-036) with document hash; banner "SIGNED v1 · read-only" and signer line with licence number and time.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Only a doctor with a verified licence and care relationship can sign; step-up authentication is required within the last 5 minutes.
* After signing, the note body cannot be modified through any API; an automated test attempts direct API and repository updates and both fail (exit gate 3).
* The stored document hash verifies against the rendered content; ledger verification passes.
* Signing writes NoteSigned.v1 (no PHI) and an audit event; Today removes it from pending notes.

Summary: Addenda, version history and print/PDF of the signed note (E-06)
Description: Addendum composer on a signed note creates a new signed version (amends_version_id, reason) with the same sign flow; version history lists v1, v2… with signer and time. Print/PDF: A4, header with patient name, MRN and DOB on every page, signer block, version, "Corrections are added as signed addenda".
Acceptance Criteria:
* An addendum never alters v1; viewing shows the original plus addenda in order.
* Addendum requires a reason and step-up authentication.
* PDF renders server-side with MRN/DOB on every page and is stored with hash.
* Print view passes screen-reader and 200 % zoom checks.

Summary: Country formulary and order sets: India (Schedule H/H1/X) and UAE drug codes, admin add medicine (F-13)
Description: FORMULARY_ITEM per tenant and country: generic (INN), strength, form, brands, national code (UAE drug code), regulatory class (India Schedule H/H1/X; UAE controlled), ATC, default sig, status. Seed from the chosen data source; admin can add a medicine (validated) and build order sets (e.g. "Diabetes review labs"). Medicines not in the formulary can be prescribed as free text, flagged for review.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The data source and licence for each country are decided and recorded in an ADR before seeding (dependency 1 closed).
* Search by generic or brand returns strength/form options in < 300 ms.
* Controlled/scheduled classes are labelled and drive print requirements (e.g. Schedule H warning text).
* Admin-added medicines are audited and marked "clinic-added".
* Order sets can be created and used in the order composer.

Summary: Prescription composer with dose builder and add-medicine-while-prescribing (E-05, E-11)
Description: Rx items: drug (from formulary), form/strength, dose builder (dose, unit, route, frequency, timing e.g. "with dinner", duration, quantity), instructions; source chip (Added by you, Chart reconciliation); safety chip (results of MDV-P2-016). Discontinue lines from reconciliation. Free-text medicine allowed with review flag.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Dose builder produces a structured sig and a human-readable instruction in the selected print language.
* Lines from reconciliation (stop) appear as discontinue lines automatically.
* Free-text medicines are flagged and excluded from interaction checks with a visible warning.
* Draft Rx autosaves; Rx is not authorised until MDV-P2-017.

Summary: Allergy and interaction safety checks before authorisation
Description: Checks run on every add/change and again on authorisation: allergy/cross-sensitivity (e.g. penicillin class), drug–drug interactions (severity levels), duplicate therapy, dose range per age/renal function where data exists (e.g. "Renal dose OK · eGFR 72"). Severe findings require an override reason; results show as chips with words, not colour only.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A seeded conflict set (allergy class, interacting pairs, duplicates, out-of-range doses) triggers the expected alert in 100 % of cases (automated test; exit gate 2).
* Authorising with a severe alert requires an override reason, recorded and audited.
* Alerts state severity in words and the evidence (e.g. "Allergy: Penicillin · verified").
* The interaction source and version are shown in an info panel and recorded with each check result.

Summary: Rx authorisation (separate from note), server-side multilingual printed Rx A4/A5 with hash and QR verify (E-10)
Description: "Authorise prescription" is a separate action from signing the note (step-up auth). Server-side PDF (QuestPDF) in A4 and A5: clinic header/logo, doctor name, qualifications, licence number, signature image, patient identifiers, generic names first then brand, sig in English (a patient-language line later if pilots ask), scheduled-drug notes, QR code to verify authenticity; stored with SHA-256 hash.
Acceptance Criteria:
* An Rx cannot be printed or shared until authorised; authorisation is audited.
* PDF renders server-side for A4 and A5 and is stored with a hash; the QR verify page shows validity without exposing PHI beyond what the patient holds.
* The PDF prints instructions in English; names and free text in Hindi, Tamil or Arabic print shaped (owner decision 11 Nov 2026: in India the pharmacist explains the medicines in the patient's language; a reviewed patient-language instruction line comes later if pilots ask for it).
* Each pilot doctor reviews and approves their own Rx layout (approval recorded per doctor; exit gate 4).
* Print layout passes 200 % zoom and screen-reader labelling checks in the on-screen preview.
* Given a prescription is printed, when it renders, then it shows the doctor's licence number and authority (moved from MDV-P1-065; the number and authority are already stored on DoctorLicence and attested by the owner).

Summary: Investigation orders composer with Draft → Ordered states (E-05)
Description: Order composer with lab/imaging tests from order sets or search, notes (e.g. "fasting 10 h"), destination lab (free text in P2), "Place orders" action separate from note signing. CLINICAL_ORDER state Draft → Ordered; printed/PDF investigation slip. Results arrive in P4 (C-01).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Orders stay Draft until "Place orders"; placing is audited and shows state Ordered with icon + label.
* An investigation slip PDF can be printed/shared with patient identifiers and instructions.
* Orders appear on the patient timeline with state.
* Placing orders never happens automatically from note signing.

Summary: Referrals out and in with status (E-09)
Description: REFERRAL: to clinician/facility (free text or directory), urgency, reason, attached summary, channel (print, email, patient carries), consent for sharing, state (draft → sent → appointment booked → report received → closed). Incoming referral letters are filed as documents linked to a referral-in.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Sending a referral requires sharing consent where the policy demands it and records channel and time.
* Referral letter PDF includes only the selected summary content.
* Status can be updated with evidence (e.g. report received → document link).
* Open referrals are visible on Patient 360.

Summary: Share Rx with patient/pharmacy (e-Rx PDF/link) and pharmacy dispatch record (E-10)
Description: Share the authorised Rx PDF to the patient (WhatsApp/SMS/email secure link with OTP, no PHI in message text) or to a named pharmacy (email/link), recording PHARMACY_DISPATCH (pharmacy ref, state, dispensed_at manual update). Regulator e-Rx submission is out of scope (P5-04).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Share links expire, require OTP to the patient's registered mobile and are audited when opened.
* Message text contains no medicine names or clinical details.
* Pharmacy dispatch records state changes with actor.
* No regulator submission endpoint exists in P2 (scope guard).

Summary: Clinical safety case and hazard log with a named clinical safety reviewer
Description: docs/clinical-safety/: intended use, hazard log (wrong patient, missed allergy, wrong dose, lost result, unsigned note treated as signed, duplicate merge error, …) with severity/likelihood, mitigations tied to tests, residual risk and release sign-off template. Name the clinical safety reviewer who signs each release from P2 onward; define clinical incident review process.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Hazard log covers every P2 clinical feature with at least one mitigation linked to a test or control.
* A named clinical safety reviewer is recorded and signs the R2 release.
* Clinical incident review process (report → triage → fix → review) is documented and tested once with a tabletop exercise.

Summary: Legal review of clinical data processing before the first real note
Description: Counsel reviews clinical data handling (purposes, consent/lawful basis, retention of notes/prescriptions per country rules, patient rights) before any real clinical note is created in production.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Written sign-off before clinical features are enabled for real patients (flag remains off until then).
* Retention periods for notes, prescriptions and documents per country are confirmed and loaded into retention configuration.

Summary: Define and operate the organisation onboarding review process (documents, SLA, rejection reasons, suspension)
Description: Superseded scope (ADR-016): Medvya reviews organisations, not doctors. Runbook for reviewing an onboarding request: which documents per type (Clinic, Hospital), what is checked against which public register or certificate, evidence recorded, SLA (target one working day, to be confirmed), standard reasons for ask-for-changes and reject, suspension and re-approval, and who may decide. Doctor licences are attested by the owner and are not checked here.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Runbook published in docs/runbooks/organisation-onboarding-review.md and linked from the platform console queue (MDV-P5-044).
* Every pilot organisation is approved with recorded evidence of what was checked before it registers patients.
* The runbook states that Medvya does not verify individual doctors and where the owner's attestation is recorded.

Summary: Clinical authorisation: care relationship and purpose checks, request access for clinics
Description: Implement the relationship + purpose parts of the authorisation hooks from P0: a clinician has a care relationship when the patient has an appointment/encounter with them, is in their facility's active patient list (configurable clinic policy), or access was granted. Purpose is recorded with every read. Request-access workflow for clinics; hospitals' break-glass comes in P7.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Clinicians without relationship get 403 + "Request access" (audited); owners can grant time-limited access.
* Every clinical read records purpose (treatment, registration, billing, audit).
* Clinic policy "all facility clinicians" vs "assigned only" is configurable and tested.
* Nurse access is limited per the matrix (Limited on Patient 360; entry of vitals/allergies).

Summary: Note template engine and specialty template pack for the partner clinics
Description: Template model (sections, prompts, required fields, quick phrases) with versioning; seed the six designed templates and specialty variants requested by the pilot doctors; templates selectable in onboarding and settings.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Six base templates exist and are reviewed by the clinical advisor.
* Each pilot doctor has their specialty template(s) configured before R2.
* Template changes create new versions; existing notes keep the version they used.

Summary: Doctor and nurse training (30 min each) and R2 materials
Description: Training, in the screen names of MDV-P2-051: My day, the Patient record (Summary, Details, Timeline, Documents), the Nurse queue, nurse intake and handoff, note writing, coding, reconciliation, signing and addenda, Rx authorisation and printing, orders, referrals, what never happens automatically. Quick reference card for doctors and nurses.
Acceptance Criteria:
* All pilot doctors and nurses trained; attendance recorded.
* Quick reference cards available at each workstation.

Summary: Print, accessibility and zoom verification across clinical screens
Description: Verify A4/A5 Rx and A4 signed note print layouts, 200 % zoom on all P2 screens, screen-reader labels on clinical controls (vitals inputs, allergy states, reconciliation decisions, sign button state), keyboard path consult → sign.
Acceptance Criteria:
* axe shows no violations on P2 screens; manual screen-reader pass recorded for N-01, E-07 and sign modal.
* Full keyboard path from Today → Patient 360 → note → sign → Rx authorise → print works.
* Print outputs match the designs and include identifiers on every page.

Summary: R2 pilot, exit gate review (≥ 20 signed visits per doctor) and release notes
Description: Pilot R2 on flags; evidence for: ≥ 20 real visits per pilot doctor signed in Medvya; allergy/interaction seeded tests 100 %; signed-note immutability test; each doctor's Rx layout approval. Clinical safety reviewer signs the release. R2 release notes and known-issues list. Journey steps for J1/J2/J3 without AI turn green.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Evidence for all four exit criteria attached and confirmed at the exit gate review.
* Clinical safety reviewer sign-off recorded for R2.
* R2 release notes list P2-01…P2-08 status and exclusions (AI drafting, billing, results inbox, regulator e-prescription).
* Playwright journeys J2/J3 pass for the non-AI path (consent declined/manual note).

Summary: Encounters start race: a second start that loses the race answers with the winner's encounter
Description: Two starts of the same visit at the same moment (double click, two tabs) could fail: the losing start read no encounter for the visit, then the winner committed, then the loser's open-consultation check found the winner's encounter for this same visit and refused with "another consultation is open". The open-consultation check now ignores this visit's own encounter, so the loser goes on to the insert, meets the unique index and answers with the winner.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A start that reads no encounter for the visit and then loses the race to another start of the same visit answers with the winner's encounter, not "another consultation is open".
* A start whose insert meets the unique index answers with the winner's encounter (row-level security still applies to the re-read).
* The visit moves to In consult once and the board is told once.
* The lost-race interleavings are forced in the test (not left to parallel timing) and the test fails when the fix is removed.

Summary: Import the 12 Nov 2026 design (one-page chart, one-page consultation, Add medicine) and plan the upgrade epic
Description: Replace Medvya Web, Admin, Mobile and Foundations with the 12 Nov design. Record the gap between what is built (P2-E02 to P2-E05) and the design in the screen specs, and plan the stories MDV-P2-031 to P2-045. List the clinical sign-offs the design asks for (growth curves, vaccine schedules, drug rules) in the session handoff.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The four design files are the 12 Nov versions and the source README records the import and what changed.
* The screen specs describe the one-page chart, the life-stage modules, the one-page consultation and Add medicine, with what is already built.
* The session handoff lists the clinical sign-offs needed before the pilot uses the new rules.

Summary: More vitals and key labs on the chart, each flagged against its reference range
Description: Add observation codes for height, respiratory rate, pain score, standing blood pressure, fundal height and fetal heart rate, and the key labs LDL cholesterol, eGFR, urine albumin/creatinine ratio, haemoglobin, ferritin, potassium, sodium, TSH, vitamin D and platelets. BMI is calculated from the latest weight and height, never stored as typed. Each code has a fixed unit and a reference range; a reading outside it is flagged in words (High, Low, with the range) on the chart. Nurse intake can enter height and respiratory rate. Patient 360 returns the latest reading and the trend for every code that has readings.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Every new code has one unit and a reference range, and a value outside the range is returned with a High or Low flag and the range text.
* BMI is shown only when a weight and a height exist, uses the latest of each and states the date of the older one.
* Nurse intake saves height and respiratory rate with the same refusal of impossible values as the other vitals.
* Patient 360 returns a trend for each code with two or more readings, oldest first, with the source of each point.
* shortcut: reference ranges are one adult set (children's vitals keep the age bands of #956) and wait for clinical sign-off.

Summary: Life stage, history sections and the fuller chart banner
Description: The chart works out the patient's life stage: child under 18, pregnancy while a pregnancy is open (MDV-P2-034), older adult from 65, otherwise adult. The life stage drives the chart module, the consultation template and the safety checks, and is shown as a label with an icon and words, not colour alone. History is kept in sections (past medical, surgical, family, social, women's health or obstetric, birth and feeding for a child, function and falls for an older adult), each with who wrote it and when. The banner adds blood group, preferred language, the care team and the consent state.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The life stage rule is tested at the edges: 17 y 364 d is a child, 18 y is an adult, 65 y is an older adult, and an open pregnancy wins over adult.
* A doctor or nurse can edit each history section; every save records the author and time and the previous text is kept.
* The banner shows blood group and language only when recorded; nothing is guessed.
* The history sections offered depend on the life stage (birth for a child, function for an older adult).

Summary: Patient chart on one page (E-01 redesign) with section filters and a life-stage module
Description: Patient 360 becomes one page: banner (name, age, date of birth, MRN, blood group, language, life-stage label, allergy chip, alerts, care team, consent); vitals strip of six tiles with a trend line and a flag; problems with ICD-10 codes; medicines with "Add medicine" (MDV-P2-039); the life-stage module; results and trends table; history; timeline; and a right column for care gaps, goals (MDV-P2-038) and documents. Section buttons show everything or one part. Empty, loading, error and no-access states as today.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Every block shows its data source as today (provenance tags) and an empty state when there is nothing.
* The section buttons filter the page and are keyboard operable; the choice is kept per user in the session only.
* The page works at 375 px (one column), 200 % zoom and right to left in Arabic; axe has no violations.
* A user without clinical access sees the banner and the locked notice only (server decides, as today).

Summary: Pregnancy record: dates, gestation, obstetric history, antenatal contacts and danger signs
Description: PREGNANCY_EPISODE per patient: last menstrual period, dating scan date and gestation at the scan, due date (LMP + 280 days, or from the scan when the scan differs by more than the dating rule), gravida, para, abortions and living children, blood group and Rh, and an outcome that closes it. Gestation today is worked out from the due date in the facility time zone. Antenatal contacts (8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 38, 40 weeks) show as done, today or to come, linked to visits. Danger signs counselled are recorded with who and when. The chart shows the pregnancy module and the life stage becomes Pregnancy.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Due date and gestation are tested: LMP 19 May 2026 gives due date 23 Feb 2027 and 24 w 3 d on 06 Nov 2026.
* A scan date that moves the due date records which date is used and why; the earlier date is kept.
* Only one open pregnancy per patient; closing it needs an outcome and the life stage returns to adult.
* Pregnancy data is SensitiveHealth, tenant isolated (EF filter and RLS) and never in logs or URLs.
* shortcut: the dating rule and the contact plan are the WHO model and wait for clinical sign-off.

Summary: Child growth: measurements and WHO centiles with a growth chart
Description: GROWTH_MEASUREMENT: weight, length or height and head circumference with date, from nurse intake or the chart. Centiles and z-scores for weight-for-age, length/height-for-age and BMI-for-age from 0 to 5 years by sex use the WHO LMS tables. The chart draws the 3rd, 15th, 50th, 85th and 97th lines with the child's points, states the centile in words and flags a crossing of two major centile lines or a fall below the 3rd. Weight velocity is shown between the last two weights.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The z-score calculation reproduces WHO's published examples to two decimals (test).
* The growth chart has a text alternative stating the latest centile and the trend.
* A child over 5 years shows the measurements without centiles and says why.
* shortcut: 0–5 y WHO only; IAP 2015 (5–18 y, India) and UAE national charts when the clinical reviewer chooses them. The tables wait for clinical sign-off.

Summary: Immunisations against the country schedule, and developmental milestones
Description: IMMUNIZATION: vaccine, dose, date given, batch, who gave it, or deferred with a reason. The country schedule (India IAP 2023, UAE national) is a country rule class; the chart lists each age band as given, due now, overdue or upcoming from the child's date of birth. DEVELOPMENTAL_MILESTONE: per age band, each milestone answered yes, no or unsure, with who answered (parent or clinician). Vaccines due feed the care gaps (MDV-P2-038).
Acceptance Criteria:
* The schedule is chosen by the facility's country through a country rule class, never an if on the country.
* Due and overdue are worked out from the date of birth in the facility time zone and tested at the band edges.
* Deferring a dose needs a reason; nothing is deleted.
* shortcut: the schedules are the design's reading of IAP 2023 and the UAE schedule and are marked unverified until clinical sign-off.

Summary: Older adult review: falls, walking test, standing blood pressure drop, frailty, memory, daily activities and a medicine review
Description: GERIATRIC_ASSESSMENT with date and author: falls in 12 months, Timed Up and Go seconds, lying and standing blood pressure (the drop is calculated and flagged as orthostatic at 20 systolic or 10 diastolic), Clinical Frailty Scale 1–9, Mini-Cog 0–5, ADL and IADL, PHQ-2 and a nutrition note. The medicine review lists suggestions from a small rule set (benzodiazepines, a proton pump inhibitor for more than 8 weeks, oral NSAIDs, and an ACE inhibitor or ARB with low eGFR and high potassium) as "suggestions, the doctor decides", each with a "plan change" action.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Each score is refused outside its scale and the orthostatic drop is tested at the flag line.
* The medicine review never changes a medicine by itself; a planned change goes to the consultation plan.
* shortcut: the flag lines and the rule set wait for clinical sign-off.

Summary: Chronic care targets, care gaps due today and care-plan goals
Description: Targets per patient for HbA1c, blood pressure, LDL, eGFR and urine albumin, with defaults the doctor can change; the chart shows each latest value against its target. Care gaps come from rules: diabetic eye and foot checks once a year, urine albumin once a year for diabetes, a test ordered but never resulted, vaccines due (MDV-P2-036), the glucose tolerance test window at 24–28 weeks of pregnancy, and a falls review after a fall. Each gap has an action (add to today's visit, order, refer). Care-plan goals are text with a target and progress.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Each gap rule is tested for due, not due and done.
* A gap's action adds the item to the open consultation's plan; with no open consultation it says so.
* shortcut: the gap rules are the design's list and wait for clinical sign-off.

Summary: Add medicine panel from the chart and the consultation: strength, how often, when, how long, instructions, line and quantity
Description: A side panel opened from the chart's Medicines card and the consultation plan: search the formulary (brand or generic), choose the strength, how often (1-0-0, 0-0-1, 1-0-1, 1-1-1, when needed, weekly), when (before food, after food, bedtime, any time), for how long (3 days, 5 days, 1 month, 3 months, ongoing) and the patient instructions. It shows the patient (name, age, the context that drives the checks) and the allergy chip, the safety checks for this line (MDV-P2-016, MDV-P2-040), the finished prescription line and the quantity. "Add to prescription" adds the line to the encounter's draft prescription; a severe finding blocks it until another medicine is chosen or an override reason is given.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The quantity is calculated from frequency and duration (when needed: one pack) and tested.
* The line uses the existing sig, so print and share are unchanged.
* From the chart without an open consultation, the panel says a consultation must be started; nothing is prescribed outside an encounter.
* Keyboard path, 44 px targets, English and Arabic right to left, axe clean.

Summary: Patient-aware prescribing checks: pregnancy, weight-based child dose, kidney function and older adult
Description: The safety checks read the patient context: pregnancy and gestation (NSAIDs from 20 weeks severe), the latest weight no older than one month for a child (dose per kg and per day, worked out in mg and, for a liquid, in mL; over the maximum is severe), the latest eGFR (NSAIDs and metformin thresholds), and age 65 or over (a small Beers subset as moderate). Missing context (no weight, no eGFR) is reported as "not checked" with the reason, never as safe. The rule set version is raised and recorded with each check and override.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A seeded set (ibuprofen at 24 weeks, paracetamol 15 mg/kg at 14.2 kg = 213 mg = 8.9 mL of 120 mg/5 mL, diclofenac tablets with eGFR 52 and losartan, diazepam at 76) gives the expected finding in every case (automated test).
* A child dose without a weight from the last month is not checked, and says so.
* Each new finding is mutation checked: the test fails when the rule is removed.
* shortcut: a curated pilot rule set waiting for the clinical safety reviewer (MDV-P2-028); a licensed knowledge base later.

Summary: Consultation on one page (E-04 redesign) with the guided steps kept as an option
Description: The consultation opens as one page: the patient strip with life stage and allergies, the recording consent bar first (patient agreed, declined so the doctor types, consent withdrawn while listening), then numbered sections Vitals, History, the adaptive template (MDV-P2-042), Examination, Assessment, Plan (MDV-P2-043) and Review and sign (MDV-P2-044), with a section bar that stays at the top and ticks each finished section. A switch flips to the existing guided steps; nothing of the old flow is lost. The right panel has Assist suggestions, a chart summary and the checklist.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The one-page and guided views save the same note; switching keeps every typed word (autosave as today).
* The section bar is a nav landmark with links that move focus to the section; ticks are icon and words.
* Declined consent hides Assist and keeps the manual note path as today.
* Desktop two columns, phone one column, Arabic right to left, axe clean.

Summary: Structured review of systems and examination, and a template chosen by the patient
Description: New template versions add a review of systems (each symptom yes or no, unanswered stays blank) and an examination by body system (Normal, Abnormal with a note, Not examined). The consultation suggests a template from the life stage and problems: diabetes review for diabetes, antenatal for a pregnancy, paediatrics for a child and a new older-adult review (standing blood pressure, walking test, frailty, home safety) for an older adult; the doctor can change it. Released versions stay pinned on old notes. The signed note and its PDF show the structured answers in words.
Acceptance Criteria:
* An unanswered symptom or system stays blank in the signed note; nothing defaults to normal.
* Abnormal needs a note; Not examined is printed as such.
* The suggested template is tested per life stage, and the doctor's choice wins.
* Old notes keep their template version (fingerprint test unchanged for released versions).

Summary: Plan section: medicine actions, tests to order, advice in the patient's language, follow-up and referral
Description: The plan shows the prescription with an action per medicine: continue, new, change (new dose), taper (a stepped dose with an end date) or stop, using the reconciliation and the composer. Tests are toggles that create draft orders. Advice for the patient is written once and printed and sent in the patient's language when a reviewed translation exists, otherwise in English with a note. Follow-up is a choice (for example 2 weeks, 1 month, 3 months) that the front desk sees as a booking to make. Referral opens the existing referral letter.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Change and taper are recorded on the reconciliation with the old and new dose and print on the prescription.
* A test toggled on creates a draft order once; toggling off removes the draft, not an ordered one.
* The follow-up choice appears on the front desk's list for that patient.

Summary: Review and sign checklist: signing stays locked until every item is reviewed
Description: The checklist: identity confirmed, allergies reconciled, medicines reconciled, recording consent recorded, history reviewed, every AI suggestion accepted or dismissed, diagnoses reviewed and plan reviewed. The Sign button stays locked and says how many items remain. The server refuses a signature while an AI draft or suggestion is still undecided or consent is unrecorded, so the lock is not only the screen. After signing, changes go in as an addendum, as today.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Signing with an undecided AI suggestion is refused by the server (test, mutation checked).
* The remaining count and each item are announced to screen readers.
* The checklist state is derived from the note, never stored separately.

Summary: J2 journey steps for the one-page chart, Add medicine and the one-page consultation on the real stack
Description: Add J2 steps: the doctor opens Meera's one-page chart, adds a medicine from the chart into the open consultation and sees the allergy block for amoxicillin, writes the one-page consultation and signs after the checklist. Green on the real stack, English and Arabic, axe clean.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The new J2 steps are in docs/02-design/journeys.md and green in the full-stack run.
* The steps check the amoxicillin allergy block and the locked Sign until the checklist is complete.

Summary: Token slip: a small printable slip and Reprint; the display names the doctor per token after a reassignment
Labels: phase-P2 front-desk queue print tv epic-ux-programme track-safety wave-s3
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S3. This is audit backlog UX-23 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Walk-in success, board card menu, queue display · receptionist.
Findings and reviewers: F-15 · reviewer A-12.
Rationale: Tokens cannot be printed, reissued or cancelled; the desk speaks or writes the number by hand. After a reassignment, tokens B-01 and A-09 sat in the other doctor's queue and the display did not say whose they were.
Proposed UX behaviour: After check-in, Print slip opens a small print view: clinic name, token, doctor's name, date and time, and nothing else about the patient (no name, MRN, phone or reason). Reprint is on the card menu. A cancelled or left-without-being-seen visit's token is void and cannot be reprinted. After a reassignment the queue display shows the doctor beside each token.
Prototype and blueprint reference: None.
Components and tokens affected: A print view in the house print style; card menu. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Front end; small back end if the display needs the doctor per token.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the queue-rule ticket.
Clinical sign-off: Decision required before work starts: question 13 of the validation plan (paper token or spoken number). If spoken is enough, only the display part is built.
Effort and regression risk: M · Low.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) A thermal printer integration. (2) Kiosk self check-in (MDV-P8-006).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a checked-in visit, when the slip is printed, then it shows clinic, token, doctor, date and time and no name, MRN, phone or reason, and the test fails if a name is added
* Given a waiting visit, when Reprint is chosen from the card menu, then the same token prints
* Given a cancelled visit, when Reprint is tried, then it is not offered and the server refuses
* Given a reassigned token, when the queue display renders, then the doctor's name is beside the token and no patient name appears
* Given the walk-in path, when it is measured without printing, then it is still at most 6 clicks new and 3 returning
* Given the slip view, when axe runs in English and Arabic, then there is no violation and it has one h1

Summary: After the identity step-up the doctor returns to the section that asked, with focus on its button
Labels: phase-P2 auth prescribing signing a11y epic-ux-programme track-safety wave-s3
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S3. This is audit backlog UX-24 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Authorise prescription → identity provider → back to /consult/:id · doctor.
Findings and reviewers: F-25 · reviewer A-14.
Rationale: After confirming identity the page was at the top (scrollY 0), the prescription out of view, and Authorise had to be found and pressed a second time.
Proposed UX behaviour: The step-up remembers which action asked (authorise, sign, place orders, offboard) as an opaque key, not patient data. On return the page scrolls to that section, focuses its button and says Identity confirmed. Press Authorise. The action is not completed automatically: the doctor still presses the button, so authorising stays a deliberate act.
Prototype and blueprint reference: None.
Components and tokens affected: The step-up return handler; a status line. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Front end. Tested with real Entra on Azure dev.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None. Easier to verify after the Azure redeploy ticket.
Clinical sign-off: Not required.
Effort and regression risk: S · Low. The return address must not carry patient data.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Auto-completing the pending action. (2) Changing the step-up window.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a doctor who pressed Authorise and confirmed identity, when the page returns, then the prescription section is in view and focus is on Authorise
* Given the return, when the status is read by sight or screen reader, then it says identity was confirmed and what to press
* Given the return, when nothing is pressed, then nothing is authorised
* Given the round trip, when every address and the provider's state value are read, then they hold only opaque identifiers
* Given Azure dev, when the founder runs the path with MFA, then the return lands on the section
* Given English and Arabic, when axe runs after the return, then there is no violation

Summary: Nurse intake: one confirmation for all flagged readings, and a correction with a reason until the doctor starts
Labels: phase-P2 nurse vitals clinical safety epic-ux-programme track-safety wave-s3 needs-clinical-sign-off
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S3. This is audit backlog UX-25 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: /nurse/:id at 1024 touch · nurse.
Findings and reviewers: F-28 · reviewers A-18, A-20.
Rationale: BP 168/96, pulse 104 and temperature 39.2 each needed Keep this value: four taps before hand-off, most for the sickest patients; habitual tapping weakens the check. After hand-off a mistyped weight cannot be corrected.
Proposed UX behaviour: When several readings are flagged, one panel lists them in words with their ranges and one confirmation, I re-checked these readings, covers all; each can still be re-measured singly. Until the doctor starts the consultation, the nurse may correct a reading with a reason; the earlier value is kept with who and when, and the doctor sees the corrected value marked corrected. After the doctor starts, readings are fixed as today. The ranges and flags themselves do not change here.
Prototype and blueprint reference: None (the concept did not design nurse intake).
Components and tokens affected: Intake vitals form; Banner for the flagged list. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Front end and back end (the correction with history and its window).
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by a person: the vitals ranges sign-off (issue #956) comes first.
Clinical sign-off: Required before merge: question 16 of the validation plan (clinician and nurse), recorded on the issue with a date.
Effort and regression risk: M · Medium: a clinical check is being made lighter; do not ship without the sign-off.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Changing vitals ranges or flags. (2) A vitals form for a nurse when nurse intake is switched off (a product decision recorded on the navigation names ticket). (3) Nurse intake on a phone.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given three flagged readings, when the nurse confirms once, then all three are kept and the record shows each was confirmed
* Given the flagged list, when the nurse re-measures one, then only that reading changes
* Given a handed-off intake and a consultation not yet started, when the nurse corrects the weight with a reason, then the new value shows marked corrected and the old one is kept with who and when
* Given a started consultation, when a correction is sent, then the server refuses it, and the test fails if that rule is removed
* Given a flagged reading, when it renders, then High or Low and the range are text, not colour alone
* Given 1024 touch in English and Arabic, when axe runs, then there is no violation and every control is at least 44 px

Summary: Signed note print: vitals, allergies and diagnoses by default, and a page heading
Labels: phase-P2 notes print signing clinical a11y epic-ux-programme track-safety wave-s3 needs-clinical-sign-off
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S3. This is audit backlog UX-26 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: /consult/:id/note/print · doctor.
Findings and reviewers: F-27 · reviewer A-16, lead arbiter.
Rationale: The print shows identity and the note sections but not the nurse's vitals, the allergy, the coded diagnosis or the medicines; vitals enter only if the doctor pressed Add to Objective. The legal record of the visit may be thinner than the doctor believes. The page has no h1 (the only axe finding on 615 pages).
Proposed UX behaviour: The print of a signed note includes, by default and from what was recorded at signing: vitals with their time and source, the allergy state in words (recorded, not recorded, or no known allergies), coded diagnoses, and the medicines authorised in that visit by reference to the prescription. It has a page heading with clinic, doctor and licence line. The signed note itself is not edited: the print reads the signed version and the data linked to it at signing; anything added later appears only through an addendum.
Prototype and blueprint reference: None.
Components and tokens affected: NotePrintPage and the server PDF (QuestPDF) if the note has one. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Back end and front end.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None in code.
Clinical sign-off: Required before merge: question 9 of the validation plan (what the visit record and the printed prescription must contain), recorded on the issue with a date.
Effort and regression risk: M · Low to medium: signed records are immutable; the print must never show data newer than the signature without saying so.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) The prescription print (its own sign-off, #1097). (2) Editing a signed note.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a signed note for a visit with nurse vitals, a penicillin allergy and a coded diagnosis, when it is printed, then all three are on the print with their sources
* Given allergies not recorded at signing, when the note is printed, then it says not recorded and never none
* Given a vital corrected after signing, when the note is printed, then the print shows the value as at signing, and the test fails if later data replaces it silently
* Given the print view at five widths, when axe runs, then there is no violation and the page has one h1
* Given the issue, when it is closed, then it holds the pilot doctor's dated agreement on the contents
* Given English and Arabic, when the print renders, then it mirrors and prints on A4 at 200 % zoom without loss

Summary: Audit log: every action has a plain name; the default view is chart opens and changes
Labels: phase-P2 audit i18n ux settings epic-ux-programme track-safety wave-s3
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S3. This is audit backlog UX-28 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Settings → Security → Audit log · owner, practice admin.
Findings and reviewers: F-31 · reviewers A-24, C-24.
Rationale: The action filter lists Appointment booked beside encounter.end, rx.check and patient.chart.allergy-flag; one load of Today writes a row per patient. An owner asked who opened this chart reads developer codes among hundreds of rows.
Proposed UX behaviour: Every action code has a name in English, Hindi and Arabic; a code with no name fails a unit test, so a new action cannot ship unnamed. The log opens on Opened or changed a chart; routine list reads sit behind a filter (All activity). Nothing is removed from the log or the export: this changes the view only.
Prototype and blueprint reference: None.
Components and tokens affected: Audit log table and filter; i18n keys. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Front end and translations. The audit store is untouched.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None.
Clinical sign-off: Not required. The owner tries it in the session (owner scenario step 4).
Effort and regression risk: S · Low. The log's content and integrity are unchanged.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Compact rows, paging and sort (the table ticket). (2) Any change to what is audited.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the audit log and its filter, when every row and option is read, then none shows a dotted developer code
* Given a new audit action with no translation, when the unit test runs, then it fails
* Given the log opened fresh, when the rows are read, then they are chart opens and changes, and All activity shows the rest
* Given the export, when it is downloaded, then it holds every row regardless of the view
* Given English, Hindi and Arabic, when the log renders, then names are translated and axe finds no violation in English and Arabic

Summary: Navigation names in one batch: My day, Front desk, one Patient record with tabs, Register patient as a button
Labels: phase-P2 navigation i18n ux training epic-ux-programme track-design wave-d3
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D3. This is audit backlog UX-18 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Navigation and page titles · all roles.
Findings and reviewers: F-32 · reviewers C-07, A-20.

The desk surface is Front desk in the menu and the title, with By status and By doctor as views inside it. Patients is a real page; a row opens one Patient record whose tabs depend on capability: Summary (clinicians), Details (desk), Timeline, Documents. Register patient leaves the menu and becomes a button on Front desk and Patients and a search action. Menu order per role follows blueprint section 3. Route addresses do not change; old addresses keep working. Effort and regression risk: M · Medium: staff have learned the current names; tests and training material name them.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Changing route addresses. (2) Changing what any role may see. (3) The account menu and rail labels (already landed).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given every role, when the menu and each page title are read, then the doctor's day is My day, the desk surface is Front desk, and no screen has two names
* Given a nurse with intake off, when the menu renders, then no two items open the same screen
* Given a doctor and a receptionist opening the same patient, when the record opens, then both see Patient record, the doctor with Summary and the receptionist with Details, and the receptionist's tabs hold no clinical data
* Given Front desk and Patients, when each renders, then Register patient is a button there and not a menu item, and the walk-in path is still at most 6 clicks new and 3 returning

* Given the issue, when it is merged, then it records the training date and that the merge is before training or after the first pilot weeks

* Given a needs-attention line, when its action is pressed, then the matching screen opens filtered to that item
* Given the board and the doctors' days, when the counts are compared at the same moment, then they are equal
* Given a receptionist or another clinic's owner, when the page's API is called, then the server answers 403 or returns only their own clinic, and the test fails if the policy is removed
* Given the page and its API answers, when they are read, then they hold counts and staff names only

Summary: Tables: one controller for sort and paging, stacked rows on phones, and compact density for four reference tables only

Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D3. This is audit backlog UX-30 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Staff, audit log, formulary, order sets (compact allowed); every other table (controller, paging, stacked rows).
Findings and reviewers: F-24 · reviewers C-06, C-13.
Rationale: Staff rows are about 69 px (7 per screen); the audit table starts 800 px down a 4,192 px page; 2 of 19 tables can be sorted; 10 rely on sideways scrolling on phones, which can hide dose or identity columns.
Proposed UX behaviour: A shared table controller hook for sort, filter and paging state (the pattern AGENTS.md section 4 already asks for), adopted one table at a time, audit log and staff first. Sort on the columns people sort by (name, time, wait). Paging above 50 rows. Under 768 px a table becomes stacked rows and never scrolls sideways with hidden columns that carry dose or identity. Numbers right-aligned with tabular numerals; the identifying cell bold and nothing else; one visible row action, the rest in a menu. Compact density (36 px rows) is an explicit per-table prop allowed only on the audit log, formulary, order sets and staff list; it is ignored on any device that reports a coarse pointer (any-pointer: coarse), and a destructive action inside a compact table (Offboard, Remove) stays 44 px or asks to confirm. AGENTS.md section 4 is amended in the same change, as the house rule requires for any row under 44 px.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/08-design-system-blueprint.md sections 4 and 9.
Components and tokens affected: table.tsx (density prop, stacked variant), a table controller in web/clinic/src/features/table, pagination. Density tokens.
Front end and back end split: Front end only. Server paging only where a list is already paged.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the library-defaults and token tickets. Timing: after the first pilot weeks, or before the first staff training session if the founder moves it there; never between training and the first two pilot weeks (arbitration ruling 6).
Clinical sign-off: Question 20 of the validation plan (mouse or touch at the desk and in the office) informs it. Compact on any clinical list would need clinical sign-off and is not in scope.
Effort and regression risk: L · Medium: many tables; one table per pull request.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Compact density on the patient directory, patient pickers, medicine lines, the front-desk list or any row that changes state (forbidden by ruling 2). (2) Virtual scrolling. (3) New table features nobody asked for.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the density prop, when it is set on a table other than audit log, formulary, order sets or staff, then the build or lint fails
* Given a compact table on a device with a coarse pointer, when it renders, then rows are 48 px
* Given the audit log at 1440 by 900 with a mouse, when it opens, then at least 15 rows are visible and the table starts in the first 300 px
* Given staff and audit log, when a sortable header is used by keyboard, then the order changes, the sort state is announced, and lists over 50 rows are paged
* Given any table at 375 px, when it renders, then there is no sideways scrolling and no dose or identity field is hidden
* Given Offboard in the compact staff table, when it is measured, then it is at least 44 px or opens a confirmation
* Given AGENTS.md section 4, when this change merges, then it names the four tables and the coarse-pointer rule
* Given English and Arabic, when axe runs on each migrated table, then there is no violation and every scrollable region has a label

Summary: Truthful status and small motion: an Updated mark on live board changes, skeletons, an offline strip, named transition properties
Labels: phase-P2 ui a11y realtime design-system epic-ux-programme track-design wave-d3
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D3. This is audit backlog UX-32 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Board, My day, schedule, patient record (skeletons and live mark); packages/ui switch, tabs, button.
Findings and reviewers: F-36, F-47 · reviewers B-15, B-23, B-24. WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages for the live mark.
Rationale: A card changed by someone else arrives with no cue. Pages show a Loading sentence, then the layout appears and the height jumps (900 to 2,074 px on the board). The offline card covers the Done column and talks about recordings. No animation is needed; a few truthful status cues are.
Proposed UX behaviour: In this order. (1) Replace transition-all on Switch and Tabs with named properties and stop the focus ring fading in. (2) A board card or My day row changed by someone else gets the text tag Updated for 5 seconds and is announced in the existing live region; with motion allowed its background also fades from the brand tint to white over 1,200 ms; no movement. (3) Skeletons in the final layout for the board, My day, schedule and a record page: shown only after 200 ms, opacity pulse over 1,200 ms, static blocks under reduced motion. (4) Offline is a 40 px strip under the top bar with wording for the screen (Offline. The board shows the last update from 10:31. Actions are paused.). (5) The global reduced-motion rule allows colour and opacity changes up to 150 ms and no transforms. Never: page transitions, cards sliding between columns, staggered lists, animating the Ctrl+K search, anything that moves while a doctor types, animated counters, toasts over the patient strip.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/08-design-system-blueprint.md section 12 (the motion table and its values).
Components and tokens affected: New Skeleton in packages/ui; switch.tsx, tabs.tsx, button.tsx; the motion tokens; the connectivity banner.
Front end and back end split: Front end only.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the SaveStatus ticket, the token ticket (motion values) and the board chrome ticket. Timing: after the first pilot weeks, or before the first staff training session if the founder moves it there; never between training and the first two pilot weeks (arbitration ruling 6). Item 2 may be pulled forward before the pilot if the device check shows two people share one board.
Clinical sign-off: Not required.
Effort and regression risk: S to M · Low, as long as nothing in the never list is added.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Everything in the never list. (2) A motion library. (3) Press feedback and drawer animation beyond what Sheet already has.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given two people on one board, when one moves a card, then the other sees the tag Updated on that card for 5 seconds and a screen reader announces it once
* Given the Updated mark and the skeletons, when they play, then no element changes position, and under reduced motion there is no fade
* Given the board on a slow connection, when data arrives, then the layout height changes by less than 10 % from the skeleton
* Given the board offline, when the strip shows, then it names the last update time, covers no column and does not mention recordings
* Given a button, when it is focused by keyboard, then the ring is at full colour on the first frame, and no library component uses transition-all
* Given the change, when it is reviewed, then no page transition, sliding card, staggered list, animated counter or toast was added
* Given English and Arabic, when axe runs with skeletons and the strip showing, then there is no violation

Summary: Apply the type and width tokens: stray font sizes removed, body weight 500, page maximum 1,600 px, reading width, no sm:grid-cols

Findings and reviewers: F-21 · reviewers B-11, B-18, C-05, C-11, C-16. Part 2 of 2 of audit backlog UX-29 (part 1 defined the tokens).

The ratchet counts for arbitrary font sizes and sm:grid-cols fall to zero and their lint rules turn to error (queue display and print stay on the allow-list).
