* Given Arabic is selected, when the app restarts, then layout is right-to-left while dates and phone numbers stay left-to-right.
* Given a string is hard-coded in a component, when lint runs, then the build fails.
* Given the tokens file changes, when web and native build, then both pick up the same colours and spacing.

Summary: Mobile backend: native token sign-in, device registry, push registry and remote revoke
Description: Server side for native clients: OIDC code + PKCE token endpoints, refresh rotation, patient sign-in by mobile number + SMS code, device registration (device key, platform, app version), push token registry, per-device and all-device revoke (feeds the 'My devices' screen and staff offboarding MDV-P1-009), rate limits and audit. Every endpoint declares a policy; tenant isolation unchanged.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a staff member is offboarded, when the owner confirms, then every mobile session and push token of that person is revoked at once.
* Given a refresh token is replayed, when the server sees it twice, then the whole token family is revoked and the event is audited.
* Given a wrong SMS code is entered five times, when the limit is reached, then the number is locked for a period and the patient is told in plain words.
* Given a lost phone is reported, when the user revokes it in My devices, then the next request from that device is refused.

Summary: Staff app: sign-in, 15-minute biometric lock, Today, queue, patient search and patient summary
Description: Staff app: work email + passkey or code, choose facility, Face ID / fingerprint unlock after a 15-minute lock with PIN fallback and switch user, Today with next patient hero, queue with tokens and 'via app' marks, privacy-safe patient search, patient summary (allergy never by colour alone), offline banner with read-only last copy, role-based tabs (5 maximum). Same capabilities and care-relationship rules as the web app, enforced by the API.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the app is idle for 15 minutes, when it is opened again, then it asks for Face ID, fingerprint or PIN before showing anything.
* Given a receptionist signs in, when the tabs load, then clinical-only tabs are absent and their API calls return 403.
* Given the phone is offline, when the doctor opens Today, then the last copy shows with an offline banner and no edit action.
* Given a patient has an allergy, when the summary opens, then the allergy shows as text and icon, not colour alone.
* Given the staff app is open, when someone takes a screenshot, then Android blocks it and iOS blurs the app switcher and audits the screenshot (ADR-011 §6).
* Given the phone is revoked or the user switches, when the app next talks to the server, then the encrypted store is wiped and nothing of the previous user remains (ADR-011 §3, §5).

Summary: Staff app: consent script, background recording with offline queue, AI note review and sign
Description: Consult flow on the phone: ask-first consent script (agree / decline to manual note), recording with a visible indicator and background audio, chunk upload with retry and an encrypted offline queue, draft note with per-field accept, sign with biometrics. AI output stays a draft until the licensed doctor accepts each field and signs. Prescribing stays on the web app at launch (the design says so).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the doctor declines recording, when the patient says no, then the app opens the manual note and records nothing.
* Given the network drops mid-recording, when it returns, then queued chunks upload in order and none is lost or duplicated.
* Given an AI draft field, when the doctor has not accepted it, then the note cannot be signed.
* Given the phone is lost, when the queue held audio, then it is encrypted and removed on remote revoke.
* Given unsent audio was wiped by a revoke, when the visit is opened on the web, then it is flagged 'recording incomplete: write the note by hand' (ADR-011 §4).

Summary: Patient app: SMS sign-in, family profiles, home, booking, check-in and reschedule
Description: Patient app (indigo): mobile number + SMS code (iOS one-time-code autofill, Android SMS Retriever), then biometric or PIN; 'who is this for' with family profiles and proxy access that is explicit, time-limited and visible; home with next visit, to-do list and emergency line; book (doctor, visit type, date, time, fee line), confirmation with add-to-calendar, check-in and reschedule; last copy offline, bookings queued. Same booking service and no-double-booking rule as reception.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a patient books from the app, when a reception booking takes the same slot, then only one succeeds and the other sees the next free slots.
* Given a family member is viewed, when the proxy has expired, then access ends and the patient sees why.
* Given the phone is offline, when the patient books, then the booking is queued and shown as not yet confirmed.
* Given the SMS code arrives, when the patient opens the app, then the code is filled in automatically on iOS and Android.
* Given a rooted or jailbroken phone, when the patient app starts, then it warns and keeps working; the staff app refuses to sign in (ADR-011 §7).

Summary: Patient app: results, prescriptions, messages, consents, payments and video visit
Description: Records the patient may see (signed summaries and reviewed results only, plain words, never AI drafts), prescriptions with QR, clinic messages (with the 'not for emergencies' rule), consents and family access, payment sheet (UPI, cards; Apple Pay in UAE) marked paid only when the bank or gateway confirms, receipts to Records and WhatsApp, and the video-visit join screen (camera and microphone check). Video joins only when teleconsultation (MDV-P8-002) is switched on for the clinic; until then the entry is hidden by flag.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a result is not reviewed, when the patient opens Records, then it shows as pending, not as a value.
* Given a payment, when the bank has not confirmed, then the invoice is not marked paid.
* Given a draft AI note exists, when the patient opens Records, then nothing of it is visible.
* Given video visits are not enabled for the clinic, when the patient opens the app, then no video entry is shown.

Summary: Private push notifications for both apps (IDs only, no health text on the lock screen)
Description: APNs and FCM through Azure Notification Hubs in the tenant's country. Payloads carry an opaque ID and the fixed text 'You have an update from your clinic'; the app fetches the detail after unlock. Per-user opt-in and quiet hours; failures visible in the staff notification centre (MDV-P1-034).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a result is ready, when a push is sent, then the payload holds an ID and the fixed text and no test, doctor speciality or result.
* Given the user turns notifications off, when an event happens, then no push is sent and the in-app list still shows it.
* Given a push token is revoked, when an event happens, then no push goes to that device.

Summary: Store release: accounts, privacy labels, MASVS test, accessibility and RTL checks, EAS Update policy
Description: Apple and Google developer accounts under the company; privacy labels and data-safety forms matching the data map; MASVS L1 review plus root/jailbreak and screenshot rules; TestFlight and closed testing with a pilot clinic; accessibility (screen reader labels, 200 % text) and en/hi/ar checks; EAS Update limited to UI fixes while clinical logic ships with store builds and release notes.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a build, when it is submitted, then privacy labels match the data map.
* Given the MASVS review, when it finishes, then no open high or critical finding.
* Given an OTA update, when it contains clinical logic, then the pipeline refuses it.

Summary: Platform console shell (`web/platform-admin`): company sign-on plus security key, platform roles, reason on every action, no PHI
Description: Separate app and host for the Medvya team: company SSO then a security key (no passwords, no shared accounts), lost-key recovery by a second owner with a one-hour link, roles (owner, operations, support, finance, reviewer), quarterly access review, nav of 16 pages, every action needs a reason and is logged to an append-only platform audit log that can be exported. The console reads only the control plane: tenant catalogue, plan, routing and counts; it never shows patient records (data map and architecture test).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a Medvya user, when signs in without a security key, then access is refused.
* Given a platform action, when is taken without a reason, then it is rejected.
* Given any console endpoint, when returns data, then it holds no patient field (architecture test).
* Given a key is lost, when another owner verifies on a video call, then a one-hour link is issued, the old key is revoked and both steps are logged.

Summary: Feature rollouts: staged release (internal, beta tenants, percentage, everyone), kill switch and clinical sign-off gate
Description: Extends the per-tenant flags (MDV-P0-028) with stages and a percentage, owner and description, and a one-click 'turn off for all' that hides a feature without deleting data. A clinical feature (recording, AI notes, e-prescriptions) cannot reach 'everyone' until clinical sign-off is recorded. Plans decide who is entitled; flags decide what is on.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a clinical flag, when is moved to everyone without sign-off, then the change is refused.
* Given the kill switch, when is used, then the feature disappears for all tenants and no data is deleted.
* Given a flag change, when is made, then it is audited with a reason.

Summary: Plans and entitlements: versioned plans, India and UAE prices, seats, trial days, 30 days' notice
Description: Plans (Clinic with one doctor ₹1,999 per month; Clinic ₹3,499 per doctor per month; Hospital custom) with separate INR and AED prices, seats, trial days and the feature list. An edit creates a new plan version: new subscriptions use it now, existing ones at renewal with 30 days' notice. Removing a feature never deletes data. Entitlements are read by the feature gate.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a plan is edited, when it is saved, then a new version exists and current subscribers keep the old one until renewal.
* Given a price changes, when a subscriber exists, then they are notified 30 days before it applies.
* Given a feature is removed from a plan, when data exists, then the data stays.

Summary: Subscription billing in the console and for owners: invoices, payment method, add seats, dunning ladder, close practice
Description: Owner screens: plan and seats, invoices from Medvya, update payment method, add seats, close the practice (full export first). Console: INR and AED reported separately, never summed. Dunning: retries day 3 and 7, reminder day 14, limited mode day 30 (online bookings pause), read-only day 60, suspended day 90; patients and clinical records are never locked for non-payment. Only the owner sees plan and billing.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a payment fails, when day 30 is reached, then online bookings pause and clinicians can still read and treat.
* Given a non-owner, when opens billing, then the API returns 403.
* Given a practice is closed, when the owner confirms, then a full export is offered first and the plan stops at the end of the paid period.

Summary: Organisation approval console: onboarding request queue, document view, approve, ask for changes, reject, suspend
Description: Superseded scope (ADR-016): the reviewer queue lists organisation onboarding requests (type Clinic or Hospital, country, submitted date, documents, state), not doctors. The reviewer opens the uploaded documents, then approves, asks for changes with a plain reason, rejects with a reason, or later suspends an approved organisation. The queue reads only the control-plane request and documents through its own narrow, reviewed read path (ADR-014), never patient data. Extends the simple queue and documented API built in MDV-P1-064 (documents view, suspension, reviewer roles).  The design (10 Nov 2026) now shows this screen: queue filters Waiting, Needs changes, Decided, All; detail with profile, documents with checks, decision, reason, email preview and history.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given an organisation is Submitted, when a reviewer approves it, then reviewer, documents checked and time are recorded and the organisation can register patients.
* Given a reviewer asks for changes or rejects, when it is saved, then the applicant gets the reason in plain words by email and on the status page.
* Given an organisation is suspended, when staff sign in, then new registration, booking and signing are refused and existing records stay readable for care.
* Given a Hospital request without a signed DPA, when a reviewer tries to approve, then the server refuses and offers Ask for changes (design 10 Nov 2026).
* Given a Suspended organisation, when operations or a reviewer reinstates it with a reason, then it is Approved again and the owner is emailed.
* Given a support or finance user, when they open a request, then they can read it but approve, ask for changes, reject and suspend are refused with 403.
* Given a document, when a reviewer opens it, then it shows in a watermarked viewer with no download and the view is logged.
* Given any queue endpoint, when it returns data, then it holds no patient field (architecture test); every action needs a reason.

Summary: Releases and What's new, maintenance and incident banners, integrations register
Description: Announcements linked to a flag and shown when the flag reaches the tenant (in-app What's new, owner email, never to patients). Planned maintenance and incident messages per region as banners in the clinic app and on the public status page (MDV-P5-018). Integrations register per country (NHCX, DHA eClaimLink, Shafafiya, Riayati, payment gateways, ABDM, WhatsApp) with status, read-only.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a flag reaches a tenant, when an announcement is linked, then it shows in What's new only then.
* Given maintenance is scheduled for India, when the time comes, then only India practices see the banner.
* Given the register, when is opened, then it shows each integration's status and country.

Summary: Legal documents: versioned terms, privacy notice and DPA, re-acceptance gate that pauses booking only
Description: Counsel writes the wording and uploads it; staff can only publish an approved version, never edit text. A new version can require every owner to accept again; until they do only online booking pauses, nothing clinical stops (the existing terms gate is reused). Acceptance is recorded with who, version and time.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a new version requires acceptance, when an owner has not accepted, then online booking pauses and clinical work continues.
* Given platform staff, when try to edit wording, then the console offers no edit, only publish.
* Given an owner accepts, when it is saved, then user, version and time are recorded.

Summary: Service requests: Help in the clinic app, support inbox with SLA, internal notes, diagnostics
Description: Clinic side: search help first, raise a request with category and description, warning not to include patient details, screenshots blurred where patient data appears, app version and recent errors attached. Console side: inbox with SLA timer, assignee, public replies and internal notes, 'request support access' that needs the owner's approval, lasts 60 minutes and shows no patient records. Support hours and urgent-outage line shown.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a screenshot shows patient data, when it is attached, then the patient data is blurred before storage.
* Given support, when asks for access, then nothing is visible until the owner approves and it ends after 60 minutes.
* Given a request breaches its SLA, when time passes, then it is flagged to the team lead.

Summary: Platform analytics, practice health score and scheduled reports with small-count hiding
Description: Aggregated adoption and usage by practice, staff and patients with no patient data; any count under 5 is hidden. Health score from usage, payments, support tickets and errors, with a reason and a next step. Reports (metrics, daily/weekly/monthly, PDF or CSV) sent to named people only. Reuses the PHI-free reporting store decided in MDV-P4-029.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a count is 4, when the chart renders, then it shows as hidden.
* Given a report, when is scheduled, then only the named recipients get it and it holds no patient data.
* Given a practice's health score falls, when it is shown, then the reasons are listed.

Summary: Data requests and offboarding runs from the console without opening records
Description: Queue of export, correction, erasure and practice-closure requests from owners. Closure: full export first, records kept under a hold for the legal retention period, then deleted with a certificate; region never changes. Operations run the jobs and see counts and status only, never records.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a closure is requested, when it is approved, then a full export is delivered before any retention clock starts.
* Given retention ends, when the job runs, then records are deleted and a certificate is stored.
* Given an operator, when opens a request, then no record content is shown.

Summary: Public pricing page with 14-day trial, monthly and yearly toggle and country currency
Description: Pricing page on the public site reading the approved plans (MDV-P5-042): Solo, Clinic (most popular), Hospital (talk to us), monthly and yearly toggle with the yearly saving, ₹ or AED by region, 'prices approved' line, payment methods by country. 'Start free trial' goes to sign-up (MDV-P1-004) with the plan chosen. No card needed to start unless the pricing decision says otherwise. Also the 6 Nov blocks: Compare plans table (Solo, Clinic, Hospital), the Medvya Assist add-on per doctor, "If a payment fails" (nothing locks for 30 days; records are never locked and can always be exported) and free migration. Until the console plans exist (MDV-P5-042), the approved plans are read from a versioned file in PublicSite (like trust-centre.json), recorded as a shortcut.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a visitor in the UAE, when opens pricing, then prices show in AED with Apple Pay and cards listed.
* Given a visitor, when chooses Clinic and starts a trial, then sign-up opens with that plan.
* Given a price changes in the console, when the page reloads, then the new price shows.
* Given JavaScript is off, when the monthly or yearly choice is made, then the prices switch (plain links or a form, no script); axe is clean in en, hi and ar.

Summary: Patient app trackers: BP and sugar log, a child's growth and vaccines, and a private cycle tracker (PT-09)
Description: Records gains a Trackers tab: the patient's BP and fasting sugar log (patient-reported observations the doctor sees on the chart, labelled as patient reported), a managed child's growth curve, next vaccine and milestone questions, and a cycle tracker (period days, predicted next period and fertile days as estimates, averages, log a period or symptoms). Cycle data is private to the patient: never visible to family members or proxies, and shared with the doctor only when she opts in; pregnancy pauses it.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A reading logged in the app shows on the chart's trend as patient reported.
* A proxy or family member never sees another person's cycle data (server test, mutation checked).
* Sharing cycle history with the clinic is an explicit opt-in the patient can withdraw.
* Predictions carry the "estimate, not contraception or a diagnosis" text.

Summary: Platform console switches for the new chart sections and the patient-app trackers
Description: Feature switches per tenant for the pregnancy, child growth and older-adult chart modules and for the patient-app trackers, off until the clinical review of growth charts, vaccine schedules and drug rules is signed. The console's pending list shows that clinical review.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Each switch defaults off and is audited when changed.
* The chart and app hide a switched-off module and the server refuses its writes.

Summary: Fix the Expo bundling error, then run the same UX audit on the mobile apps in a simulator
Labels: phase-P5 mobile dependencies ux a11y epic-ux-programme track-safety wave-s3
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track S (safety, trust and handoff behaviour), wave S3. This is audit backlog UX-33 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: mobile/clinician and mobile/patient in Expo Go on a simulator.
Findings and reviewers: F-34 · reviewers C-20, C-21, B-25.
Rationale: pnpm dev:clinician then opening in Expo Go fails with Cannot find module @babel/helper-define-polyfill-provider, so nobody can run or review the mobile apps. From code only: native button borders at 1.25:1 and placeholders at 3.05:1, and web and native use different icons for the same status.
Proposed UX behaviour: Part 1: make the Babel helper resolvable in the workspace (dependency resolution only, pinned through the lockfile) so both apps bundle and open. Part 2: run the audit's method on a simulator for both apps and write the findings as tickets. Part 3, small and known: control borders use the input colour and placeholders ink600 in packages/ui-native so they meet 3:1 and 4.5:1; one icon mapping per status shared by web and native is recorded as a finding if not fixed here.
Prototype and blueprint reference: None.
Components and tokens affected: packages/ui-native controls; workspace dependency resolution.
Front end and back end split: Dependency and native front end.
Prerequisites and blocked by: None. Not in the pilot flow: the pilot runs on the web app.
Clinical sign-off: Not required.
Effort and regression risk: S · Low. A dependency change needs the reason in the pull request and pnpm audit clean.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Porting the web consolidation to ui-native. (2) Real data in the apps (MDV-P5-033). (3) Store builds.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given a clean checkout, when pnpm dev:clinician and the patient app are opened in Expo Go on a simulator, then each bundles and shows its first screen
* Given the running apps, when the audit is done, then its findings are tickets with evidence and synthetic data only

Summary: Later: date and time pickers and a combobox in the app language; dark and high contrast only after the tone tokens
Labels: phase-P5 design-system i18n a11y theme epic-ux-programme track-design wave-d3
Description:
Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D3. No audit backlog id. Created from the audit's rulings and blueprint, not from a backlog line (see Findings).

Persona and route: 34 native date and time inputs; the booking patient picker and Add medicine search · all roles.
Findings and reviewers: F-42 · reviewers C-18, C-19.
Rationale: Native date inputs follow the browser's language, not the app's: an Arabic screen can show an English-format date widget. Dark mode and high contrast are documented and not built; starting them before the tone layer means editing look tables by hand.
Proposed UX behaviour: DatePicker and TimePicker in packages/ui that follow the app language and direction, accept typed input, and replace the 34 native inputs; a Combobox for the patient and medicine pickers with the same keyboard behaviour as today's lists. Each new dependency, if any, is justified in the pull request. Dark and high-contrast themes stay in MDV-P5-023, which now depends on the tone-token ticket and must not start before it.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/08-design-system-blueprint.md section 7 (Later).
Components and tokens affected: New date-picker.tsx, time-picker.tsx, combobox.tsx.
Front end and back end split: Front end only.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the tone-token ticket and the table ticket. Later than every other ticket of the programme.
Clinical sign-off: Not required. Dates of birth and dose times are safety-relevant: typed entry must stay possible and unambiguous.
Effort and regression risk: L · Medium: date entry is on the registration and booking paths.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Dark and high-contrast themes themselves (MDV-P5-023). (2) Any calendar redesign.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Given the app in Arabic on a browser set to English, when a date field opens, then the picker is in Arabic, right-to-left, and the stored value is the same ISO date
* Given a date of birth field, when a date is typed by keyboard, then it is accepted without opening the picker and an impossible date is refused with a message
* Given features, when searched, then no input of type date or time remains
* Given the patient picker, when it is used by keyboard, then arrow keys, Enter and Escape work and each option is announced with name and date of birth
* Given the walk-in and registration paths, when measured, then the click counts did not rise
* Given English and Arabic, when axe runs with the picker open, then there is no violation

Summary: Hardware partner, device certification and regulated-device classification advice

Acceptance Criteria:
* Partner contract and BOM recorded; certification plan with dates.
* Written classification advice for the final intended use and marketing claims.
* Go/no-go decision recorded against the phone-capture metrics from P3.

Summary: Clip pairing with code match and microphone self-test (W-01)
Description: Hold button 3 s → LED pulses → companion shows 4-digit code that must match the clip's LED pattern → mic self-test ("say testing") → pair to the doctor (DEVICE_PAIRING valid 90 days). Clip becomes selectable at consent (A-02).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Pairing requires explicit code confirmation; mismatches abort and are logged.
* Pairing expires after 90 days and requires re-pairing.
* Self-test failure blocks pairing with guidance.
* Paired clip appears in A-02 device list with battery and firmware.

Summary: Clip capture bound to encounter and consent with visible recording light (capture FSM)
Description: Start/stop only for the verified current encounter with consent; device-bound session start with nonce; LED on throughout capture (firmware-enforced); chunks uploaded via phone relay or Wi-Fi with integrity hashes; never attachable to two encounters.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The clip cannot record without an active encounter + consent authorisation (server and firmware).
* LED is on whenever the microphone captures (hardware test).
* Replayed or out-of-sequence chunks are rejected.
* Device, consent and overlap test suites pass (exit gate 1).

Summary: Device health, battery, encrypted offline buffer, upload conflicts and staged firmware updates (W-02)
Description: Device page: battery %, BLE status, firmware version, encrypted offline queue ("2 recordings in encrypted queue"), Sync now, staged firmware update (1.4.2 → 1.5.0) with signed images and rollback/anti-rollback; upload conflict (same session on phone + clip) keeps both and the clinician picks.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Firmware updates only accept signed images; tampered images are rejected (test).
* Offline recordings stay encrypted on the device and sync later without loss (offline suite; exit gate 1).
* Battery lasts a full clinic day (≥ 8 h mixed use) in a field test (exit gate 2).
* Upload conflicts surface a choice and never silently merge.

Summary: Loss/theft revoke effective in under one minute (W-03)
Description: Revoke with reason (lost/stolen/retired): binding revoked, keys/tokens invalidated, queued audio on the device becomes unreadable, audit event and admin notification.
Acceptance Criteria:
* After revoke, the device cannot authenticate or upload within 60 seconds (exit gate 3 test).
* Revocation is audited and the admin notified.
* A revoked device must be re-provisioned to be used again.

Summary: Private voice assistant through earpiece only (A-07)
Description: Doctor taps or hotword to ask (e.g. "last eGFR"); answers shown as text first and spoken only through a connected private earpiece ("whisper mode"); if the earpiece disconnects, the assistant turns off; answers come only from the patient's verified chart with source.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The assistant never speaks through the room speaker; disconnecting the earpiece disables it immediately (test).
* Every answer cites its chart source; no diagnosis or treatment advice.
* Queries and answers are audited without storing audio beyond policy.

Summary: Multilingual notes: Arabic, English, Hindi and Malayalam incl. mixed-language consultations
Description: Extend transcription and drafting to Arabic and Malayalam (and mixed AR/EN, ML/EN, HI/EN) with original and translation side by side in transcript and evidence; per-language evaluation sets.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Per-language evaluation sets meet the same safety gate (0 fabricated medicines/doses).
* Transcript and evidence show original-language text beside the translation for each language.
* Language quality results are documented per language before enabling it per tenant.

Summary: Stronger AI QA: per-language evaluation sets, clinician trust metrics, red-team prompts on uploaded documents
Description: Per-language evaluation sets, ongoing clinician trust metrics, red-team prompt-injection tests against uploaded documents and transcripts, overlap/speaker suites for multi-speaker clip recordings.
Acceptance Criteria:
* CI runs per-language and red-team suites on every prompt/model change.
* Overlap and speaker-attribution suites pass for clip recordings (exit gate 1).
* Trust metrics are reported monthly per clinician cohort.

Summary: Outbound voice reminder and recall calls; waitlist fill from cancellations
Description: Automated reminder/recall calls for patients without WhatsApp, and calls/messages to waitlisted patients when a slot frees; same identity and safety rules as inbound.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Calls are placed only to patients with a consent/opt-in for calls.
* Waitlist fill offers slots in order and books only on explicit confirmation.
* Call outcomes are logged as contact attempts and never close care tasks by themselves.

Summary: Device kit, quick-start guide, fleet guide and R6 gate
Description: Device kit (clip, charger, quick-start), fleet guide for admins (assign, firmware rings, revoke), evidence for exit criteria, R6 release notes. Journey J4 (ward round with clip) passes.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Quick-start and fleet guides published; kits delivered to pilot doctors.
* Exit criteria evidence attached; R6 notes list exclusions (autonomous triage/diagnosis).
* Playwright/device test for J4 passes (with device simulator where needed).

Summary: Hospital procurement, HIS vendor engagement and integration contract

Acceptance Criteria:
* Signed hospital contract and integration specification (delivery package 1).
* Security review by the hospital passed (exit gate 1).

Summary: Hospital onboarding wizard and record authority per facility (H-08)

Per facility choose Medvya EMR or Existing HIS; statuses "HIS authoritative · write-back on" / "Medvya authoritative" / "HIS not connected yet"; mixed-authority warning; sets ENCOUNTER.authority_mode.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Authority is set per facility and stamped on every new encounter.
* With HIS authority, chart items show "Synced from HIS" and Medvya never creates a second authoritative chart.
* Mixed authority shows the attention banner and cross-facility views show source badges.

Summary: Organisation, facilities and departments administration (H-02)
Description: Facility tree with departments, beds/type metadata, authority badge, time zone; multi-location administration.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Facility scope drives every permission check (tests with cross-facility users).
* Departments are assignable to staff and encounters.

Summary: SSO (SAML/OIDC via Entra federation), SCIM provisioning and facility/department role grants with expiry (H-03)
Description: Federate hospital IdP; SSO-enforced tenant; SCIM create/update/deactivate users; grants table user × role × facility scope × expiry; locum grants with end dates; licence count; quarterly access review.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Deactivating a user in the hospital IdP removes Medvya access within the SCIM cycle.
* Role alone never grants another facility (tests).
* Expired grants end access automatically.
* An SSO-enforced tenant hides the one-time-code options and shows "Hospital staff? Sign in with SSO", chosen by a verified email domain or a tenant link without a lookup that reveals which organisations exist (moved from MDV-P0-011).

Summary: Hospital integration console: connection tiles for HIS, LIS, ABDM/HIE, SSO, messaging (H-01)

Acceptance Criteria:
* Tile status reflects real health checks and message flow.
* Secrets for connections live in Key Vault; rotation is audited.

Summary: FHIR R4 HIS interface and write-back queue with conflict review and retry (H-04)

Acceptance Criteria:
* Medvya never overwrites the HIS silently; conflicts always go to the clinician (test).
* Write-back success ≥ 99 % in the pilot with every failure/conflict visible (exit gate 2).
* Duplicate deliveries are prevented by idempotency keys.
* Attempts list shows timestamps and response codes without PHI in logs.

Summary: Lab feeds (HL7 v2 ORU/ORM over MLLP/VPN) and imaging viewer links (N-15)
